{{nihongo|'''Ayaka Sasaki'''|佐々木 彩夏|Sasaki Ayaka|born June 11, 1996}} is a [[Japanese idol]]. She is known as a member of the female musical group [[Momoiro Clover Z]].

Her Momoiro Clover Z signature color is Pink.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.starchild.co.jp/artist/momoclo/profile/|title=starchildももいろクローバーZ|publisher=Starchild|accessdate=2012-12-07|language=Japanese}}</ref> She is the youngest member of the group. Her self-introduction is: <!--{{nihongo|-->"I am a playful and little bit sexy idol of Momoclo Ayaka Sasaki a.k.a. Ārin!"<!--|ちょっぴりセクシーでおちゃめなももクロのアイドル、あーりんこと佐々木彩夏です！}}-->.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sankei.jp.msn.com/entertainments/news/120304/ent12030407010001-n1.htm |script-title=ja:ももクロ「お前ら、ちゃんと店に行ってＣＤ買えよな！」 |publisher=MSN News |date=2012-03-04 |accessdate=2012-12-07 |language=Japanese |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20121206063749/http://sankei.jp.msn.com/entertainments/news/120304/ent12030407010001-n1.htm |archivedate=2012-12-06 }}</ref>

On July 24, 2021, it was reported Sasaki was hospitalized on July 23. She was diagnosed with right peripheral facial nerve paralysis. A concert that was scheduled for August 1, 2021 has been postponed.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2021-07-26/momoiro-clover-z-ayaka-sasaki-hospitalized-due-to-paralyzed-facial-nerves/.175543|title = Momoiro Clover Z's Ayaka Sasaki Hospitalized Due to Paralyzed Facial Nerves| date=12 June 2023 }}</ref>

== Career ==
Ayaka Sasaki was born on June 11, 1996, in [[Kanagawa]], Japan.

Ayaka entered Momoiro Clover together with [[Yukina Kashiwa]] and [[Akari Hayami]] on November 23, 2008.<ref>{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20081224060957/http://official.stardust.co.jp/section3/momokuro/index.html|title=新曲・新メンバー！(2008.11.25)|date=2008-11-25|publisher=ももいろクローバー -スターダストプロモーション [[3B Junior|３Bジュニア]]|url=http://official.stardust.co.jp/section3/momokuro/index.html|archivedate=2008-12-24|accessdate=2013-04-01}}</ref>

On October 12, 2012, she made a solo appearance in a special issue of the Japanese culture magazine ''QuickJapan''. The 21-page material featuring her was titled "Summer Memories of a 16-year-old". It reported about Momoclo's summer of 2012 activities, included many photographs and a long interview with Ayaka.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://natalie.mu/music/news/78193|title=最新号「QuickJapan」にももクロあーりん21ページ特集|publisher=[[Natalie (website)|Natalie]]|date=2012-10-23|accessdate=2012-12-07|language=Japanese}}</ref>

Since 2019, she has also been part of the unit idol group ''{{ill|LumiUnion|ja|LumiUnion}}'' (formerly named {{Nihongo||浪江女子発組合|Namie Joshihatsu Kumiai}} until June 28, 2025<ref>{{Cite web |title=佐々木彩夏が総合プロデューサーを務める浪江女子発組合、新たなグループ名はLumiUnion |url=https://natalie.mu/music/news/630048 |website=音楽ナタリー |access-date=2025-06-28 |language=ja}}</ref>), serving as a producer and member.<ref>{{Cite web |title=雨でも大盛り上がり「復興なみえ町十日市祭」が開催されました - 浪江町ホームページ |url=https://www.town.namie.fukushima.jp/soshiki/2/23334.html |website=www.town.namie.fukushima.jp |access-date=2024-08-14}}</ref> In the same year, she started her fashion brand ''Chubby Bunny''.<ref>{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221006070557/https://www.momoclo.net/pub/pc/information/?id=4676|title=あーりんプロデュース新ブランド『Chubby Bunny(チュビー・バニー)』緊急速報！|date=2018-11-15|publisher=momoclo STAFF|url=https://www.momoclo.net/pub/pc/information/?id=4676|archivedate=2022-10-06|accessdate=2024-12-14}}</ref>

'''Gastón Maximiliano Álvarez Suárez''' (born 5 April 1993) is a professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for the [[UAE Pro League]] club [[Al Wahda FC|Al Wahda]]. Born in Argentina, he represents the [[United Arab Emirates national football team|United Arab Emirates national team]].<ref name="Soccerway profile">{{cite news|title=Gastón Álvarez Suárez profile|url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/gaston-suarez/207949/|access-date=16 April 2017|work=Soccerway|date=16 April 2017}}</ref>

==Career==
===Club===
Álvarez Suárez began his career with [[Argentine Primera División]] side [[Club Atlético Belgrano|Belgrano]] in 2011, making his debut on 26 September in the league against [[Estudiantes de La Plata|Estudiantes]].<ref name="Soccerway profile"/> Between 2014 and 2015, Álvarez Suárez was loaned out twice. Firstly to [[Primera B de Chile]] side [[San Marcos de Arica]], before joining [[Primera B Nacional]]'s [[Sportivo Belgrano]].<ref name="Soccerway profile"/>

'''Federico Vicente Lanzillotta''' (born 1 December 1992) is an Argentine professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for Chilean club [[Deportes La Serena]].<ref name="Soccerway profile">{{cite news|title=Federico Lanzillota profile|url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/federico-lanzillota/258180/|accessdate=19 October 2017|work=Soccerway|date=19 October 2017}}</ref>

==Career==
Lanzillotta started his career in 2013 with [[Club Atlético Nueva Chicago|Nueva Chicago]] of [[Primera B Nacional]], making his debut on 2 June 2013 versus [[Club Atlético Douglas Haig|Douglas Haig]].<ref name="Soccerway profile"/> He made two more appearances in [[2012–13 Primera B Nacional|2012–13]], prior to seven in the [[2015 Argentine Primera División]] which turned out to be his last games for the club.<ref name="Soccerway profile"/> In January 2016, Lanzillotta completed a move to [[Argentinos Juniors]].<ref name="Soccerway profile"/><ref name="Argentinos profile">{{cite news|title=Federico Lanzillotta profile|url=http://www.argentinosjuniors.com.ar/futbol/profesional/plantel/perfil/2369_federicolanzillotta|accessdate=19 October 2017|work=Argentinos Juniors|date=19 October 2017|archive-date=20 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171020033451/http://www.argentinosjuniors.com.ar/futbol/profesional/plantel/perfil/2369_federicolanzillotta|url-status=dead}}</ref> His first match for Argentinos came in the Primera División in a 0–3 home defeat to [[Atlético Tucumán]] in March.<ref name="Soccerway profile"/> The club won promotion in [[2016–17 Primera B Nacional|2016–17]], but prior to the start of the [[2017–18 Argentinos Juniors season|2017–18]] season he suffered a [[cruciate ligament]] injury which took him out of action for the next six months.<ref name="Injury 1">{{cite news|title=Lanzillota sufrió la rotura de ligamentos cruzados|url=http://www.tycsports.com/futbol/lanzillota-sufrio-la-rotura-de-ligamentos-cruzados|accessdate=19 October 2017|work=TyC Sports|date=20 July 2017}}</ref><ref name="Injury 2">{{cite news|title=Argentinos: Lanzillotta se rompió los ligamentos cruzados|url=http://www.espn.com.ar/futbol/argentina/nota/_/id/3403767/argentinos-lanzillotta-se-rompio-los-ligamentos-cruzados|accessdate=19 October 2017|work=ESPN|date=20 July 2017}}</ref>

On 29 July 2019, Lanzillotta was loaned for five months to [[Chilean Primera División]] side [[Club Deportivo Palestino|Palestino]].<ref name="AJ1">{{cite news|title=El jugador Federico Lanzillotta, es cedido a préstamo sin cargo y sin opción de compra, a Palestino de Chile hasta el 31-12-2019, en busca de continuidad|url=https://twitter.com/AAAJoficial/status/1155872113632456704|accessdate=29 July 2019|work=Argentinos Juniors|date=29 July 2019}}</ref> Just three appearances followed due to the goalkeeper experiencing a knee injury, which required surgery.<ref name="AS1">{{cite news|title=El sorpresivo regreso de arquero argentino en Palestino|url=https://chile.as.com/chile/2020/07/20/futbol/1595269685_432191.html|accessdate=19 February 2021|work=AS|date=20 July 2020}}</ref> Lanzillotta returned to Argentinos in early December, though would rejoin Palestino on fresh loan terms in January 2020; he joined for twelve months, whilst also renewing his contract until 30 June 2023 with his parent club.<ref name="AS1"/><ref name="TYC1">{{cite news|title=Argentinos Juniors compró la mitad del pase de Elías Gómez|url=https://www.tycsports.com/superliga/argentinos-juniors-compro-la-mitad-del-pase-de-elias-gomez-20200103.html|accessdate=19 February 2021|work=TyC Sports|date=3 January 2020}}</ref><ref name="AS2">{{cite news|title=El fichaje estrella que sólo jugó 3 partidos en el torneo|url=https://chile.as.com/chile/2019/12/06/futbol/1575644269_033873.html|accessdate=19 February 2021|work=AS|date=7 December 2019}}</ref> He wouldn't play for the Chileans until 14 November 2020, due to the aforementioned surgery and the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], with fourteen appearances eventually arriving in [[2020 Chilean Primera División|2020]].<ref name="Soccerway profile"/> He returned to Argentinos in February 2021.<ref name="AJ2">{{cite news|title=Luego de su paso a préstamo por Palestino de Chile, Federico Lanzillota regresa a nuestra Institución|url=https://twitter.com/AAAJoficial/status/1362732587366645761|accessdate=19 February 2021|work=Argentinos Juniors|date=19 February 2021}}</ref>

In January 2026, Lanzillotta returned to Chile and joined [[Deportes La Serena]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Oficial: Federico Lanzillotta es nuevo arquero de CD La Serena |url=https://www.diarioeldia.cl/noticias/2026/01/15/132164-oficial-federico-lanzillotta-es-nuevo-arquero-de-cd-la-serena |access-date=18 January 2026 |work=[[El Día (Chile)|Diario El Día]] |date=15 January 2026 |language=es}}</ref>

'''Travis Etienne Jr.''' ({{IPAc-en|US|ˈ|eɪ|tʃ|æ|n}} {{respell|AY|chan}}<ref name=":1">{{cite news |last1=Terrell |first1=Katherine |title=Saints' Travis Etienne corrects how to say his name |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/48196375/saints-travis-etienne-updates-how-say-name |access-date=17 March 2026 |work=[[ESPN.com]] |date=13 March 2026 |language=en}}</ref>; born January 26, 1999) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[running back]] for the [[New Orleans Saints]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson Tigers]] and was selected by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] in the first round 25th pick of the [[2021 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Etienne was raised in [[Jennings, Louisiana]], and is of [[Louisiana Creole people|Louisiana Creole]] ancestry. His father works for a well service company in the oil industry, while his mother, Donnetta, is a nurse.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 7, 2019 |editor-last=Cleary, Tom |title=Travis Etienne's Family: 5 Fast Facts You Need to Know |url=https://heavy.com/sports/2019/01/travis-etienne-parents-father-brother-mother-family/ |access-date=July 20, 2021 |publisher=[[Heavy (website)|Heavy.com]]}}</ref>

Etienne attended [[Jennings High School (Louisiana)|Jennings High School]] in [[Jennings, Louisiana]]. As a senior, he rushed for 2,459 yards with 39 touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Oliver |first=Gavin |date=August 11, 2017 |title=Etienne's explosiveness jumps out at Elliott |url=https://theclemsoninsider.com/2017/08/11/etiennes-explosiveness-jumps-out-at-elliott/ |access-date=September 6, 2019 |website=The Clemson Insider}}</ref> For his career, he had 8,864 total yards with 115 total touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dabe |first=Christopher |date=December 31, 2017 |title=Clemson's Louisiana-born Travis Etienne comes home to face Alabama in Sugar Bowl semifinal |url=https://www.nola.com/sugarbowl/index.ssf/2017/12/travis_etienne_sugar_bowl_2018.html |access-date=September 6, 2019 |website=[[The Times-Picayune/The New Orleans Advocate]]}}</ref> He was rated as a four-star recruit and the 15th highest-rated running back recruit in the country by the [[247Sports.com]] Composite, which aggregates the ratings of the major recruiting services.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Travis Etienne, Jennings, Running Back |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Travis-Etienne-88104/high-school-165432/ |access-date=January 7, 2019 |website=[[247Sports.com]]}}</ref> Etienne committed to [[Clemson University]] to play [[college football]] on January 21, 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hunte |first=Sydney |date=September 18, 2017 |title=Clemson football: Travis Etienne "glad" he choose Clemson over LSU |url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/college/clemson-football-travis-etienne-glad-choose-clemson-over-lsu/yaKSWoQ0SX85U85sBCaTYJ/ |access-date=September 6, 2019 |website=[[Dayton Daily News]] |publisher=[[Cox Enterprises]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bewers |first=James |date=January 26, 2017 |title=Video: LSU target, Jennings RB Travis Etienne commits to Clemson, 'the real Death Valley |url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/article_10114972-e406-11e6-9baf-c3142e4d3acd.html |access-date=September 6, 2019 |website=[[The Advocate (Louisiana)|The Advocate]]}}</ref>

==College career==
===2017 season===
As a freshman at Clemson in 2017, he was part of a backfield that contained Tavien Feaster, Adam Choice, C.{{nbsp}}J. Fuller, and dual-threat quarterback Kelly Bryant.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 Clemson Tigers Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/clemson/2017.html |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He led the team in rushing with 766 yards on 107 carries with 13 touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Raynor |first=Grace |date=July 11, 2018 |title=Clemson football Top 10: What's next for explosive RB Travis Etienne? |url=https://www.postandcourier.com/sports/clemson-football-top-what-s-next-for-explosive-rb-travis/article_608911b6-8516-11e8-bd7e-775732c0aa2d.html |access-date=September 6, 2019 |website=[[The Post and Courier]] |publisher=[[Evening Post Industries]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Connolly |first=Matt |date=June 25, 2018 |title=What Travis Etienne did to earn Clemson's starting running back job |url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/acc/clemson-university/article213786524.html |access-date=September 6, 2019 |website=[[The State (newspaper)|The State]] |publisher=[[McClatchy]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Louis-Jacques |first=Marcel |date=March 14, 2018 |title=Clemson RB Travis Etienne more comfortable in first spring, but still has a lot to learn |url=https://www.independentmail.com/story/sports/college/clemson/football/2018/03/14/clemson-rb-travis-etienne-more-comfortable-first-spring-but-still-has-lot-learn/426754002/ |access-date=September 6, 2019 |website=[[The Anderson Independent-Mail]] |publisher=[[Gannett]]}}</ref>

===2018 season===
As a sophomore in 2018, he was a key member of a Clemson team that [[2019 College Football Playoff National Championship|won the national championship]]. Etienne rushed for 1,659 yards on the year and had an [[NCAA Division I Football Bowl Subdivision|FBS]]-leading 24 rushing touchdowns. He had an additional two receiving touchdowns, bringing his total touchdowns from scrimmage to 26, which also led FBS.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2018 College Football Leaders|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/years/2018-leaders.html|website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com|access-date=November 28, 2025|language=en}}</ref> He had eight games going over 100 rushing yards<ref>{{Cite web |title=Travis Etienne 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/travis-etienne-1/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=January 8, 2019 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2018 Leaders |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/years/2018-leaders.html |access-date=January 8, 2019 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> After winning the [[2018 ACC Championship Game]] against Pitt, Etienne was named the MVP of the game.  Etienne was named ACC Player of the Year and ACC Offensive Player of the Year following the regular season.<ref name="POY">{{Cite web |date=November 28, 2018 |title=Clemson's Etienne Voted ACC Player of the Year |url=http://theacc.com/news/2018/11/28/football-clemsons-etienne-voted-acc-player-of-the-year.aspx |access-date=November 28, 2018 |website=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]]}}</ref> He was named a [[2018 College Football All-America Team|first-team All-American]] by ''[[Sporting News]]'' and [[ESPN]], and was a consensus second-team All-American.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Russo |first=Ralph D. |date=December 10, 2018 |title=AP All-America team: Tide leads with 4 of 10 CFP players |url=https://apnews.com/fae9919b680940b9894dd530493690bb |access-date=December 10, 2018 |website=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=2019 Football All-Americans|url=https://clemsontigers.com/2019-football-all-americans/|website=Clemson Tigers Official Athletics Site|date=December 19, 2019|access-date=November 28, 2025|language=en-US}}</ref>

===2019 season===
Etienne started his junior year at Clemson with a career-high 205 yards and three touchdowns in the first game of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Keepfer |first=Scott |date=August 30, 2019 |title=Travis Etienne's performance against Georgia Tech boosted his Heisman Trophy prospects |url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/2019/08/29/clemson-football-travis-etienne-gets-heisman-campaign-off-fast-start/2093185001/ |access-date=September 7, 2019 |website=[[The Greenville News]] |publisher=[[Gannett]] |language=en}}</ref> He bested this in a November 2 game against [[2019 Wofford Terriers football team|Wofford]], when he ran for 212 yards and two touchdowns on just 9 attempts (23.6 yards per attempt).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wofford at Clemson Box Score, November 2, 2019 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2019-11-02-clemson.html |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He became the first Clemson running back to have three career 200-yard games.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 2, 2019 |title=No. 4 Clemson routs Wofford 59–14 for 24th straight victory |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap?gameId=401112496 |access-date=October 5, 2022 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> At the conclusion of the regular season, Etienne was named [[Atlantic Coast Conference football individual awards#Player of the Year|ACC Player of the Year]], ACC Offensive Player of the Year, and [[2019 All-ACC football team|first-team All-ACC]]; all for the second consecutive year. He is the first Clemson player to win consecutive ACC Player of the Year awards since [[Steve Fuller (American football)|Steve Fuller]] in 1977–78.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gillespie |first=Mike |date=December 4, 2019 |title=Travis Etienne named ACC Player of the Year again |url=https://www.abccolumbia.com/2019/12/04/travis-etienne-named-acc-player-of-the-year-again/ |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=ABC Columbia}}</ref> Etienne ended his junior season with 1,614 rushing yards and an ACC-leading 19 rushing touchdowns. His 7.8 yards-per-carry were second most in FBS.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019 College Football Summary |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/years/2019.html |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the Fiesta Bowl, he caught the game winning touchdown with 1:49 left in the game, running it in from 34 yards. Following the season, he was named a consensus second-team All-American.<ref name=":0" />

Despite projections that Etienne would enter the [[2020 NFL draft]], he announced on January 17, 2020, that he would return to Clemson for his senior year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rittenberg |first=Adam |author-link=Adam Rittenberg |date=January 17, 2020 |title=Clemson RB Travis Etienne surprises by returning for senior season |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/28503387/clemson-rb-travis-etienne-surprises-returning-senior-season |access-date=October 5, 2022 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

===2020 season===
On October 31, 2020, in a 34–28 win over [[Boston College Eagles football|Boston College]], Etienne finished with two touchdowns and a career-high 264 all-purpose yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Boston College at Clemson Box Score, October 31, 2020 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2020-10-31-clemson.html |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> With the performance, he scored a touchdown in 42 games, breaking [[Donnel Pumphrey]]'s record for most in FBS history. He finished his career with touchdowns scored in 46 games.  With his 4,952 career rushing yards Etienne also broke the ACC career rushing record previously held by [[Ted Brown (American football)|Ted Brown]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Adelson |first=Andrea |date=October 31, 2020 |title=Clemson Tigers' Travis Etienne sets records for career rushing yards, games with touchdown |work=[[ESPN]] |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/30230351/clemson-tigers-travis-etienne-sets-records-career-rushing-yards-games-touchdown |access-date=November 7, 2020}}</ref> He also set ACC career records for rushing touchdowns (70), total touchdowns (78), and total points scored (468).  He scored at least one touchdown in 46 of 55 career games, setting the FBS and NCAA records.<ref name="GarrySmits">{{Cite web |last=Smits |first=Garry |date=October 23, 2022 |title=Hard to be happy: Travis Etienne said reaching NFL milestones meaningless without a win |url=https://www.jacksonville.com/story/sports/nfl/2022/10/23/jaguars-travis-etienne-said-reaching-goals-meaningless-without-win/10489693002/ |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=The Florida Times-Union |language=en-US}}</ref> He was named as a Consensus All-American.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Consensus All-America Teams (2020-2022) |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/awards/all-america-2020-2029.html#2020 |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
====2021 season====
Etienne officially declared for the [[2021 NFL draft]] in January 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lentz |first=Zack |date=January 7, 2021 |title=Travis Etienne Declares For the NFL Draft |url=https://www.si.com/college/clemson/football/travis-etienne-declares-for-the-nfl-draft |access-date=April 3, 2021 |website=si.com}}</ref> He was selected by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] with the 25th overall selection, which they previously obtained from a trade that sent [[Jalen Ramsey]] to the [[Los Angeles Rams]]. This reunited Etienne with his college quarterback [[Trevor Lawrence]], who was taken by the Jaguars first overall in the same draft.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Oehser |first=John |date=April 29, 2021 |title=No. 25 overall: Etienne is the selection |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/no-25-overall-etienne-is-the-selection |access-date=May 7, 2021 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref> On May 15, Jaguars coach [[Urban Meyer]] announced that Etienne would spend the Jaguars minicamp as a [[wide receiver]], rather than a [[running back]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiRocco |first=Michael |date=May 15, 2021 |title=Meyer, Jags envision rookie Etienne as a 'hybrid' |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/31450913/saying-feels-great-rookie-rb-travis-etienne-aims-maximize-my-opportunity-wr-jacksonville-jaguars |access-date=October 5, 2022 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> On July 19, 2021, Etienne signed his four-year rookie contract with the Jaguars, worth $12.9 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Links |first=Zachary |date=July 19, 2021 |title=Jaguars Sign Travis Etienne |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2021/07/jaguars-sign-travis-etienne |access-date=October 5, 2022 |website=Pro Football Rumors |language=en-US}}</ref>

During the Jaguars second preseason game against the [[New Orleans Saints]], Etienne suffered a Lisfranc injury and was subsequently ruled out indefinitely.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=August 24, 2021 |title=Jaguars RB Travis Etienne suffered Lisfranc injury vs. Saints, will undergo further tests |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/jaguars-rb-travis-etienne-suffered-lisfranc-injury-saints-undergo-further-tests |access-date=August 24, 2021 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=DiRocco |first=Michael |date=August 24, 2021 |title=Source: Jags' Etienne grounded with foot injury |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/32075203/jacksonville-jaguars-travis-etienne-indefinitely-midfoot-sprain-source-says |access-date=August 24, 2021 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> It was later revealed that Etienne had suffered a significant tear in the lisfranc zone of his foot, which required surgery, and prematurely ended his 2021 season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shook |first=Nick |date=August 24, 2021 |title=Travis Etienne to have foot surgery, out for the season |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/jaguars-rookie-rb-travis-etienne-to-undergo-foot-surgery-likely-to-miss-2021-sea |access-date=August 24, 2021 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He was placed on season-ending injured reserve later in the day.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiRocco |first=Michael |date=August 24, 2021 |title=Jaguars RB Etienne placed on season-ending IR |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/32077723/jacksonville-jaguars-rb-travis-etienne-likely-season-lisfranc-injury-source-says |access-date=August 25, 2021 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

====2022 season====
[[file:Jaguars at Commanders Photo 184 (52391274423).jpg|thumb|right|225px|Etienne playing for the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] in 2022]]
Etienne made his professional debut in the Jaguars' 2022 season opener against the [[Washington Commanders]] and had four carries for 47 rushing yards.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bergman |first=Jeremy |date=September 18, 2022 |title=James Robinson, Travis Etienne to split carries for Jaguars vs. Colts |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/james-robinson-travis-etienne-to-split-carries-for-jaguars-vs-colts |access-date=October 5, 2022 |website=NFL.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

Etienne recorded his first career touchdown in Week 7 against the [[New York Giants]], adding 14 carries for 114 yards and 1 lost fumble in the 23–17 loss. This marked the first time in his NFL career that he recorded a touchdown and over 100 yards in an NFL game.<ref name="GarrySmits" /> After a trade with the New York Jets involving Jaguars running back James Robinson, Etienne was named the starting running back in Jacksonville.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Michael David |date=October 24, 2022 |title=Jaguars trade James Robinson to Jets |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2022/10/24/jaguars-trade-james-robinson-to-jets/ |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=ProFootballTalk |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 24, 2022 |title=Jaguars' Travis Etienne: No. 1 RB following Robinson trade |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/jaguars-travis-etienne-no-1-rb-following-robinson-trade/ |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref> In the following game, he recorded 24 carries for 156 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown in the 21–17 loss to the [[Denver Broncos]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Denver Broncos at Jacksonville Jaguars – October 30th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202210300jax.htm |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He had 28 carries for 109 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns in the next game against the [[Las Vegas Raiders]], a 27–20 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Las Vegas Raiders at Jacksonville Jaguars – November 6th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202211060jax.htm |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He had two more games over the 100-yard mark on the season, in Week 15 against the [[Dallas Cowboys]] and Week 17 against the [[Houston Texans]].<ref name="22gl" />

Etienne finished the 2022 season with 220 carries for 1,125 rushing yards and five rushing touchdowns to go along with 35 receptions for 316 receiving yards.<ref name="22gl">{{Cite web |title=Travis Etienne 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/E/EtieTr00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the [[2022–23 NFL playoffs#AFC: Jacksonville Jaguars 31, Los Angeles Chargers 30|Wild Card Round]] against the [[Los Angeles Chargers]], he had 20 carries for 109 rushing yards in the 31–30 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card – Los Angeles Chargers at Jacksonville Jaguars – January 14th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202301140jax.htm |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On the Jaguars' final drive, Etienne had a 25-yard run on fourth down to set up the game-winning field goal attempt.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sutelan |first=Edward |date=January 15, 2023 |title=Doug Pederson explains crucial fourth-down run by Travis Etienne late in Jaguars vs. Chargers |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nfl/news/jaguars-doug-pederson-travis-etienne-fourth-down/c2jkwzxbogsgej8ffxfctlsc |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=Sporting News |language=en-us}}</ref>

====2023 season====
During Week 5 against the Buffalo Bills at [[Tottenham Hotspur Stadium]], Etienne finished with 136 rushing yards and two touchdowns as the Jaguars won 25–20.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacksonville Jaguars at Buffalo Bills - October 8th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202310080buf.htm |access-date=2024-06-24 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He finished the season with 267 carries for 1,008 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Travis Etienne 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/E/EtieTr00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2024-06-24 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2024 season====
On April 29, 2024, the Jaguars picked up the fifth-year option on Etienne's contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Oehser |first=John |date=April 29, 2024 |title=Official: Jaguars Exercise Fifth-Year Option on Trevor Lawrence and Travis Etienne |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/official-jaguars-exercise-fifth-year-options-on-lawrence-etienne |access-date=2025-02-03 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref> He finished the 2024 season with 150 carries for 558 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns to go with 39 receptions for 254 receiving yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Travis Etienne 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/E/EtieTr00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=2025-02-03 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

==== 2025 season ====
In the season opener, Etienne had 16 carries for 143 yards in a 26–10 win over the Carolina Panthers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carolina Panthers at Jacksonville Jaguars - September 7th, 2025 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202509070jax.htm |access-date=2026-04-10 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He had 19 carries for 124 yards and a touchdown in a 26–21 win over the 49ers in Week 6.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacksonville Jaguars at San Francisco 49ers - September 28th, 2025 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202509280sfo.htm |access-date=2026-04-10 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In Week 15, against the Jets, he had three receiving touchdowns in the 48–20 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New York Jets at Jacksonville Jaguars - December 14th, 2025 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202512140jax.htm |access-date=2026-04-10 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Etienne bounced back in the 2025 season, finishing the year with 1,107 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns on 260 carries. He also set a career high in receiving touchdowns with six.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Travis Etienne 2025 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/E/EtieTr00/gamelog/2025/ |access-date=2026-04-10 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He had a receiving touchdown to go with 116 scrimmage yards in the 27–24 loss to the Bills in the Wild Card Round.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card - Buffalo Bills at Jacksonville Jaguars - January 11th, 2026 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202601110jax.htm |access-date=2026-04-10 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===New Orleans Saints===
On March 13, 2026, Etienne signed a four-year, $52 million contract with the [[New Orleans Saints]].<ref>{{cite web |date=11 March 2026 |title=Saints agree to terms with running back Travis Etienne Jr. |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/travis-etienne-jr-running-back-nfl-free-agency-2026-saints-roster-moves |access-date=April 7, 2026 |website=NewOrleansSaints.com}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Through the 2025 season, Etienne's surname was believed to be pronounced {{IPAc-en|i|.|t|i|.|'|E|n}} ({{respell|ee|tee|EN}}). Upon signing with the Saints and returning to his home state of Louisiana, he informed the media during his introductory press conference that it is actually pronounced {{IPAc-en|'|ei|.|tS|ae|n}} ({{respell|AY|chan}}).<ref name=":1" />

Travis has a younger brother [[Trevor Etienne|Trevor]] who was drafted by the [[Carolina Panthers]] with the 114th pick in the [[2025 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=With the No. 114 overall pick, the Panthers pick running back Trevor Etienne |url=https://www.panthers.com/news/with-the-no-114-overall-pick-the-panthers-pick-running-back-trevor-etienne|author1=Gantt, Darin|author2=Hill, Kassidy|date=April 26, 2025|website=Panthers.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Bruno Méndez Cittadini''' (born 10 September 1999) is a Uruguayan professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[centre-back]] or [[right-back]] for [[Liga MX]] club [[Toluca FC|Toluca]].<ref>[https://www.elobservador.com.uy/nota/bruno-mendez-un-bohemio-fanatico-de-aguada-y-la-vela-2018102220221 Bruno Méndez, un bohemio fanático de Aguada y La Vela y que se ganó la confianza de Tabárez] elobservador.com.uy</ref><ref name="soccerway">{{Soccerway|bruno-mendez/486251}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Montevideo Wanderers===
Méndez developed through the academy of [[Montevideo Wanderers F.C.|Montevideo Wanderers]] and made his professional debut on 19 November 2017 against [[Rampla Juniors]] in a 1–0 home win.<ref name="First match">{{cite web|url=https://us.soccerway.com/matches/2017/11/19/uruguay/primera-division/montevideo-wanderers-futbol-club/rampla-juniors-futbol-club/2560007/|title=Wanderers vs. Rampla Juniors - 19 November 2017|website=Soccerway|accessdate=11 November 2018}}</ref> He scored his debut professional goal on 21 October 2018 against [[Club Atlético River Plate (Montevideo)|River Plate Montevideo]] in a 5–0 away win.<ref name="First goal">{{cite web|url=https://us.soccerway.com/matches/2018/10/21/uruguay/primera-division/ca-river-plate/montevideo-wanderers-futbol-club/2724877/|title=River Plate vs. Wanderers - 21 October 2018|website=Soccerway|accessdate=11 November 2018}}</ref>

===Corinthians===
In February 2019, he signed a four-year contract with Brazilian [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|Série A]] club [[Sport Club Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.corinthians.com.br/zagueiro-bruno-mendez-assina-com-o-timao|title=Zagueiro Bruno Méndez assina com o Timão|publisher=Sport Club Corinthians Paulista|date=28 February 2019|accessdate=15 March 2019}}</ref>

====Internacional (loan)====
On 1 July 2021, Corinthians sent Méndez on a one-year loan to fellow Série A club [[SC Internacional|Internacional]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 July 2021 |title=Inter oficializa a contratação de Bruno Méndez por empréstimo do Corinthians |trans-title=Inter announces signing of Bruno Méndez on loan from Corinthians |url=https://ge.globo.com/rs/futebol/times/internacional/noticia/inter-oficializa-a-contratacao-de-bruno-mendez-por-emprestimo-do-corinthians.ghtml |access-date=27 December 2023 |website=Globo Esporte |language=pt-br}}</ref>

===Granada===
On 26 December 2023, [[La Liga]] side [[Granada CF|Granada]] announced that Méndez would join the club on 1 January 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 December 2023 |title=Bruno Méndez, nuevo jugador del Granada CF |trans-title=Bruno Méndez, new Granada CF player |url=https://www.granadacf.es/noticias/comunicado-oficial-or-bruno-mendez-nuevo-jugador-del-granada-cf |access-date=27 December 2023 |publisher=Granada CF |language=es}}</ref>

===Toluca===
On 9 July 2024, Méndez joined [[Liga MX]] club [[Toluca FC|Toluca]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Toluca anunció al nuevo líder de su defensa: Él es Bruno Méndez|url=https://esto.com.mx/830144-toluca-anuncio-a-bruno-mendez-como-refuerzo-para-el-apertura-2024/|language=es|date=9 July 2024|access-date=9 July 2024}}</ref>

==International career==
===Youth===
Méndez is a former Uruguay youth international and has represented his nation at different age levels. He was also the captain of Uruguay team at the [[2019 South American U-20 Championship]], [[2019 FIFA U-20 World Cup]] and the [[Football at the 2019 Pan American Games – Men's tournament|2019 Pan American Games]].

===Senior===
Following the injuries of [[Diego Godín]] and [[Marcelo Saracchi]], Méndez received his first call-up to the [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay senior team]] for friendlies against [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] and [[France national football team|France]] in November 2018.<ref name="Maiden call up">{{cite web|url=http://www.auf.org.uy/Portal/NEWS/14912/0/Comunicado_de_Sanidad_y_convocados/|website=auf.org.uy|title=Comunicado de Sanidad y convocados|accessdate=2018-11-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181111133536/http://www.auf.org.uy/Portal/NEWS/14912/0/Comunicado_de_Sanidad_y_convocados/|archive-date=2018-11-11|url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his debut in a friendly that was played in London against Brazil on 16 November 2018 and played the full game.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=[[ESPN]]|url=http://www.espn.co.uk/soccer/match?gameId=527623|title=Brazil v Uruguay game report|date=16 November 2018}}</ref>

On 21 October 2022, Méndez was named in Uruguay's 55-man preliminary squad for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Selección: Diego Alonso entregó la lista de 55 reservados para el Mundial de Catar|url=https://www.futbol.com.uy/Deportes/Seleccion-Diego-Alonso-entrego-la-lista-de-55-reservados-para-el-Mundial-de-Catar-uc835965|date=21 October 2022|access-date=21 October 2022|language=es}}</ref>

'''Éderson José dos Santos Lourenço da Silva''' (born 7 July 1999), simply known as '''Éderson''' ({{IPA|pt-BR|ˈɛdeʁsõ(w̃)|lang}}), is a Brazilian professional [[footballer]] who plays as a [[central midfielder]] for {{Italian football updater|Atalanta}} club [[Atalanta BC|Atalanta]] and the [[Brazil national football team|Brazil national team]].

Éderson began his career in Brazilian football, playing for [[Desportivo Brasil]], [[Cruzeiro EC|Cruzeiro]], [[SC Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]] and [[Fortaleza EC|Fortaleza]]. He joined Italian club [[US Salernitana 1919|Salernitana]] in January 2022. Later that year, he signed for Atalanta. He has made more than 150 appearances for Atalanta, and won the [[UEFA Europa League]] in [[2023–24 UEFA Europa League|2023–24]].

Éderson played youth international football for Brazil at [[Brazil national under-20 football team|under-20 level]], before making his senior international debut in June 2024. He represented Brazil at the [[2024 Copa América]] and [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].

==Club career==
===Early career===
Born in [[Campo Grande]], [[Mato Grosso do Sul]], Éderson played in the youth academy, and started his professional career, at [[Desportivo Brasil]], a club from [[São Paulo (state)|São Paulo]]. He was loaned to Chinese club [[Shandong Taishan F.C.|Shandong Luneng]] in 2017.<ref name="fullname">{{cite news |url=https://breakingthelines.com/player-analysis/ederson-the-relentless-brazilian-workhorse-whos-reinvigorating-atalantas-midfield/ |title=Éderson: The Relentless Brazilian Workhorse Who’s Reinvigorating Atalanta’s Midfield |website=breakingthelines.com |date=28 January 2025 |access-date=27 May 2026}}</ref>

===Cruzeiro===
On 15 July 2018, Éderson was loaned to [[Cruzeiro Esporte Clube|Cruzeiro]], a team playing in the [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A]], that has the [[Option (finance)|option to sign him]] after the loan ending in mid-2019.<ref name="Sob olhares do profissional, Cruzeiro contrata volante em último ano do sub-20">{{cite web |last1=Duarte |first1=Gabriel |title=Sob olhares do profissional, Cruzeiro contrata volante em último ano do sub-20 |url=https://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/times/cruzeiro/noticia/sob-olhares-do-profissional-cruzeiro-contrata-volante-em-ultimo-ano-do-sub-20.ghtml |website=[[GloboEsporte.com]] |date=13 August 2018 |accessdate=22 November 2018 |archive-date=23 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181123023059/https://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/times/cruzeiro/noticia/sob-olhares-do-profissional-cruzeiro-contrata-volante-em-ultimo-ano-do-sub-20.ghtml |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Cruzeiro acerta contratação de meio-campista; jogador ‘cutuca’ rival nas redes sociais">{{cite web |last1=Bahúte |first1=Eder |title=Cruzeiro acerta contratação de meio-campista; jogador 'cutuca' rival nas redes sociais |url=https://www.torcedores.com/noticias/2018/08/cruzeiro-acerta-contratacao-de-meio-campista-jogador-cutuca-rival-nas-redes-sociais |website=Torcedores.com |accessdate=22 November 2018 |archive-date=1 May 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190501204328/https://www.torcedores.com/noticias/2018/08/cruzeiro-acerta-contratacao-de-meio-campista-jogador-cutuca-rival-nas-redes-sociais |url-status=live }}</ref> At first, the player was expected to be part of Cruzeiro's under-20 team, but after training with the first team for some time, Éderson impressed coach [[Mano Menezes]] who decided to give him a chance in the first team.<ref name="Contratado para a base, Ederson treina com grupo principal do Cruzeiro e é 'batizado' por experientes">{{cite web |last1=Arruda |first1=Rafael |title=Contratado para a base, Ederson treina com grupo principal do Cruzeiro e é 'batizado' por experientes |url=https://www.mg.superesportes.com.br/app/noticias/futebol/cruzeiro/2018/08/14/noticia_cruzeiro,496167/jovem-treina-com-grupo-do-cruzeiro-e-e-batizado-por-experientes.shtml |website=Super Esportes |date=14 August 2018 |accessdate=22 November 2018 |archive-date=23 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181123065516/https://www.mg.superesportes.com.br/app/noticias/futebol/cruzeiro/2018/08/14/noticia_cruzeiro,496167/jovem-treina-com-grupo-do-cruzeiro-e-e-batizado-por-experientes.shtml |url-status=live }}</ref>

As Cruzeiro was playing three competitions at once, Menezes was forced to use most of the players in the squad in order of rest some important players for some priority competitions. Due to this fact, many young and reserve players had his chance in the first team. On 5 September 2018, Éderson debuted in a 1–1 draw against [[Botafogo de Futebol e Regatas|Botafogo]]. He came in the match's 75th minute, replacing [[Thiago Neves]].<ref name="Após estreia, meia Éderson espera novas oportunidades no Cruzeiro">{{cite web |title=Após estreia, meia Éderson espera novas oportunidades no Cruzeiro |url=https://esportes.estadao.com.br/noticias/futebol,apos-estreia-meia-ederson-espera-novas-oportunidades-no-cruzeiro,70002491336 |website=[[O Estado de S. Paulo]] |accessdate=22 November 2018 |archive-date=23 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181123023026/https://esportes.estadao.com.br/noticias/futebol,apos-estreia-meia-ederson-espera-novas-oportunidades-no-cruzeiro,70002491336 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Botafogo vs. Cruzeiro 1 - 1">{{cite web |title=Botafogo vs. Cruzeiro 1 – 1 |url=https://br.soccerway.com/matches/2018/09/06/brazil/serie-a/botafogo-de-futebol-e-regatas/cruzeiro-esporte-clube-belo-horizonte/2729462/ |website=Soccer Way |accessdate=22 November 2018 |archive-date=23 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181123024620/https://br.soccerway.com/matches/2018/09/06/brazil/serie-a/botafogo-de-futebol-e-regatas/cruzeiro-esporte-clube-belo-horizonte/2729462/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Despite Cruzeiro's disastrous campaign in the [[2019 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A]] (which led the team to be relegated to Série B for the first time in its history), Éderson was one of the best players in the team and was considered by many journalists one of the club's few bright spots in the season.<ref name="Da base, Cacá, Fabrício Bruno e Éderson se destacam no Cruzeiro">{{cite web |last1=Pazini |first1=Gabriel |title=Da base, Cacá, Fabrício Bruno e Éderson se destacam no Cruzeiro |url=https://www.otempo.com.br/superfc/cruzeiro/da-base-caca-fabricio-bruno-e-ederson-se-destacam-no-cruzeiro-1.2257532 |website=O Tempo |accessdate=21 February 2020 |archive-date=21 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200221012445/https://www.otempo.com.br/superfc/cruzeiro/da-base-caca-fabricio-bruno-e-ederson-se-destacam-no-cruzeiro-1.2257532 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Corinthians fecha contratação de Ederson por cinco temporadas" />

===Corinthians===
After Cruzeiro's relegation to [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série B|Série B]], Éderson sued the club for unpaid wages. They reached an agreement allowing him to freely sign with another club. On 20 February 2020, after several days of speculation, [[Sport Club Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]] announced they had signed Éderson for five years.<ref name="Corinthians fecha contratação de Ederson por cinco temporadas">{{cite web |last1=Carvalho |first1=Samir |title=Corinthians fecha contratação de Ederson por cinco temporadas |url=https://www.uol.com.br/esporte/futebol/ultimas-noticias/2020/02/20/corinthians-fecha-contratacao-de-ederson-por-cinco-temporadas.htm |website=UOL |accessdate=21 February 2020 |archive-date=20 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200220175657/https://www.uol.com.br/esporte/futebol/ultimas-noticias/2020/02/20/corinthians-fecha-contratacao-de-ederson-por-cinco-temporadas.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Fortaleza===
On 20 February 2021, Éderson was loaned to [[Fortaleza EC|Fortaleza]]. He debuted with Fortaleza on 10 March of the same year. In Fortaleza, in 2021, he was one of the main players of the club during the Campeonato Brasileiro of that year, helping the club to qualify to the Copa Libertadores of 2022.

===Salernitana===
On 30 January 2022, Éderson signed a contract with [[US Salernitana 1919|Salernitana]] in Italy until 2026.<ref>{{cite press release|publisher=[[U.S. Salernitana 1919|Salernitana]]|url=https://www.ussalernitana1919.it/ederson-e-un-nuovo-giocatore-della-salernitana/|title=EDERSON È UN NUOVO GIOCATORE DELLA SALERNITANA|date=30 January 2022|access-date=30 January 2022|language=it|archive-date=30 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220130093054/https://www.ussalernitana1919.it/ederson-e-un-nuovo-giocatore-della-salernitana/|url-status=live}}</ref> A few months later, on 16 April, he scored his first [[Serie A]] goal in a 2–1 away win over [[U.C. Sampdoria|Sampdoria]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/614602/salernitana-sampdoria |title=Sampdoria 1–2 Salernitana |publisher=ESPN |date=16 April 2022 }}</ref>

===Atalanta===
On 6 July 2022, Éderson joined fellow Serie A club [[Atalanta BC|Atalanta]].<ref>{{cite press release|publisher=[[Atalanta B.C.|Atalanta]]|url=https://www.atalanta.it/en/news/welcome-ederson/|title=Welcome, Éderson!|date=6 July 2022|access-date=6 July 2022|language=en|archive-date=8 July 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220708052524/https://www.atalanta.it/en/news/welcome-ederson/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 15 January 2023, he netted his first goal for the club in an 8–2 victory over his former club Salernitana.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/match/_/gameId/644787/salernitana-atalanta |title=Atalanta 8–2 Salernitana |publisher=ESPN |date=15 January 2023 }}</ref> In his second season, he managed to achieve the [[2023–24 UEFA Europa League|UEFA Europa League]] title with the club.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://copaamerica.com/en/news/ederson-an-europa-league-champion-dreaming-of-his-first-conmebol-copa-america |title=Éderson, An Europa League champion dreaming of his first CONMEBOL Copa América™ |publisher=Copa America CONMEBOL |date=22 May 2024 }}</ref> On 29 January 2025, he scored his first [[UEFA Champions League]] goal in a 2–2 away draw against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/player-ratings-barcelona-2-2-221100914.html |title=Player ratings: Barcelona 2-2 Atalanta – Ederson and Pasalic on target |publisher=Yahoo Sports |date=29 January 2025 }}</ref>

==International career==
On 7 October 2018, Éderson was called up to play for the [[Brazil national under-20 football team|Brazil under-20 team]] in two [[Exhibition game|friendly matches]] against [[Chile national under-20 football team|Chile]] on 13 and 15 October 2018.<ref name="Volante Ederson é convocado para a Seleção Sub-20">{{cite web |title=Volante Ederson, do Cruzeiro, é convocado para a Seleção Sub-20 |url=https://www.terra.com.br/esportes/lance/volante-ederson-do-cruzeiro-e-convocado-para-a-selecao-sub-20,b78c522d2a510d6b54b79c03d1b89ea0fwarct7i.html |website=[[Terra (company)|Terra.com]] |accessdate=22 November 2018 |archive-date=23 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181123022645/https://www.terra.com.br/esportes/lance/volante-ederson-do-cruzeiro-e-convocado-para-a-selecao-sub-20,b78c522d2a510d6b54b79c03d1b89ea0fwarct7i.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Volante Ederson, do Cruzeiro, é convocado para a Seleção Sub-20">{{cite web |title=Volante Ederson, do Cruzeiro, é convocado para a Seleção Sub-20 |url=https://www.lance.com.br/cruzeiro/volante-ederson-convocado-para-selecao-sub.html |website=[[Lance!]] |accessdate=22 November 2018 |archive-date=25 January 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190125110143/https://www.lance.com.br/cruzeiro/volante-ederson-convocado-para-selecao-sub.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He played as a starter in the second game, a 2–2 draw.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 October 2018 |title=Seleção Brasileira Sub-20 empata com o Chile em Santiago |url=https://www.cbf.com.br/selecao-brasileira/jogos/selecao-base-masculina/amistoso-internacional-brasil-sub-20-x-chile |access-date=4 May 2022 |website=Confederação Brasileira de Futebol |language=pt-BR |archive-date=29 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220529050821/https://www.cbf.com.br/selecao-brasileira/jogos/selecao-base-masculina/amistoso-internacional-brasil-sub-20-x-chile |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 19 May 2024, Éderson received his first call-up to the senior [[Brazil national football team|Brazil national team]], being included in the squad for the [[2024 Copa América]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cbf.com.br/selecao-brasileira/noticias/selecao-masculina/dorival-junior-completa-lista-da-copa-america |title=Dorival Júnior completa lista da Copa América |date=19 May 2024 |website=cbf.com.br |publisher=[[Brazilian Football Confederation]] |access-date=19 May 2024 |language=pt-br |trans-title=Dorival Júnior completes Copa América list}}</ref> He made his debut on 8 June 2024, in a friendly against [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]] at [[Kyle Field]] in Texas, United States. He started the game and played 84 minutes, Brazil won 3–2.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/692533/|title=Mexico v Brazil game report|date=8 June 2024}}</ref> Éderson was named in Brazil's preliminary 55-man squad for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]], but initially did not make the final 26-man squad.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/czd2ev0ggj5o |title=Man Utd closing in on £38m Ederson deal |website=BBC Sport |date=27 May 2026 |access-date=28 May 2026}}</ref> However, on 7 June, he was named in the final squad, replacing right-back [[Wesley França|Wesley]], who suffered a injury the day before in a friendly against [[Egypt national football team|Egypt]] and had to be cut out.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ge.globo.com/google/amp/futebol/copa-do-mundo/noticia/2026/06/07/wesley-e-cortado-da-selecao-por-lesao-na-perna-esquerda.ghtml |title=Wesley é cortado da Seleção por lesão na perna esquerda; volante Éderson é convocado |date=7 June 2026 |website=ge.globo |publisher=ge |access-date=7 June 2026 |language=pt-br |trans-title=Wesley is cut from the national team due to an left leg injury; midfielder Éderson is called}}</ref>

==Style of play==
{{Quote box
| width = 30%
| align = right
| quote = Éderson. He is out of this world for his ability to combine running, physicality, technique and intelligence.
| source = Italian former manager [[Fabio Capello]]<ref>{{cite news |title=Fabio Capello boccia il Milan e critica duramente Emerson Royal |work=Sport2U |date=7 December 2024 |url=https://sport2u.tv/fabio-capello-boccia-il-milan-e-critica-duramente-emerson-royal/ |access-date=5 June 2026}}</ref>
}}
Éderson has been described as an all-round midfielder, capable of winning possession and then either passing or carrying the ball forward. [[Fabio Capello]] praised his "rare tactical intelligence", while former Corinthians coach [[Tiago Nunes]] described him as a [[box-to-box midfielder]] rather than a [[deep-lying playmaker]]. Nunes highlighted his ability to break through lines, reach the final third and progress the ball up the pitch, as well as his physical strength, capacity to sustain the pace of a match and strong mentality.<ref>{{cite news |last=Bate |first=Adam |title=Manchester United transfer news: Ederson can adapt to the Premier League and be flexible for Michael Carrick |work=Sky Sports |date=3 June 2026 |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13548882/manchester-united-transfer-news-ederson-can-adapt-to-the-premier-league-and-be-flexible-for-michael-carrick |access-date=3 June 2026}}</ref>

Under [[Gian Piero Gasperini]], Éderson was typically used in a two-man midfield within a 3–4–3 system, often alongside players such as [[Teun Koopmeiners]] or [[Marten de Roon]]. His all-action style of play helped ensure that Atalanta's midfield was rarely overpowered physically. Gasperini's departure the following year altered Éderson's role at Atalanta, but he remained a dynamic midfielder who offered more than a traditional ball-winner, combining strong positional awareness with physicality across his key duties.<ref>{{cite news |last=Anka |first=Carl |title=Analysing Ederson, the first piece of Manchester United’s midfield rebuild |work=The Athletic |date=5 June 2026 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7157454/2026/06/05/ederson-manchester-united-atalanta-midfield-rebuild-analysis/ |access-date=5 June 2026}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
He has matrilineal roots in the [[Terena people|Terena]] Indigenous people of the Bananal Village in [[Aquidauana]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pimentel |first=Rilton |date=2026-06-23 |title=Seleção brasileira tem jogador de origem indígena |trans-title=The Brazilian national team has a player of Indigenous descent |url=https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/radioagencia-nacional/esportes/audio/2026-06/selecao-brasileira-tem-jogador-de-origem-indigena |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260624055248/https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/radioagencia-nacional/esportes/audio/2026-06/selecao-brasileira-tem-jogador-de-origem-indigena |archive-date=2026-06-24 |access-date=2026-07-02 |website=Agência Brasil |language=pt-br}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Varjão |first=Karina |date=2026-06-07 |title=Com raiz terena, Éderson leva nome do povo indígena ao maior palco do futebol |trans-title=With Terena roots, Éderson takes the name of the Indigenous people to the biggest stage in football |url=https://correiodoestado.com.br/cidades/com-raiz-terena-ederson-leva-nome-do-povo-indigena-ao-maior-palco-do/467758/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260617170044/https://correiodoestado.com.br/cidades/com-raiz-terena-ederson-leva-nome-do-povo-indigena-ao-maior-palco-do/467758/ |archive-date=2026-06-17 |access-date=2026-07-02 |website=correiodoestado.com.br |language=pt-BR}}</ref>

'''Wesley dos Santos Rodrigues''' (born 2 April 1992), known as '''Wesley Rodrigues''' or just '''Wesley''', is a Brazilian [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[centre-back]] for [[São José Esporte Clube|São José-SP]].

==Career==
Born in [[Paranaguá]], Paraná, Wesley represented [[Coritiba Foot Ball Club|Coritiba]] as a youth, but made his senior debut while on loan at [[Rio Branco Sport Club|Rio Branco-PR]] in 2012. In 2013, after another loan spell at [[Junior Team Futebol|Junior Team]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.coritiba.com.br/noticias/0/3215|title=Coxa cede jogadores da base ao Júnior Team|trans-title=''Coxa'' loan youth players to Junior Team|publisher=Coritiba FBC|language=pt-BR|date=30 April 2012|accessdate=16 June 2026}}</ref> he moved to [[Marília Atlético Clube|Marília]], but was rarely used.

In January 2015, after playing for [[Parnahyba Sport Club|Parnahyba]], [[Vila Operária Clube Esporte Mariano|VOCEM]] and [[Hercílio Luz Futebol Clube|Hercílio Luz]] the previous year, Wesley was included in [[Foz do Iguaçu Futebol Clube|Foz do Iguaçu]]'s squad for the [[Campeonato Paranaense]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/pr/noticia/2015/01/foz-do-iguacu-apresenta-elenco-e-comissao-tecnica-do-paranaense-2015.html|title=Foz do Iguaçu apresenta elenco e comissão técnica do Paranaense 2015|trans-title=Foz do Iguaçu present squad and technical staff of the 2025 Paranaense|publisher=[[Grupo Globo|ge]]|language=pt-BR|date=3 January 2015|accessdate=16 June 2026}}</ref> In April, he signed for [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série C|Série C]] side [[Botafogo Futebol Clube (PB)|Botafogo-PB]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tribunapr.com.br/esportes/com-o-fim-do-paranaense-foz-do-iguacu-e-desmontado/|title=Com o fim do Paranaense, Foz do Iguaçu é desmontado|trans-title=With the end of the Paranaense, Foz do Iguaçu is disbanded|publisher=Tribuna PR|language=pt-BR|date=30 April 2015|accessdate=16 June 2026}}</ref> but featured in just one match for the club.

On 24 November 2015, Wesley agreed to a deal with [[Ypiranga Futebol Clube|Ypiranga-RS]] for the upcoming season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lance.com.br/futebol-nacional/zagueiro-wesley-acerta-com-ypiranga-para-gauchao-2016.html|title=Zagueiro Wesley acerta com Ypiranga para o Gauchão 2016|trans-title=Centre-back Wesley signs with Ypiranga for the 2016 ''Gauchão''|publisher=[[Lance!]]|language=pt-BR|date=24 November 2015|accessdate=16 June 2026}}</ref> Regularly used during the [[2016 Campeonato Gaúcho]], he moved to [[Maringá Futebol Clube|Maringá]] in May, but ended the year at [[Clube Esportivo União|União Beltrão]].

In 2017, Wesley moved abroad for the first time in his career and joined [[Global Cebu F.C.|Global Cebu]] of the [[Philippines Football League]]. He left the club in May 2018,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1035970|title=Ahead of PFL return, Cebu parts ways with foreign recruits|publisher=[[Philippine News Agency]]|date=22 May 2018|accessdate=16 June 2026}}</ref> and signed for fellow league team [[Davao Aguilas F.C.|Davao Aguilas]] on 1 June.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.ph/football/asian-football/philippine-football/pfl/863540/wesley-rodrigues-joins-davao-aguilas/|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180711103457/https://www.foxsports.ph/football/asian-football/philippine-football/pfl/863540/wesley-rodrigues-joins-davao-aguilas/|title=Brazilian defender Wesley Dos Santos Rodrigues joins Davao Aguilas|publisher=[[Fox Sports (Philippines)|Fox Sports]]|date=1 June 2018|archivedate=11 July 2018|accessdate=16 June 2026}}</ref>

On 10 December 2018, Wesley returned to his home country after being announced at [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série B|Série B]] side [[Esporte Clube São Bento|São Bento]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/sp/tem-esporte/futebol/noticia/sonho-antigo-sao-bento-acerta-a-contratacao-do-centroavante-henan.ghtml|title=Sonho antigo, São Bento acerta a contratação do centroavante Henan|trans-title=Old dream, São Bento sign centre forward Henan|publisher=[[Grupo Globo|ge]]|language=pt-BR|date=10 December 2018|accessdate=16 June 2026}}</ref> He moved to third division side [[Boa Esporte Clube|Boa Esporte]] on 3 November 2019,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/mg/sul-de-minas/futebol/times/boa-esporte/noticia/boa-esporte-anuncia-contratacao-do-zagueiro-wesley-ex-sao-bento.ghtml|title=Boa Esporte anuncia contratação do zagueiro Wesley, ex-São Bento|trans-title=Boa Esporte announce the signing of centre-back Wesley, formerly of São Bento|publisher=[[Grupo Globo|ge]]|language=pt-BR|date=3 November 2019|accessdate=16 June 2026}}</ref> and signed for [[Thep Xanh Nam Dinh F.C.|Nam Định]] in Vietnam in December 2020.

Wesley left Nam Định after the remaining matches of the [[2021 V.League 1]] were cancelled, and returned to Brazil with [[Associação Atlética de Altos|Altos]] in November of that year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/pi/futebol/times/altos/noticia/altos-anuncia-zagueiro-wesley-ex-nam-dinh-do-vietna.ghtml|title=Altos anuncia zagueiro Wesley, ex- Nam Dinh, do Vietnã|trans-title=Altos announce centre-back Wesley, formerly of Nam Dinh, from Vietnam|publisher=[[Grupo Globo|ge]]|language=pt-BR|date=8 November 2021|accessdate=16 June 2026}}</ref> However, the deal fell through, and he joined [[Camboriú Futebol Clube|Camboriú]] on 8 January 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/sc/futebol/times/camboriu/noticia/camboriu-confirma-contratacao-do-zagueiro-wesley-dos-santos.ghtml|title=Camboriú confirma contratação do zagueiro Wesley dos Santos|trans-title=Camboriú confirm signing of centre-back Wesley dos Santos|publisher=[[Grupo Globo|ge]]|language=pt-BR|date=8 January 2022|accessdate=16 June 2026}}</ref>

Wesley subsequently had short spells at [[Sociedade Esportiva e Recreativa Caxias do Sul|Caxias]] and [[Barra Futebol Clube (SC)|Barra-SC]] before returning to Maringá in February 2023. He renewed his contract with the latter until October 2025 in August,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.jornaldooeste.com.br/maringa-futebol-clube-renova-o-contrato-com-o-zagueiro-wesley-santos-ate-outubro-de-2025/|title=Maringá Futebol Clube renova o contrato com o zagueiro Wesley Santos até outubro de 2025|trans-title=Maringá Futebol Clube renew contract with centre-back Wesley Santos until October 2025|publisher=Jornal do Oeste|language=pt-BR|date=18 August 2023|accessdate=16 June 2026}}</ref> before being loaned out to [[Paysandu Sport Club|Paysandu]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dol.com.br/esporte/esporte-para/823642/paysandu-contrata-zagueiro-wesley-apos-lesao-grave-de-paulao?d=1|title=Paysandu contrata zagueiro Wesley após lesão grave de Paulão|trans-title=Paysandu sign centre-back Wesley after Paulão's serious injury|publisher=DOL|language=pt-BR|date=17 August 2023|accessdate=16 June 2026}}</ref>

Wesley terminated his link with ''Dogão'' on 8 December 2023,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/pr/futebol/noticia/2023/12/08/wesley-rescinde-com-o-maringa-e-encaminha-acerto-com-o-abc.ghtml|title=Wesley rescinde com o Maringá e encaminha acerto com o ABC|trans-title=Wesley rescinds with Maringá and sets deal with ABC|publisher=[[Grupo Globo|ge]]|language=pt-BR|date=8 December 2023|accessdate=16 June 2026}}</ref> and was announced at [[ABC Futebol Clube|ABC]] two days later.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://abcfc.com.br/comunicacao/noticias/zagueiro-wesley-e-mais-um-reforco-abecedista/|title=Zagueiro Wesley é mais um reforço abecedista|trans-title=Centre-back Wesley is another ''abecedista'' addition|publisher=ABC FC|language=pt-BR|date=10 December 2023|accessdate=16 June 2026}}</ref> On 4 November 2024, he joined [[Floresta Esporte Clube|Floresta]] for the year's [[Copa Fares Lopes]].

On 11 January 2025, Wesley agreed to a deal with [[Cianorte Futebol Clube|Cianorte]]. On 2 April of the following year, he was announced at [[Pouso Alegre Futebol Clube|Pouso Alegre]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/mg/sul-de-minas/futebol/times/pouso-alegre-fc/noticia/2026/04/02/pouso-alegre-anuncia-quatro-reforcos-e-intensifica-preparacao-para-estreia-na-serie-d.ghtml|title=Pouso Alegre anuncia quatro reforços e intensifica preparação para estreia na Série D|trans-title=Pouso Alegre announce four signings and intensify preparations for Série D debut|publisher=[[Grupo Globo|ge]]|language=pt-BR|date=2 April 2026|accessdate=16 June 2026}}</ref> but moved to [[São José Esporte Clube|São José-SP]] on 15 June, after ''Pousão''{{'}}s elimination from the [[2026 Campeonato Brasileiro Série D|2026 Série D]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/sp/vale-do-paraiba-regiao/futebol/times/sao-jose-sp/noticia/2026/06/15/sao-jose-contrata-o-zagueiro-wesley-rodrigues-ex-pouso-alegre-para-a-disputa-da-copa-paulista.ghtml|title=São José contrata o zagueiro Wesley Rodrigues, ex-Pouso Alegre, para a disputa da Copa Paulista|trans-title=São José sign centre-back Wesley Rodrigues, formerly of Pouso Alegre, for the Copa Paulista|publisher=[[Grupo Globo|ge]]|language=pt-BR|date=15 June 2026|accessdate=16 June 2026}}</ref>

'''Yuri Jonathan Vitor Coelho''' (born 12 June 1998), commonly known as '''Yuri Tanque''', is a Brazilian [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Criciúma Esporte Clube|Criciúma]].

==Career==
Having started his career at Ponte Preta, Tanque particularly distinguished himself while playing for [[Jeju United]] in the [[K League 1]]<ref>{{cite web | last1=Pereira | first1=Leo | title=Tanque analisa primeira temporada pelo Jeju United | work=Jogada 10 | date=22 November 2023 | url=https://jogada10.com.br/tanque-analisa-primeira-temporada-no-jeju-united-da-coreia-do-sul/ }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://correio.rac.com.br/esportes/yuri-tanque-esta-a-caminho-do-jezu-united-1.1324239|title=Yuri Tanque está a caminho do Jezu United|date=23 December 2022|website=Correio Popular}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.maisgoias.com.br/esportes/nascido-em-porangatu-centroavante-do-jeju-united-vibra-com-estreia-na-k-league-2024-entenda/|title=Nascido em Porangatu, centroavante do Jeju United vibra com estreia na K-League 2024; entenda|first1=Mais|last1=Goiás|first2=Victor|last2=Pimenta|work=Mais Goiás |date=5 March 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://esportes.r7.com/futebol/ex-ponte-preta-e-guarani-brasileiro-se-destaca-no-futebol-sul-coreano-06122023/ |title=Ex-Ponte Preta e Guarani, brasileiro se destaca no futebol Sul-Coreano  |website=R7 Esportes |date=6 December 2023 |language=pt }}</ref> and for [[Capivariano Futebol Clube|Capivariano]], where he was the top scorer of the 2022 edition of [[Campeonato Paulista Série A3]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.futebolinterior.com.br/serie-a3-atacante-yuri-do-capivariano-se-emociona-ao-receber-trofeu-de-artilheiro/|title=Paulista A3: Atacante Yuri, do Capivariano, se emociona ao receber troféu de artilheiro|work=Futebol Interior|last=Silva|first=Oscar|date=25 May 2022}}</ref> For the 2026 season, he signed a contract with [[Criciúma Esporte Clube|Criciúma]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/sc/futebol/times/criciuma/noticia/2026/04/18/saiba-como-esta-a-recuperacao-de-atleta-do-criciuma-que-teve-lesao-antes-de-estreia.ghtml|title=Saiba como está a recuperação de atleta do Criciúma que teve lesão antes de estreia|date=18 April 2026|website=ge}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.4oito.com.br/blog/enio-biz/post/yuri-tanque-e-apresentado-pelo-criciuma-relembra-recuperacao-e-diz-mao-de-deus-em-cada-detalhe-16628 |title=Yuri Tanque é apresentado pelo Criciúma, relembra recuperação e diz: 'Mão de Deus em cada detalhe' |website=4oito |author=Ênio Biz |date=4 August 2026 |language=pt}}</ref>

'''Agustín Oliveros Cano''' (born 17 August 1998) is a Uruguayan professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|left-back]] for [[Liga MX]] club [[Club Necaxa|Necaxa]].<ref name="soccerway">{{Soccerway|new_id=oliveros-agustin/Iqp4kDKm|access-date=29 September 2026}}</ref>

==Club career==
Oliveros is a youth academy graduate of [[Racing Club de Montevideo|Racing Montevideo]]. He made his professional debut for the club, on 2 June 2018 in a 2–0 league defeat to [[Danubio F.C.|Danubio]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Debutantes de las fechas 6 y 7|url=https://auf.org.uy/debutantes-de-las-fechas-6-y-7/|date=8 June 2018|access-date=27 May 2024}}</ref>

On 14 February 2020, Oliveros joined [[Club Nacional de Football|Nacional]] on loan, signing a 2.5 year contract,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Racing Club de Montevideo |date=2020-02-15 |title=Agustín Oliveros pasa a préstamo por dos años y medio a Nacional. |url=https://x.com/racingcluburu/status/1228712396698595329 |access-date=2025-03-31 |website=twitter}}</ref> when the club acquired 50% of the player's rights.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mesa de Redacción |date=2020-02-14 |title=Agustin Oliveros, la última alta |url=https://www.tenfield.com.uy/agustin-oliveros-la-ultima-alta/ |access-date=2025-03-31 |website=Tenfield.com |language=es}}</ref>

After winning the [[2020 Uruguayan Primera División season|2020 Uruguayan Primera División]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Comisión Historia C. N. de F |first= |date=2021-04-07 |title=CAMPEONATO URUGUAYO 2020 |url=https://atilio.uy/copa:260 |access-date=2025-03-31 |website=Atilio Software}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-04-09 |title=Agustín Oliveros: del descenso con Racing en 2019 a campeón uruguayo con Nacional en el 2020 |url=https://espndeportes.espn.com/futbol/uruguay/nota/_/id/8445055/agustin-oliveros-del-descenso-con-racing-en-2019-a-campeon-uruguayo-con-nacional-en-el-2020 |access-date=2025-03-31 |website=ESPNdeportes.com |language=es}}</ref> and getting called up to the [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguayan national team]],<ref name=":0" /> on 7 June 2021, he joined [[Liga MX]] side [[Club Necaxa|Necaxa]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-06-08 |title=AGUSTÍN OLIVEROS LLEGA A LOS RAYOS DEL NECAXA. |url=https://www.clubnecaxa.mx/noticias/2552/AGUSTN-OLIVEROS-LLEGA-A-LOS-RAYOS-DEL-NECAXA |access-date=2025-03-31 |website=www.clubnecaxa.mx |language=en}}</ref>

==International career==

[[Sinn Bodhi]] | debut = September 22, 2012 }} '''Jacob Fatu''' (born April 18, 1992) is an American [[professional wrestler]]. He is signed to [[WWE]], where he performs on the [[Raw (WWE brand)|Raw]] [[WWE brand extension|brand]] and is a member of [[The Bloodline]] stable. Fatu made his professional wrestling debut in 2012, performing in various [[independent circuit|independent]] [[Professional wrestling promotion|promotions]] including [[All Pro Wrestling]], [[DEFY Wrestling]], [[Game Changer Wrestling]], [[House of Glory]], and [[PCW Ultra]]. In 2019, he signed with [[Major League Wrestling]] (MLW), where he won the [[MLW World Heavyweight Championship]], the [[MLW National Openweight Championship]], and the fourth [[Battle Riot]] in [[Battle Riot IV|2022]]. His 819-day reign as MLW World Heavyweight Champion is the longest in the promotion's history. In 2024, Fatu signed with WWE and debuted as part of The Bloodline stable. During the following year, he won the [[WWE Tag Team Championship]] and the [[WWE United States Championship]] at [[WrestleMania 41]]. Fatu is part of the [[Anoaʻi family]] of professional wrestlers. He then went outside, where he killed a man, discarded his Windham WW-15, and retrieved a [[Ruger AR-556]] AR-15 from his car. He went to the mosque's southern gate and, from there, killed two people and injured a third in the car park as they were sheltering behind vehicles. He reentered the mosque and shot already-wounded people, then again went outside, where he killed a woman.{{cite web |title=5.3 Firearms, ammunition and other equipment used in the terrorist attack |date=17 August 2017 |url=https://christchurchattack.royalcommission.nz/the-report/firearms-licensing/preparation-for-the-terrorist-attack/ |publisher=Royal Commission of Inquiry into the Attack on Christchurch Mosques on 15 March 2019 |access-date=25 October 2023 |archive-date=30 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231030171406/https://christchurchattack.royalcommission.nz/the-report/firearms-licensing/preparation-for-the-terrorist-attack/ |url-status=live }} Thereupon Tarrant drove over the deceased woman, leaving six minutes after he arrived at the mosque. He shot at fleeing worshippers and cars through the [[Windshield|windscreen]] and closed window of his own car with the [[Remington Model 870]] shotgun as he was driving towards the Linwood Islamic Centre.{{cite web|title=The terrorist attack|url=https://christchurchattack.royalcommission.nz/the-report/part-1-purpose-and-process/the-terrorist-attack/|access-date=12 December 2020|website=Royal Commission of Inquiry into the Attack on Christchurch Mosques on 15 March 2019|language=en-NZ|archive-date=23 December 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201223110253/https://christchurchattack.royalcommission.nz/the-report/part-1-purpose-and-process/the-terrorist-attack/|url-status=live}} At 1:46{{nbsp}}p.m., police arrived near the mosque just as Tarrant was leaving, but his car was hidden by a bus, and at the time, no description of the vehicle had been provided, or that he had left.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/new-zealand/2019/04/christchurch-terror-attack-police-release-official-timeline.html|title=Christchurch terror attack: Police release official timeline|work=[[Newshub]]|access-date=28 February 2020|archive-date=28 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200228235047/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/new-zealand/2019/04/christchurch-terror-attack-police-release-official-timeline.html|url-status=dead}} He drove eastwards on [[Bealey Avenue]] at up to {{convert|130|km/h|abbr=on}}, weaving between lanes against oncoming traffic and driving onto a grass [[median strip]]. At 1:51{{nbsp}}p.m., just after the livestream had ended due to a connection interruption, he aimed a shotgun at the driver of a vehicle on Avonside Drive and attempted to fire it twice, but it failed to fire on both occasions. The GoPro device attached to Tarrant's helmet continued recording until he was apprehended by police eight minutes later. === Linwood Islamic Centre === [[File:Linwood Islamic Centre, March 2020. At the time of the shootings, there was a building at the front of the section and access was along an ungated driveway to the left.]] At 1:52{{nbsp}}p.m., Tarrant arrived at the [[Linwood Islamic Centre]], {{Convert|5|km|mi|0|abbr=}} east of the Al Noor Mosque,{{Cite news|last1=Perry|first1=Nick|last2=Baker|first2=Mark|date=15 March 2019|title=Mosque shootings kill 49; white racist claims responsibility|work=Star Tribune|url=http://www.startribune.com/witness-many-dead-in-new-zealand-mosque-shooting/507178452/|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190321201556/http://www.startribune.com/witness-many-dead-in-new-zealand-mosque-shooting/507178452/|archive-date=21 March 2019}} while about 100 people were inside. He parked his vehicle on the mosque's driveway, preventing other cars from entering or leaving. According to a witness, Tarrant was initially unable to find the mosque's main door, instead shooting people outside and through a window, killing four and alerting those inside.{{cite news |last=Macdonald |first=Nikki |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/christchurch-shooting/111378767/brenton-tarrant-approached-linwood-mosque-from-wrong-side-giving-those-inside-time-to-hide-survivor-says |title=Alleged shooter approached Linwood mosque from wrong side, giving those inside time to hide, survivor says |work=[[Stuff (company)]] |date=18 March 2019 |access-date=20 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190318191317/https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/christchurch-shooting/111378767/brenton-tarrant-approached-linwood-mosque-from-wrong-side-giving-those-inside-time-to-hide-survivor-says |archive-date=18 March 2019 |url-status=live}} A worshipper named [[Abdul Aziz Wahabzadah|Abdul Aziz Wahabzada]] ran outside. As Tarrant was retrieving more weapons from his car, Aziz threw a [[payment terminal]] at him. Tarrant fired back at Aziz, who picked up an empty shotgun that Tarrant had dropped. He took cover among nearby cars and attempted to draw Tarrant's attention by shouting, "I'm here!" Regardless, Tarrant entered the mosque, where he shot and killed three people. When Tarrant returned to his car, Aziz confronted him again. Tarrant removed a [[bayonet]] from his vest but then retreated into his car instead of attacking Aziz. === Guilty plea and sentencing arrangements === On 26 March 2020, Tarrant appeared at the Christchurch High Court via audio-visual link from Auckland Prison. === Media response === For the three months following the shooting, almost 1,000 reports were published in major news outlets in New Zealand. Less than 10% of news reports published by major media outlets mentioned Tarrant's name. [[Susanna Every-Palmer]], an academic psychiatrist, suggested that the media made a moral choice to deny Tarrant exposure and not sensationalise his views, deviating from how similar events internationally were covered in the media. The court required the media to pixelate Tarrant's face when covering the legal proceedings, thus, within New Zealand, he remained largely faceless and nameless. Instead, media coverage focused largely on the victims and their families.{{cite journal |last1=Every-Palmer |first1=S. |last2=Cunningham |first2=R. |last3=Jenkins |first3=M. |last4=Bell |first4=E. |title=The Christchurch mosque shooting, the media, and subsequent gun control reform in New Zealand: a descriptive analysis |journal=Psychiatry, Psychology and Law |date=23 June 2020 |volume=28 |issue=2 |pages=274–285 |doi=10.1080/13218719.2020.1770635 |pmid=34712096 |pmc=8547820 |s2cid=225699765 |issn=1321-8719}}{{cite journal |last1=Ellis |first1=Gavin |last2=Muller |first2=Denis |title=The proximity filter: the effect of distance on media coverage of the Christchurch mosque attacks |journal=Kōtuitui: New Zealand Journal of Social Sciences Online |date=2 July 2020 |volume=15 |issue=2 |pages=332–348 |doi=10.1080/1177083X.2019.1705358|doi-access=free }} In contrast, the media response in Australia was different, focusing on the extreme violence of the attack, as well as the attacker and his manifesto. For example, ''[[The Australian]]'' published an audio excerpt containing cries for help, and ''[[The Herald Sun]]'' wrote dramatic descriptions of victims being shot and used poetic devices to create more vivid imagery. The operation was designed to reassure New Zealanders after the attack and to also investigate possible threats who shared a similar ideology to the gunman. Police increased visibility in streets and visited many schools, businesses, and religious places as part of the operation. In Canterbury alone, there were almost 600 people of interest to police, where hundreds of properties were searched. |archive-date=3 August 2021|url-status=live}} ''Widows of Shuhada'' (widows of martyrs) was the name of a [[Radio New Zealand]] (RNZ) documentary series about the widows of four men who were killed in 2021}} ===Awards=== On 6 July 2022, [[Governor-General of New Zealand|Governor-General]] [[Cindy Kiro]] awarded the [[New Zealand Cross (1999)|New Zealand Cross]] to Linwood Mosque survivor Abdul Aziz and the late Naeem Rashid for confronting Tarrant. In addition, Kiro awarded the [[New Zealand Bravery Decoration]] to Senior Constables Scott Carmody and Jim Manning for apprehending the terrorist; and Liam Beale and Wayne Maley for helping survivors of the Al Noor mosque.
