In both cases, Rossi was found guilty of rape.<ref name="BBC Rape 1" /><ref name="BBC Rape 2" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Utah State Courts {{!}} Xchange: Public Case Search |url=https://www.utcourts.gov/en/court-records-publications/records/xchange.html |access-date=2025-07-18 |website=www.utcourts.gov |archive-date=July 24, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250724221618/https://www.utcourts.gov/en/court-records-publications/records/xchange.html |url-status=live }}</ref> For the first rape conviction, he was sentenced to five years to life.{{efn|Utah uses [[indeterminate sentencing]], with a convict's release date, if any, decided by the [[Utah Board of Pardons and Parole|Board of Pardons and Parole]].<ref name="Guardian-20251020">{{cite news |title=US man accused of faking own death after rape conviction gets at least five years in prison |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/oct/20/nicholas-rossi-fake-death-rape-conviction |access-date=21 October 2025 |work=The Guardian |date=20 October 2025}}</ref>}}<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.abc4.com/news/crime/nicholas-rossi-sentencing-hearing/|title=Nicholas Rossi sentenced to 5 years to life in Salt Lake County rape case|last=Bittan|first=Ryan|work=[[KTVX]]|date=October 20, 2025|accessdate=October 20, 2025|archive-date=October 21, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251021024951/https://www.abc4.com/news/crime/nicholas-rossi-sentencing-hearing/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On November 4, 2025, Rossi was sentenced to another five years to life to be served after the completion of the first sentence.<ref>{{cite news |last1=BBC |title=US fugitive Nicholas Rossi to serve at least 10 years in jail |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cjw96x30xddo |access-date=4 November 2025 |agency=BBC |archive-date=November 4, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251104203551/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cjw96x30xddo |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Death ===
Rossi died on June 25, 2026, at a local hospital "from complications of an existing medical condition after choosing to discontinue medical treatment", according to the [[Utah Department of Corrections]], which also said he had "chronic, degenerative conditions". He was 38.<ref name=UDC>{{Cite web|title=Inmate Nicholas Rossi Passes Away|url=https://corrections.utah.gov/udc-announces-death-of-nicolas-rossi/|access-date=2026-06-26|language=en-us|publisher=[[Utah Department of Corrections]]|date=2026-06-26|archive-date=June 26, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260626175338/https://corrections.utah.gov/udc-announces-death-of-nicolas-rossi/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=June 26, 2026 |title=Nicholas Rossi: Rapist who faked death and fled to Scotland dies in US prison |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cz75px7zl0wo |access-date=June 26, 2026 |website=[[BBC News]] |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Convicted Rapist Who Fled to Scotland and Faked His Own Death Dies in Utah|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/26/us/nicholas-rossi-fugitive-rape-death.html|access-date=2026-06-27|language=en-us|work=The New York Times|first=Mack|last=Liederman|date=2026-06-26}}</ref>

== Child welfare advocacy ==
When Rossi returned to Rhode Island in the 2010s, he reinvented himself as a crusader for child welfare and aggressively sought connections with politicians and reporters. Rossi eagerly provided quotations to reporters, but he did not talk much about his life in Utah or Ohio, where he had been accused of sexually assaulting women. Dan McGowan, a reporter for the ''[[Boston Globe]]'', said that Rossi's stories "mostly checked out", and when he raised Rossi's legal issues with another reporter, they were willing to give Rossi the benefit of the doubt because of his difficult family life.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/3239615815|title=Nicholas Alahverdian faked his own death. Now he's been convicted of rape.|last=McGowan|first=Dan|work=[[Boston Globe]]|via=[[ProQuest]]|date=August 15, 2025 |id={{ProQuest|3239615815}} }}</ref>

Rossi founded NexusGovernment, an organization to lobby for child welfare.<ref name="Heller" /><ref name="Arditi11" />

In March 2011, after meeting Rossi, state representative [[Roberto DaSilva]] submitted a proposal to further restrict DCYF from using facilities outside of Rhode Island; the proposal was also a cost-cutting measure.<ref name="Heller" /> DaSilva credited Rossi's story as inspiration for his proposed legislation.<ref name="Lord">{{cite web |last1=Lord |first1=Peter |title=Rep. DaSilva says R.I. pays hundreds of thousands of dollars for out-of-state care for children in state custody |url=https://www.politifact.com/rhode-island/statements/2011/apr/08/roberto-dasilva/rep-dasilva-says-ri-pays-hundreds-thousands-dollar/ |website=Politifact |publisher=Poynter Institute |access-date=November 13, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181202031722/https://www.politifact.com/rhode-island/statements/2011/apr/08/roberto-dasilva/rep-dasilva-says-ri-pays-hundreds-thousands-dollar/ |archive-date=December 2, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> The proposed legislation failed, so DaSilva re-submitted the proposal in January 2012 and it was given a hearing the following month, but shelved for "further study" in mid-March.<ref name="DaSilva1">{{cite web|title=DaSilva reintroduces bill to keep children under DCYF care in state|url=http://www.golocalprov.com/news/new-dasilva-reintroduces-bill-to-keep-children-under-dcyf-care-in-state/|publisher=GoLocalProv|access-date=May 10, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150416031604/http://www.golocalprov.com/news/new-dasilva-reintroduces-bill-to-keep-children-under-dcyf-care-in-state|archive-date=April 16, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Rhode Island H7135 {{!}} 2012 {{!}} Regular Session |url=https://legiscan.com/RI/bill/H7135/2012 |access-date=October 6, 2022 |website=LegiScan |language=en |archive-date=October 6, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221006204500/https://legiscan.com/RI/bill/H7135/2012 |url-status=live}}</ref>

In February 2020, Rhode Island state representatives Raymond Hull, [[John J. Lombardi]], [[David Bennett (Rhode Island politician)|David Bennett]], and [[James N. McLaughlin]] proposed an "Emergency Oversight Commission" to monitor DCYF, as advocated by Rossi.<ref name="Commission2">{{cite news |last1=Cook |first1=Scott |title=Lawmakers propose 'Emergency Oversight Commission' for DCYF |url=https://www.abc6.com/story/41732073/lawmakers-propose-emergency-oversight-commission-for-dcyf |access-date=March 3, 2020 |agency=ABC 6 News|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200219190642/https://www.abc6.com/story/41732073/lawmakers-propose-emergency-oversight-commission-for-dcy| archive-date=February 19, 2020 |url-status=dead}}</ref> According to WPRI's reporting, if the legislation passed, nine state representatives would form a commission to investigate "unconstitutional or unethical procedures at DCYF that put children in harm's way", with a report to be published in May 2021.<ref name=CommPurpose>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wpri.com/news/local-news/providence/emergency-oversight-commission-for-dcyf-proposed-by-lawmakers/|title=Emergency oversight commission for DCYF proposed by lawmakers|last=Tomison|first=Bill|date=February 18, 2020|website=WPRI|access-date=February 18, 2020|archive-date=February 19, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200219005830/https://www.wpri.com/news/local-news/providence/emergency-oversight-commission-for-dcyf-proposed-by-lawmakers/|url-status=live}}</ref> Hull's proposed legislation was not voted upon and died in committee.<ref name="Death1" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Rhode Island H7639 {{!}} 2020 {{!}} Regular Session |url=https://legiscan.com/RI/bill/H7639/2020 |access-date=October 6, 2022 |website=LegiScan |language=en |archive-date=October 6, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221006205533/https://legiscan.com/RI/bill/H7639/2020 |url-status=live }}</ref> Hull later said that Rossi had continually pressed him to introduce this legislation before faking his death, describing the process as being that Rossi would "just beat you down".<ref name="pj02" />

Former Rhode Island state representatives spoke in 2022 about their past experiences with Rossi. Coogan described Rossi as "brilliant" but "dangerous", accusing Rossi of having "swindled a lot of people", by persuading some Rhode Island lawmakers to give him money, sometimes via threats of accusing them of rape and assault.<ref name=dangerous/> [[Joanne Giannini]] said that Rossi continually asked her for money. After initially acceding to his requests, Giannini eventually told him to "get a job". This resulted in Rossi saying "so many horrible things" to her, "He knew how to hurt you with words. The whole thing really bothered me."<ref name=dangerous/>

=== Lawsuit against the DCYF ===
In February 2011, Rossi initiated a federal lawsuit against the DCYF, the states of Florida and Nebraska, six residential facilities, and 18 individuals, for alleged abuse committed against him.<ref name=Arditi11>{{cite news |last1=Arditi |first1=Lynn |title=Alahverdian sues DCYF for child abuse |url=http://digital.olivesoftware.com/Olive/APA/Projo/SharedView.Article.aspx?href=TPJ%2F2011%2F04%2F08&id=Ar00702&sk=F2C80340&viewMode=text |access-date=November 13, 2019 |publisher=The Providence Journal |date=April 8, 2011 |archive-date=January 28, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210128223312/http://digital.olivesoftware.com/Olive/APA/Projo/SharedView.Article.aspx?href=TPJ%2F2011%2F04%2F08&id=Ar00702&sk=F2C80340&viewMode=text |url-status=live }}</ref> Among the individuals sued were Rhode Island Governor [[Donald Carcieri]] and Family Court Chief Judge Jeremiah S. Jeremiah.<ref name=Buteau33>{{cite web|last1=Buteau|first1=Walt|title=Suit against DCYF settled|url=https://www.wpri.com/2013/08/22/suit-against-dcyf-settled//|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151203132528/https://www.wpri.com/2013/08/22/suit-against-dcyf-settled//|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 3, 2015|website=WPRI.com|publisher=CBS News|access-date=November 10, 2019}}</ref>

In August 2013, the federal lawsuit was settled by the parties, in exchange for Rhode Island waiving a more than $200,000 lien that was placed on any settlement proceeds from the lawsuit. The lien was for medical expenses incurred while he was in state foster care.<ref name=Buteau33 /> The lawsuit concluded with the DCYF expressly denying any "liability or culpability regarding the allegations" according to the DCYF's deputy director Kevin Aucoin.<ref name=Buteau33 /> Rossi acknowledged that he had released the state of Rhode Island and its government employees from liability.<ref name="Arditi1" /> The court itself did not reveal details of the settlement.<ref name="Arditi1">{{cite news|last1=Arditi|first1=Lynn|title=Settlement ends suit by former ward alleging abuse while in care of Rhode Island's Department of Children, Youth and Families|url=http://www.providencejournal.com/breaking-news/content/20130822-settlement-ends-suit-by-former-ward-alleging-abuse-while-in-care-of-rhode-islands-department-of-children-youth-and-families.ece|access-date=May 10, 2015|agency=The Providence Journal|date=August 22, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150106141456/http://www.providencejournal.com/breaking-news/content/20130822-settlement-ends-suit-by-former-ward-alleging-abuse-while-in-care-of-rhode-islands-department-of-children-youth-and-families.ece|archive-date=January 6, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> Rossi also agreed to dismiss two other lawsuits he had filed, one which accused DCYF of violating a confidentiality agreement, and another against state sheriffs.<ref name="Arditi1" />

He made his World Cup debut in November [[2017–18 FIS Alpine Ski World Cup|2017]] at [[Lake Louise Ski Resort|Lake Louise]], [[Alberta]]. At his first [[FIS Alpine World Ski Championships|World Championships]] in [[FIS Alpine World Ski Championships 2021|2021]], Seger was fourth in the [[FIS Alpine World Ski Championships 2021 – Men's super-G|super-G]] at [[Cortina d'Ampezzo]], Italy.{{cite news|url=https://www.fis-ski.com/DB/general/athlete-biography.html?sectorcode=al&competitorid=164059&type=result|title=SAGER Brodie - Athlete Information|publisher=fis-ski.com|accessdate=12 February 2021}} In January 2022, Seger was named to [[Canada at the 2022 Winter Olympics|Canada's 2022 Olympic team]].{{cite web|url=https://olympic.ca/2022/01/21/13-alpine-skiers-and-eight-ski-cross-racers-nominated-to-team-canada-for-beijing-2022/|title=13 alpine skiers and eight ski cross racers nominated to Team Canada for Beijing 2022|last=Nichols|first=Paula|date=21 January 2022|website=olympic.ca|publisher=[[Canadian Olympic Committee]]|access-date=21 January 2022}}{{cite web|url=https://alpinecanada.org/news/21-alpine-skiing-and-ski-cross-athletes-nominated-to-compete-beijing-2022|title=21 Alpine Skiing and Ski Cross Athletes Nominated to Compete at Beijing 2022 |date=21 January 2022|website=alpinecanada.org|publisher=[[Alpine Canada]]|access-date=21 January 2022}} ==World Cup results== ===Season standings=== {| class="wikitable" style="font-size:95%; text-align:center;" width="40%" |- style="background-color:#369; color:white;" | rowspan="2" colspan="1" width="5%"| '''Season''' |- style="background-color:#4180be; color:white;" | width="3%"| Age | width="5%"| '''Overall''' | width="5%"| Slalom | width="5%"| Giant

{{Short description|Japanese manga artist (born 1992)}} {{Use mdy dates|date=October 2022}} {{Infobox comics creator | name_nonEN = 芥見下々 | nonUS = ja | bodyclass = | birth_name = Gege Akutami | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1992|2|26}} | birth_place = [[Iwate Prefecture]], Japan | nationality = Japanese | area = [[Manga artist]] | cartoonist = | write = | pencil = | ink = | edit = | publish = | letter = | color = | alias = | signature = | notable works = ''[[Jujutsu Kaisen]]'' | collaborators = | awards = | module = | website = | subcat = |manga artist = y }} {{nihongo|'''Gege Akutami'''|芥見下々|Akutami Gege|born February 26, 1992|lead=yes}} is a Japanese [[manga artist]] known for the [[manga]] series ''[[Jujutsu Kaisen]]''. == Biography == Gege Akutami was born in [[Iwate Prefecture]],{{cite web|script-title=ja:「呪術廻戦」作者・芥見下々氏はどんな人？性別や影響を受けた作品を解説|url=https://times.abema.tv/articles/-/10001390|website=[[AbemaTV|Abema Times]]|access-date=November 28, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210928113732/https://times.abema.tv/articles/-/10001390|archive-date=September 28, 2021|language=ja|date=September 28, 2021|url-status=live}} afterwards he moved to [[Sendai]] in [[Miyagi Prefecture]] in fifth grade. Akutami began drawing manga by mimicking a friend, which inspired him to become a professional manga artist.{{Cite web|script-title=ja:呪術廻戦 公式ファンブック / 芥見 下々 {{!}} 集英社の本 公式|url=https://books.shueisha.co.jp/items/contents.html?isbn=978-4-08-882636-3|access-date=April 1, 2021|website=集英社の本 {{!}} コミックス～書籍～雑誌の公式情報と試し読み|archive-date=January 23, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220123063145/https://books.shueisha.co.jp/items/contents.html?isbn=978-4-08-882636-3|url-status=live}}{{Cite web|last=says|first=Booka|date=March 15, 2021|title=Gege Akutami x Tite Kubo Special Talk|url=https://edomonogatari.wordpress.com/2021/03/14/akutami-kubo/|access-date=April 1, 2021|website=Edomonogatari|language=en|archive-date=June 20, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230620140618/https://edomonogatari.wordpress.com/2021/03/14/akutami-kubo/|url-status=live}} Akutami has named [[Tite Kubo]] as an influence in his work after reading ''[[Bleach (manga)|Bleach]]'' in fourth grade, in addition to ''[[Hunter × Hunter]]'' and ''[[Neon Genesis Evangelion (manga)|Neon Genesis Evangelion]]'' among other works. In 2014, Gege Akutami started working as an assistant to [[Yasuhiro Kanō]] in ''Kiss x Death''.{{cite web|last=Lachasse|first=Jérôme|title=Jujutsu Kaisen: ce qu'il faut savoir sur le nouveau manga événement|url=https://www.bfmtv.com/culture/jujutsu-kaisen-ce-qu-il-faut-savoir-sur-le-nouveau-manga-evenement_AN-202003080127.html|publisher=[[BFM TV]]|access-date=October 22, 2020|archive-url=https://archive.today/20201022040219/https://www.bfmtv.com/culture/jujutsu-kaisen-ce-qu-il-faut-savoir-sur-le-nouveau-manga-evenement_AN-202003080127.html|archive-date=October 22, 2020|language=fr|date=June 6, 2020|url-status=live}} He published his first work the same year, titled {{nihongo|"Kamishiro Sōsa"|神代捜査}}, a one-shot chapter published in [[Shueisha]]'s ''Jump NEXT!'' vol. 2 on May 7, 2014.{{cite web|script-title=ja:少年ジャンプNEXT!! 2014 vol.2|url=http://www.shonenjump.com/j/weeklyshonenjump/wj_next.html|website=shonenjump.com|publisher=[[Shueisha]]|access-date=October 22, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140614041135/http://www.shonenjump.com/j/weeklyshonenjump/wj_next.html|archive-date=June 14, 2014|language=ja}}{{cite web|script-title=ja:少年ジャンプNEXT! Vol.2 2014年6/1号|url=https://www.neowing.co.jp/product/NEOBK-1657893|website=Neowing|access-date=October 22, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200111025748/https://www.neowing.co.jp/product/NEOBK-1657893|archive-date=January 11, 2020|language=ja|url-status=live}} His next work was ''No.9'', with a one-shot chapter published in ''Jump NEXT!'' vol. 2 on May 1, 2015,{{cite web|script-title=ja:ジャンプNEXT!!2015 Vol.2 2015年6月号|url=https://www.neowing.co.jp/product/NEOBK-1804739|website=Neowing|access-date=October 22, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201022030332/https://www.neowing.co.jp/product/NEOBK-1804739|archive-date=October 22, 2020|language=ja|url-status=live}} and another one-shot in the 46th issue of ''[[Weekly Shōnen Jump]]'' on October 10, 2015.{{cite web|script-title=ja:週刊少年ジャンプ 2015年10/26号|url=https://www.neowing.co.jp/product/NEOBK-1866149|website=Neowing|access-date=October 22, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190430171916/https://www.neowing.co.jp/product/NEOBK-1866149|archive-date=April 30, 2019|language=ja|url-status=live}} Akutami would publish the one-shot {{nihongo|"Nikai Bongai Barabarjura"|二界梵骸バラバルジュラ}} in the 2016 44th issue of ''Weekly Shōnen Jump'', released on October 3, 2016. This one-shot was nominated for the 11th "Gold Future Cup" contest of the magazine.{{cite web|last=Hodgkins|first=Crystalyn|title=Shonen Jump Magazine Launches 11th 'Gold Future Cup' Contest|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2016-08-29/shonen-jump-magazine-launches-11th-gold-future-cup-contest/.105845|website=[[Anime News Network]]|access-date=October 22, 2020|date=August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170501073613/http://www.shonenjump.com/j/jumpgiga/index.html|archive-date=May 1, 2017|language=ja |date=November 17, 2015 }}{{cite served as a prologue to his next work, ''[[Jujutsu Kaisen]]'', being retroactively titled as ''Jujutsu Kaisen 0''.{{cite web|script-title=ja:呪術廻戦 0 東京都立呪術高等専門学校|url=https://books.shueisha.co.jp/items/contents.html?isbn=978-4-08-881672-2|publisher=[[Shueisha]]|access-date=December 9, began the publication of ''Jujutsu Kaisen'' in the 2018 14th issue of ''Weekly Shōnen Jump'', released on March 5, 2018.{{cite 1, 2019|archive-date=July 21, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190721161257/https://natalie.mu/comic/news/272211|url-status=live}} The series ended in the 44th issue of ''Weekly Shōnen '''Andrés Steven Rodríguez Ossa''' (born 13 October 1998), better known as '''Steven Rodríguez''' or '''Tití Rodríguez''', is a [[Colombian people|Colombian]] professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Striker (association football)|striker]] for [[Categoría Primera A]] club [[Deportivo Cali]], on loan from [[Atlético Junior|Junior]].

==Career==

===Independiente Medellín===
Rodríguez began his football youth with Under-20 squad, in which he always stood out as a scorer in tournaments such as the National Under-20 Tournament and Antioquia League.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://capsulas.com.co/hablando-de-goleadores-andres-stiven-rodriguez-dim-2/|title=Hablando de goleadores, Andrés Steven Rodriguez (DIM) |publisher=capsulas.com.co |date=13 March 2017 |df= dmy-all}}</ref> In mid 2019 season, due to his outstanding performances in the youth team, he was promoted to the first team squad.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.futbolred.com/futbol-colombiano/liga-aguila/medellin-presento-refuerzos-para-el-2019-siete-nuevas-caras-92684 |title=Steven Rodríguez, el ‘tití’ quiere pasar de promesa a realidad |publisher= www.futbolred.com |date=29 January 2019 |df= dmy-all}}</ref> He made his professional debut with the first team of Independiente Medellín on January 29, 2019, in the [[Categoría Primera A]] match against [[La Equidad]] under the manager [[Octavio Zambrano]] in a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.minuto30.com/el-juvenil-stiven-rodriguez-buscara-ante-patriotas-iniciar-con-pie-derecho-en-la-primera-division/769135/|title=El juvenil Steven Rodríguez buscará iniciar con pie derecho en la primera división |publisher= www.minuto30.com |date=25 January 2019 |df= dmy-all}}</ref>

===Leones===
On 15 January 2021 he was loaned to [[Leones F.C. (Colombia)|Leones]] to play the first season of the [[Categoría Primera B]] where he had an excellent performance being the tournament's top scorer with 16 goals in 19 matches.

===Envigado===
On 10 July 2021 he signed for [[Envigado F.C.|Envigado]] on loan until the end of 2021 season. He played a total of 15 matches and scored two goals for the club.

===Sri Pahang===
He continued his loan spell to join [[Malaysia Super League]] side [[Pahang FA|Sri Pahang FC]] on 29 May 2022 on a six-month loan deal.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.vocketfc.com/steven-rodriguez-tak-sabar-sarung-jersi-sri-pahang/ |title=Steven Rodríguez tak sabar sarung jersi Sri Pahang |publisher= www.vocketfc.com |date=31 May 2022 |df= dmy-all}}</ref> He scored his first goal with the club in a 2–5 defeat against [[Penang FA|Penang FC]] in the FA cup quarter finals.<ref>{{Cite news |url= https://www.bharian.com.my/sukan/bola/2022/07/979628/penang-bangkit-belasah-sri-pahang |title= Penang bangkit belasah Sri Pahang |publisher= Berita Harian |date= 23 July 2022 |df= dmy-all}}</ref> His first league goal for the club saw him scoring a solo-run goal in a 2–0 victory against long-term rival [[Selangor FA|Selangor FC]].<ref>{{Cite news |url= https://www.hmetro.com.my/arena/bola-sepak/2022/07/865738/sri-pahang-benam-selangor |title= Sri Pahang benam Selangor |publisher= Harian Metro |date= 27 July 2022 |df= dmy-all}}</ref> At the end of the season he scored a total of 12 goals in 17 appearances.

===Alianza Petrolera===
In January 2023 he returned to his home country to join [[Alianza Petrolera F.C.|Alianza Petrolera]] on a season-long loan deal. On 14 May 2023, he scored a penalty in a 2–1 victory against [[Atlético Nacional]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 May 2023 |title=Alianza Petrolera 2-1 Atlético Nacional |url=https://espndeportes.espn.com/futbol/partido/_/juegoId/662456 |access-date=2023-12-17 |website=ESPN DEPORTES |language=en}}</ref>

'''Mohammad Phaim Bhuiyan''' ({{langx|bn|{{nq|ফাহিম ভূঁইয়া}}}}, {{IPA|bn|ˈfa(h)im ˈbʱũ(i)e̯a|pron}}; born 31 October 1995) is an Italian actor, producer and filmmaker.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.repubblica.it/spettacoli/cinema/2021/11/27/news/bangla_la_serie-328085026/|title=Al Torino Film Festival la serie 'Bangla', dal film di Phaim Bhuiyan: "Risate e conflitti della seconda generazione"|date=27 November 2021|website=[[La Repubblica]]|language=it|access-date=14 May 2025}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Bhuiyan was born in [[Rome]] from parents of [[Bangladeshi]] origin and grew up in the [[Tor Pignattara|Torpignattara district]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.repubblica.it/venerdi/2022/04/01/news/bangla_la_serie_intervista_a_phaim_bhuiyan-342816987/|title=Phaim Bhuiyan: "Sono il Moretti della periferia ma sempre in stile Bangla"|date=1 April 2022|website=[[la Repubblica]]}}</ref>
He attended IPS Virginia Woolf high-school in [[Via Casilina|Circonvallazione Casilina]], Rome.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=29 September 2019|author=Stefania Ulivi|date=5 October 2019|title=La storia di Phaim Bhuiyan, romano di Torpignattara|url=https://roma.corriere.it/notizie/cronaca/19_maggio_10/storia-phaim-bhuiyan-romano-torpignattara-e81fcdca-7284-11e9-861b-d938f88a2d19.shtml|website=[[Corriere della Sera]]}}</ref>
After high school, he attended [[Istituto Europeo di Design]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ilmanifesto.it/phaim-bhuiyan-se-ti-bollano-come-straniero-e-non-lo-sei-rischi-di-crederci|title=Phaim Bhuiyan: "Se ti bollano come straniero e non lo sei, rischi di crederci"|website=[[Il Manifesto]]|date=10 July 2022}}</ref> with a scholarship.

== Career ==
Bhuiyan directed, produced, written and acted on the film ''[[Bangla (2019 film)|Bangla]]'' which was awarded the [[Globo d'oro]]<ref>{{cite web|access-date=14 May 2025|language=en|title=Bangladeshi-Italian director shines light on minority community|url=https://www.aljazeera.com/features/2019/6/26/bangladeshi-italian-director-shines-light-on-minority-community|date=26 June 2019|website=[[Aljazeera]]}}</ref> as best first work with the [[Nastro d'argento]] for the best comedy of the 2019.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=14 May 2025|date=1 April 2022|title=Phaim Bhuiyan: "Sono il Moretti della periferia ma sempre in stile Bangla"|url=https://www.repubblica.it/venerdi/2022/04/01/news/bangla_la_serie_intervista_a_phaim_bhuiyan-342816987/|website=[[La Repubblica]]}}</ref> The same year he participated in the episodes of the program "''Viva RaiPlay!''" hosted by [[Rosario Fiorello]].<ref>{{cite web|access-date=3 December 2020|date=29 December 2019|title=Fiorello: "VivaRaiPlay? Sigarette e vino per convincere Venditti e De Gregori"|url=https://www.corriere.it/spettacoli/19_dicembre_29/rivoluzionefiorello-988f2856-2985-11ea-a8f0-127c1f8f40cd.shtml|website=Corriere della Sera}}</ref>

On 8 May 2020 he won the [[65th David di Donatello|David di Donatello]] in the best new director category.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|access-date=14 May 2025|title=Bangla, la trama del film del giovane Phaim Bhuiyan candidato ai David di Donatello 2020|language=it|date=18 February 2020|url=https://tg24.sky.it/spettacolo/cinema/2020/02/18/bangla-film-trama/amp|website=[[SKY TG24]]}}</ref> Same month he directs a music-video call "''Miami a Fregene''" of the singer-songwriter {{Interlanguage link|Avincola|it|Avincola}}.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=3 December 2020|date=25 May 2020|title=AVINCOLA: "Miami a Fregene", il video diretto da Phaim Bhuiyan miglior regista esordiente ai David di Donatello 2020|url=http://meiweb.it/2020/05/25/avincola-miami-a-fregene-il-video-diretto-da-phaim-bhuiyan-miglior-regista-esordiente-ai-david-di-donatello-2020/}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

In 2021 he was included on ''[[Forbes 30 Under 30|Forbes 30 Under 30-Europe 2021: Entertainment]]'' ranking.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=12 April 2021|language=en|title=Mohammed Phaim Bhuiyan|url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/mohammed-phaim-bhuiyan/|website=Forbes}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/30-under-30/2021/europe/entertainment/|title=Forbes 30 Under 30 Europe 2021: Entertainment|website=Forbes}}</ref> Later on he became one of the judges for ''Forbes 30 under 30-Europe 2023: Entertainment''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/30-under-30/2023/europe/entertainment|title=Forbes 30 Under 30 2023: Entertainment|website=Forbes}}</ref>

On 13 April 2022, ''[[Bangla - La serie]]'' was released, directed by Bhuiyan and Emanuele Scaringi, a sequel to his 2019 film.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.repubblica.it/serietv/rai/2022/04/15/news/bangla_la_serie-345580298/|title='Bangla - La serie', una periferia di seconda generazione|language=it|date=15 April 2022|website=[[La Repubblica]]|access-date=14 May 2025}}</ref>

{{Short description|Politician from Norway}} {{Infobox officeholder | image = Linn_Kristin_Langley-Engø.jpg | office = [[List of mayors of Bergen|Mayor of Bergen]] | term_start = 27 October 2022 | term_end = 25 October 2023 | deputy = Eira Garrido | 1blankname = Chief Commissioner | 1namedata = [[Roger Valhammer]]
[[Rune Bakervik]] | predecessor = Rune Bakervik | successor = Marit Warncke | office2 = Deputy Mayor of Bergen | term_start2 = 22 September 2021 | term_end2 = 27 October 2022 | 2blankname2 = Mayor | 2namedata2 = Rune Bakervik | predecessor2 = Rune Bakervik | successor2 = Eira Garrido | office3 = Bergen City Commissioner for Schools, Kindergartens and Sports | term_start3 = 25 April 2019 | term_end3 = 27 January 2020 | 3blankname3 = Chief Commissioner | 3namedata3 = Roger Valhammer | predecessor3 = Roger Valhammer | successor3 = Endre Tvinnereim | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1993|09|20|df=y}} | birth_place = [[Bergen]], Hordaland, Norway | party = [[Labour Party (Norway)|Labour]] | education = [[University of Bergen]] }} '''Linn Kristin Langley-Rasmussen Engø''' (born 20 September 1993) is a Norwegian politician for the [[Labour Party (Norway)|Labour Party]]. She has served in several posts in Bergen, notably as the city commissioner for schools, kindergartens and sports between 2019 and 2020, and subsequently deputy mayor and then mayor. ==Background== Engø grew up in the area of [[Flaktveit]] in the borough of [[Åsane]] in Bergen. She attended [[Bergen Cathedral School]] between 2009 and 2012.{{cite web | url= https://www.ba.no/nyheter/politikk/byradet/linn-kristin-engo-25-er-ny-skolebyrad-selv-strok-hun-i-teoretisk-matte-pa-katten/s/5-8-1038588 | title= (+) Linn Kristin Engø (25) er ny skolebyråd. Selv strøk hun i teoretisk matte på Katten. | date= 27 April 2019 | access-date= 9 May 2019 | language= no | archive-date= 9 May 2019 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20190509133309/https://www.ba.no/nyheter/politikk/byradet/linn-kristin-engo-25-er-ny-skolebyrad-selv-strok-hun-i-teoretisk-matte-pa-katten/s/5-8-1038588 | url-status= live }} She has a bachelor's degree in history with specialization in Middle Eastern history from the [[University of Bergen]], and a started master's degree in democracy building. Engø has working experience as an assistant nurse, shop assistant and freelance journalist. {{cite web |url= https://www.bergen.kommune.no/bk/multimedia/archive/00348/CV_-_Linn_Kristin_E_348397a.pdf |title= Curriculum vitae – Linn Kristin Langley-Rasmussen Engø |access-date= 9 May 2019 |date= |publisher= Bergen kommune |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20190509133259/https://www.bergen.kommune.no/bk/multimedia/archive/00348/CV_-_Linn_Kristin_E_348397a.pdf |archive-date= 9 May 2019 |url-status=dead }} ==Political career== ===Youth league=== Engø joined the [[Workers' Youth League (Norway)|Workers' Youth League]] at a young age. At only the age of 17, she became acting leader for the Hordaland Workers' Youth League following Tore Eikeland's death at [[Utøya]] during the [[2011 Norway attacks]].{{cite web | url = https://www.nrk.no/hordaland/hun-skal-fore-hordaland-auf-videre-1.7747197 | title = Hun skal føre Hordaland AUF videre | publisher = [[NRK]] Hordaland | date = 12 August 2011 | access-date = 9 May 2019 | language = no | archive-date = 29 October 2023 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20231029032225/https://www.nrk.no/vestland/hun-skal-fore-hordaland-auf-videre-1.7747197 | url-status = live}} ===Local politics=== Between 2011 and 2015, Engø was a deputy representative in the Bergen City Council. She was elected as a regular representative in 2015 and was re-elected in 2019.{{cite web |url= https://www.bergen.kommune.no/politikk/valg/7449/article-89298 |title= Valgresultat for kommunestyrevalget 2011 |access-date= 9 May 2019 |date= | publisher= Bergen kommune |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20190509124845/https://www.bergen.kommune.no/politikk/valg/7449/article-89298 |archive-date= 9 May 2019 | url-status=dead}}{{cite web |url= https://www.bergen.kommune.no/politikk/valg/7449/article-129551 |title= Bystyret 2015-2019 |access-date= 9 May 2019 |date= | publisher= Bergen kommune |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20190509124832/https://www.bergen.kommune.no/politikk/valg/7449/article-129551 |archive-date= 9 May 2019 | url-status=dead}}{{cite web |url= https://www.bergen.kommune.no/politikk/valg/7449/article-162685 |title= Slik blir det nye bystyret |access-date= 13 January 2020 |date= | publisher= Bergen kommune |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20200113233319/https://www.bergen.kommune.no/politikk/valg/7449/article-162685 |archive-date= 13 January 2020 | url-status=dead}} During Harald Schjelderup's tenure as chief commissioner between 2015 and 2019, Engø served as a political advisor to city commissioner Pål Håfstad Thorsen, who was responsible for education. She then went onto serve as an advisor for Schjelderup. ===City commissioner=== On 25 April 2019, when Roger Valhammer took over as chief commissioner from Harald Schjelderup, he appointed Engø as city commissioner for schools, kindergartens and sports.{{cite web | url = https://www.nrk.no/vestland/roger-valhammer-tek-over-for-harald-schjelderup-som-byradsleiar-i-bergen-1.14526965 | title = Her er Bergen sin nye byrådsleiar | publisher = [[NRK]] Vestland | date = 25 April 2019 | access-date = 28 October 2023 | language = nn | archive-date = 7 November 2020 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20201107233007/https://www.nrk.no/vestland/roger-valhammer-tek-over-for-harald-schjelderup-som-byradsleiar-i-bergen-1.14526965 | url-status = live}} Engø resigned as city commissioner on 27 January 2020 following a scandal involving security breaches in a school app, Vigilo, which was used as a communications app between school staff and parents to children in both school and kindergartens. There had been a majority in the city council for a confidence vote against her in the leadup to her resignation.{{cite web | url = https://www.nrk.no/vestland/skulebyraden-i-bergen-gar-av-1.14878547 | title = Skulebyråden i Bergen går av | publisher = [[NRK]] Vestland | date = 27 January 2020 | access-date = 28 October 2023 | language = nn | archive-date = 26 February 2022 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20220226034629/https://www.nrk.no/vestland/skulebyraden-i-bergen-gar-av-1.14878547 | url-status = live }} Valhammer named Endre Tvinnereim as her successor on 6 February.{{cite news | url = https://www.bt.no/nyheter/lokalt/i/g7ObBL/han-blir-ny-skolebyraad | title = Klimaforsker og byluftforkjemper blir ny skolebyråd | publisher = [[Bergens Tidende]] | date = 6 February 2020 | access-date = 28 October 2023 | language = no | archive-date = 6 February 2020 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200206101812/https://www.bt.no/nyheter/lokalt/i/g7ObBL/han-blir-ny-skolebyraad | url-status = live}} ===Deputy mayor=== With then-mayor [[Marte Mjøs Persen]] nominated as a candidate for parliament ahead of the [[2021 Norwegian parliamentary election|2021 parliamentary election]], the Bergen Labour Party chose Rune Bakervik as their new mayoral candidate along with Engø as the deputy mayor candidate.{{cite web | url = https://www.bt.no/nyheter/lokalt/i/M3l27r/rune-bakervik-blir-ny-ordfoerer-i-bergen | title = Rune Bakervik blir ny ordfører i Bergen | publisher = [[Bergens Tidende]] | date = 23 April 2021 | access-date = 15 March 2022 | language = no | archive-date = 27 January 2022 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20220127200531/https://www.bt.no/nyheter/lokalt/i/M3l27r/rune-bakervik-blir-ny-ordfoerer-i-bergen | url-status = live }} Both Bakervik and Engø officially assumed office on 22 September after Persen resigned as mayor after being elected to parliament.{{cite web | url = https://www.nrk.no/vestland/ny-ordforer-i-bergen--1.15662522 | title = Ny ordfører i Bergen | publisher = [[NRK]] Vestland | date = 22 September 2021 | access-date = 28 October 2023 | language = no | archive-date = 24 November 2022 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20221124103723/https://www.nrk.no/vestland/ny-ordforer-i-bergen--1.15662522 | url-status = live }} As deputy mayor, she notably had to step in to consider new chief commissioner candidates in Bakervik's place following Valhammer's resignation. Bakervik handed her the responsibility because he was among the preferred candidates up for consideration.{{cite web | url = https://www.dagsavisen.no/nyheter/innenriks/2022/10/10/bergensordforer-rune-bakervik-trer-til-side-i-byradsprosessen/ | title = Bergensordfører Rune Bakervik trer til side i byrådsprosessen | publisher = [[Dagsavisen]] | date = 10 October 2022 | access-date = 28 October 2023 | archive-date = 17 October 2022 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20221017055600/https://www.dagsavisen.no/nyheter/innenriks/2022/10/10/bergensordforer-rune-bakervik-trer-til-side-i-byradsprosessen/ | url-status = live }} ===Mayor of Bergen=== Engø would later give Bakervik the responsibility of forming a new city government. She then ascended to the mayoralty when he resigned on 27 October in preparation to take over as chief commissioner. Bakervik officially took over on 3 November.{{cite web | url = https://www.nrk.no/vestland/arbeidarpartiet-og-venstre-dannar-byrad-i-bergen-1.16164626 | title = Visesongar blir kulturbyråd i Bergen | publisher = [[NRK]] Vestland | date = 3 November 2022 | access-date = 28 October 2023 | language = nn | archive-date = 4 October 2023 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20231004030110/https://www.nrk.no/vestland/arbeidarpartiet-og-venstre-dannar-byrad-i-bergen-1.16164626 | url-status = live }} Eira Garrido from the [[Socialist Left Party (Norway)|Socialist Left Party]] was confirmed as Engø's deputy mayor in December.{{cite web | url = https://www.kommunal-rapport.no/article/148207!/ | title = (+) Nå har Bergen fått to unge kvinner på topp | publisher = [[Kommunal Rapport]] | date = 16 December 2022 | access-date = 14 May 2023 | language = no | archive-date = 29 October 2023 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20231029032226/https://www.kommunal-rapport.no/politikk/na-har-bergen-fatt-to-unge-kvinner-pa-topp/148207!/ | url-status = live }} Engø had sought a term in her own right in the [[2023 Norwegian local elections|2023 local elections]], but ultimately lost to the [[Conservative Party (Norway)|Conservatives]]' Marit Warncke, who succeeded her on 25 October. For some time since the election until Warncke's takeover, Engø was on leave, and Garrido officially oversaw the transference in her place.{{cite web | url = https://www.nrk.no/vestland/her-blir-bergens-nye-ordforer-formelt-valgt_-men-et-nytt-byrad-er-enna-ikke-satt-1.16610002 | title = Her blir Bergens nye ordfører formelt valgt, men et nytt byråd er ennå ikke satt | publisher = [[NRK]] Vestland | date = 25 October 2023 | access-date = 25 October 2023 | language = no | archive-date = 25 October 2023 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20231025151430/https://www.nrk.no/vestland/her-blir-bergens-nye-ordforer-formelt-valgt_-men-et-nytt-byrad-er-enna-ikke-satt-1.16610002 | url-status = live }} ==References== {{reflist}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Engo, Linn}} [[Category:1993 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:People from Bergen]] [[Category:Politicians from Vestland]] [[Category:Labour Party (Norway) politicians]] [[Category:University of Bergen alumni]] [[Category:Women mayors of places in Norway]] [[Category:21st-century Norwegian women politicians]] [[Category:21st-century Norwegian politicians]]

At his mother’s suggestion, he took up climbing, as she believed it suited his abilities. He had enjoyed climbing trees from a young age and began training in climbing gyms at age 14.{{cite web |title=Six Japanese national team players gathered for a Q&A session (translated) |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cN0e4WW0ClE&t=257s |website=TAMY Climbing Channel on YouTube |access-date=12 January 2026}} ==Climbing career== === Competition climbing === In June 2018, Fujiwaki clinched a Silver in the Bouldering and Bronze in the Combined discipline at the [[FISU]] University Championships in [[Bratislava]].{{cite web|url=https://www.fisu.net/events/2018-fisu-world-university-championships-climbing/|title=2018 FISU World University Championships Sport Climbing|access-date=August 28, 2025|publisher=FISU}} In August 2018, Fujiwaki placed fifth in his first [[2018 IFSC Climbing World Cup|IFSC Bouldering World Cup]] final in [[Munich]].{{cite web|url=https://www.ukclimbing.com/news/2018/08/ifsc_boulder_world_cup_munich_-_report-71681|title=IFSC Boulder World Cup: Munich - Report |publisher=UKClimbing |access-date=28 August 2025 |date=20 August 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://ifsc.results.info/event/1057/cr/5005|title=IFSC Climbing Worldcup (B) - Munich (GER) 2018|access-date=August 28, 2025|publisher=IFSC}} Fujiwaki won the [[IFSC Climbing Asian Cup]] in bouldering in 2022.{{cite web|url=https://ifsc.results.info/event/1315/cr/7851|title=IFSC Asia - Continental Cup (B) - Manila (PHI) 2022|access-date=August 28, 2025|publisher=IFSC}} In 2025, Fujiwaki finished second at the [[Climbing Japan Cup|Boulder Japan Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://www.climbers-web.jp/news/20250202-4/|title=18歳の安楽宙斗が男子最年少V【ボルダージャパンカップ2025|access-date=August 28, 2025|publisher=climbers-web.jp}} During the [[2025 IFSC Climbing World Cup|2025 Boulder World Cup season]], he reached the finals in two out of the three events he competed in, marking his return to the [[Bouldering at the 2025 IFSC Climbing World Cup|Bouldering World Cup]] finals after a seven-year absence. He placed fifth and seventh in [[Curitiba]] and [[Salt Lake City]] respectively.{{cite web|url=https://www.olympics.com/en/news/2025-ifsc-world-cup-sport-climbing-curitiba-anraku-sorato-continues-glittering-start-season-boulder-triumph|title=2025 IFSC World Cup Sport Climbing Curitiba: Anraku Sorato continues glittering start to season with decisive boulder triumph|access-date=August 28, 2025|publisher=Olympics}}{{cite web|url=https://gripped.com/news/climber-wins-three-world-cups-in-a-row/|title=Climber Wins Three World Cups in a Row|access-date=August 28, 2025|publisher=Gripped Magazine}} He ended the season in tenth place at his first [[2025 IFSC Climbing World Championships|World Championships]] in [[Seoul]].{{cite web|url=https://www.worldclimbing.com/events/ifsc-climbing-world-championships-seoul-2025/results/index?discipline=boulder&category=men|title=IFSC Climbing World Championships Seoul 2025 - Boulder Men Semi-final |access-date=January 12, 2026|publisher=IFSC}}{{cite web |title=安楽宙斗が激戦を制してボルダー世界王者に輝く　最高峰の舞台で光った“決定力”【クライミング世界選手権2025】 |url=https://www.climbers-web.jp/news/20250928-3/ |publisher=climbers-web.jp |access-date=January 12, 2026 |language=Japanese}} == Rankings == === [[IFSC Climbing World Championships|World Championships]]=== {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: center;" ! style="background: #b0e0e6;" | Discipline ! style="background: #b0e0e6" | [[2025 IFSC Climbing World Championships|Seoul

'''Shaun Maguire''' (born 1985)<ref name=heritage /> is an American [[venture capitalist]] and political activist who is a partner at [[Sequoia Capital]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last1=Schleifer |first1=Theodore |last2=Haberman |first2=Maggie |last3=Swan |first3=Jonathan |date=2024-12-07 |title=The Silicon Valley Billionaires Steering Trump's Transition |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/12/06/us/politics/trump-elon-musk-silicon-valley.html |access-date=2025-07-06 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref name="auto1">{{Cite web |last=Tiffany |first=Kaitlyn |date=2024-10-15 |title=What's With All the Trumpy VCs? |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/technology/archive/2024/10/silicon-valley-venture-capitalists-trump/680225/ |access-date=2025-07-06 |website=The Atlantic |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Shaun Maguire |url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/shaun-maguire/ |access-date=2025-07-06 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref> Before joining Sequoia in 2019, he was a partner at [[GV (company)|GV]] and co-founded the cybersecurity company Expanse, which was acquired by Palo Alto Networks in 2020.

== Early life and education ==
In an interview with the [[California Institute of Technology|Caltech]] Heritage Project, Maguire reported that he earned a 1.8 GPA in high school and failed his Algebra 2 course, and that his admission to [[Stanford University]] depended on letters of recommendation.<ref name=heritage>{{Cite web |date=2023-01-04 |title=Shaun Maguire (PhD '18), Quantum Researcher and Venture Capitalist |url=http://heritageproject.caltech.edu/interviews-updates/shaun-maguire |access-date=2025-07-08 |website=Heritage Project |language=en}}</ref>  Maguire received his PhD in physics from [[California Institute of Technology|Caltech]].<ref name=":0" /> In 2018, Maguire married his [[Iranian Jews|Iranian Jewish]] wife in Israel and subsequently added Cohn as his last name.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=How Sequoia's Shaun Maguire became Silicon Valley's most MAGA firebrand|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/shaun-maguire-silicon-valleys-most-maga-firebrand-sequoia-mamdani-2025-7|website=Business Insider|access-date=2025-12-01|language=en-US|first=Jacob|last=Silverman}}</ref> 

== Career ==
In 2010, Maguire cofounded [[Escape Dynamics]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=MacColl |first=Margaux |date=May 10, 2024 |title=The Musk Whisperer |url=https://www.theinformation.com/articles/the-musk-whisperer |access-date=2026-03-07 |website=The Information |language=en |quote="While still working on his doctorate, Maguire joined a team of Caltech scientists to found Escape Dynamics in 2010."}}</ref> He later worked at [[DARPA]], including a deployment to Afghanistan as a civilian contractor.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Silverman |first=Jacob |date=2025-07-22 |title=The metamorphosis of Shaun Maguire |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/shaun-maguire-silicon-valleys-most-maga-firebrand-sequoia-mamdani-2025-7 |access-date=2025-10-27 |website=Business Insider |language=en-US|quote="For Maguire, who worked on a DARPA (Defense Advance Research Projects Agency) program as a civilian contractor in Afghanistan, the conflict is between radical Islam and the West — a rhetorical throwback to the Bush-era war on terror, this time with tech startups churning out drones and surveillance systems. "}}</ref>

In 2012, Maguire co-founded cyber firm Expanse (previously called Qadium), which was acquired by [[Palo Alto Networks]] in 2020 for over $1 billion.<ref name=":2" />

Maguire joined [[Google Ventures]] in 2016, where he worked for three years, before leaving for [[Sequoia Capital]] in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Loizos |first=Connie |date=2025-07-12 |title=Sequoia bets on silence |url=https://techcrunch.com/2025/07/11/sequoia-bets-on-silence/ |access-date=2025-10-27 |website=TechCrunch |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Political activity and controversies ==
Maguire served as an advisor to President [[Donald Trump]] in his second term, assisting with intelligence community picks.<ref name="auto1"/><ref name="auto">{{Cite news |last1=Schleifer |first1=Theodore |last2=Mac |first2=Ryan |last3=Boyce |first3=Lily |last4=Grind |first4=Kirsten |date=2024-12-24 |title=The Men and Women Swirling Around Elon Musk |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2024/12/23/business/elon-musk-trump-family-friends-backers.html |access-date=2025-07-06 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Maguire manages the investments of [[Sequoia Capital]] in [[Elon Musk]]'s companies, including [[SpaceX]], [[The Boring Company]], [[xAI (company)|xAI]], and [[Twitter|X]], and assisted Musk during his tenure at DOGE.<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{Cite web |last=Tecotzky |first=Alice |title=DOGE under Musk unites Trumpworld vets with tech industry giants |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/doge-employees-hire-musk-ramaswamy-2024-12 |access-date=2025-07-06 |website=Business Insider |language=en-US}}</ref> Maguire supported Trump during the 2024 election.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Chernova |first=Yuliya |date=2025-01-21 |title=At Trump's Inauguration, Tech and Venture Cement Their Insider Status |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/at-trumps-inauguration-tech-and-venture-cement-their-insider-status-135b9c6a |access-date=2025-07-06 |work=Wall Street Journal |language=en-US |issn=0099-9660}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last1=Sorkin |first1=Andrew Ross |last2=Mattu |first2=Ravi |last3=Warner |first3=Bernhard |last4=Kessler |first4=Sarah |last5=Merced |first5=Michael J. de la |last6=Hirsch |first6=Lauren |last7=Livni |first7=Ephrat |date=2024-05-31 |title=Why Megadonors Are Unfazed by Donald Trump's Guilty Verdict |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/05/31/business/dealbook/megadonors-donald-trump-guilty-verdict.html |access-date=2025-07-06 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

=== Mamdani comments ===
On July 4, 2025, Maguire posted on X that New York City [[Mayor of New York City|mayoral]] candidate [[Zohran Mamdani]] “...comes from a culture that lies about everything. It's literally a virtue to lie if it advances his Islamist agenda. The West will learn this lesson the hard way."<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1941135110922969168 |user=shaunmmaguire |title=Mamdani comes from a culture that lies about everything  It’s literally a virtue to lie if it advances his Islamist agenda  The West will learn this lesson the hard way |first=Shaun |last=Maguire |date=2025-07-04}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last1=Sorkin |first1=Andrew Ross |last2=Warner |first2=Bernhard |last3=Kessler |first3=Sarah |last4=Merced |first4=Michael J. de la |last5=Kaye |first5=Danielle |date=2025-07-08 |title=A Prominent Investor Is Criticized Over Mamdani Comments |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/07/08/business/dealbook/mamdani-sequoia-maguire.html |access-date=2025-07-09 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Novet |first=Jordan |date=2025-07-07 |title=Tech founders call on Sequoia Capital to denounce VC Shaun Maguire's Mamdani comments |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2025/07/07/founders-sign-letter-to-sequoia-on-shaun-maguires-mamdani-remarks.html |access-date=2025-07-09 |website=CNBC |language=en}}</ref> Maguire's comments were widely criticized as [[racist]] and [[Islamophobic]], including by [[Dilawar Syed]], former deputy administrator of the [[United States Small Business Administration]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/trending/sequoias-shaun-maguire-slammed-for-racist-jibe-at-zohran-mamdani-comes-from-a-culture-that-lies-101751767467601.html|title=Sequoia's Shaun Maguire slammed for racist jibe at Zohran Mamdani: 'Comes from a culture that lies'|date=July 6, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1941565441601830944 |user=dilawar |title=Silicon Valley was built by entrepreneurs of all backgrounds. @sequoia  owes its success to them, including my early team @FreshworksInc .  Disagree with a candidate’s policies, fine. But this attack is Islamophobic. Tech leaders must speak out—we can’t normalize bigotry. |first=Dilawar |last=Syed |date=2025-07-06}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-07-06 |title=Shaun Maguire's racist remarks about Zohran Mamdani ignite social media outrage: 'Comes from a culture that lies' |url=https://www.indiatimes.com/trending/shaun-maguires-racist-remarks-about-zohran-mamdani-ignite-social-media-outrage-comes-from-a-culture-that-lies-662999.html |access-date=2025-07-06 |website=Indiatimes |language=en-IN}}</ref> Saudi entrepreneur Hisham Al-Falih criticized Maguire's comments, describing them as "appalling".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-07-07/sequoia-partner-maguire-s-posts-on-mamdani-spark-founder-petition|title=Sequoia Partner Maguire's Posts on Mamdani Spark Founder Petition|accessdate=Sep 18, 2025}}</ref>

Maguire defended his post on July 7, 2025,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Murray |first=Conor |title=Sequoia VC Shaun Maguire Keeps Pushing Mamdani 'Islamist' Claims |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/conormurray/2025/07/08/sequoias-shaun-maguire-doubles-down-on-mamdani-islamist-comments-despite-furor/ |access-date=2025-07-09 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref> after which a petition signed by 900 tech leaders was circulated calling for Sequoia Capital to apologize for, condemn, and investigate Maguire's comments.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Au-Yeung |first=Angel |title=The Sequoia Investor Whose Anti-Mamdani Posts Set Off a Silicon Valley Storm |url=https://www.wsj.com/tech/the-sequoia-investor-whose-anti-mamdani-posts-set-off-a-silicon-valley-storm-56965cdf |access-date=2025-07-09 |website=WSJ |language=en-US}}</ref> Supporters issued an open letter in defense of Maguire on July 8, 2025.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite news |date=2025-07-09 |first1=Madeline |last1=Berg |first2=Kelsey |last2=Vlamis |first3=Katherine |last3=Li |title=Read the open letter circulating in support of the Sequoia partner who called Zohran Mamdani an 'Islamist' |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/shaun-maguire-letter-of-support-2025-7 |access-date=2025-07-09 |work=Business Insider |language=en-US}}</ref>

In the aftermath of the controversy, Sequoia’s COO Sumaiya Balbale, a practicing Muslim, resigned in August 2025. According to the [[Financial Times|''Financial Times'']], Maguire’s remarks not only strained the firm’s relations with its Middle Eastern investors but were also described by Balbale as "Islamophobic".<ref name="FT2025">{{Cite web |last=Morris |first=Stephen |last2=Hammond |first2=George |last3=Murgia |first3=Madhumita |date=21 October 2025 |title=Sequoia COO quit over Shaun Maguire’s comments about Islamism |url=https://www.ft.com/content/8e6de299-3eb6-4ba9-8037-266c55c02170 |website=Financial Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Holloman |first=Christer |title=Sequoia Capital COO Quits After Partner’s Tweet About Zohran Mamdani |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/christerholloman/2025/10/22/sequoia-capital-coo-quits-after-partners-tweet-about-zohran-mamdani/ |access-date=2025-10-23 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-10-22 |title=Sequoia Capital faces cash flow concerns as COO resigns amid free speech row - CNBC TV18 |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/business/sequoia-capital-faces-cash-flow-concerns-as-coo-resigns-amid-free-speech-row-ws-l-19723508.htm |access-date=2025-10-23 |website=CNBCTV18 |language=en}}</ref> [[Roelof Botha]], Sequoia's former managing partner, defended Maguire's comments in an October 2025 interview with ''[[TechCrunch]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bort |first=Sarah Perez, Julie |date=2025-10-27 |title=Roelof Botha explains why Sequoia supports Shaun Maguire after COO quit |url=https://techcrunch.com/2025/10/27/roelof-botha-explains-why-sequoia-supports-shaun-maguire-after-coo-quit/ |access-date=2025-12-20 |website=TechCrunch |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Garfinkle |first=Allie |title=Roelof Botha steps aside as Sequoia’s steward, passing the role to Alfred Lin and Pat Grady |url=https://fortune.com/2025/11/04/roelof-botha-steps-aside-as-sequoias-steward-passing-the-role-to-alfred-lin-and-pat-grady/ |access-date=2025-12-21 |website=Fortune |language=en}}</ref>

===Brown University shooting===

After the [[2025 Brown University shooting]], Maguire spread a conspiracy theory on social media inaccurately identifying a Palestinian student at [[Brown University]] as the perpetrator.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Loizos |first=Connie |date=2025-12-20 |title=Sequoia partner spreads debunked Brown shooting theory, testing new leadership |url=https://techcrunch.com/2025/12/19/sequoia-partner-spreads-debunked-brown-shooting-theory-testing-new-leadership/ |access-date=2025-12-20 |website=TechCrunch |language=en-US}}</ref> Maguire said there was "very strong evidence" that this student was the shooter, and inaccurately claimed that an [[MIT]] professor who was also killed was targeted because he was Jewish. A different individual, Claudio Manuel Neves Valente, was subsequently identified as the shooter. Maguire then deleted his posts on the shooting.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stokel-Walker|first=Chris|date=2025-12-19 |title=Sequoia’s Shaun Maguire accused an innocent Palestinian of being the Brown shooter. Then he doubled down |url=https://www.fastcompany.com/91463942/sequoia-shaun-maguire-brown-university-shooter-palestine |access-date=2025-12-19 |website=[[Fast Company]]|language=en}}</ref>

On December 19, 2025, [[Council on American–Islamic Relations|Council on American-Islamic Relations]] (CAIR) National Deputy Director Edward Ahmed Mitchell released a statement condemning Maguire, writing "We strongly condemn anti-Muslim, pro-Israel extremists who rushed to blame the recent campus shooting on an innocent Brown University student who is Muslim and an advocate for Palestinian human rights. The remarks that Shaun Maguire and other bigots made about this student were irresponsible, dangerous, and, sadly, predictable."<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-12-19 |title=CAIR Condemns Shaun Maguire, Others Who Smeared and Endangered Innocent Muslim Student at Brown University |url=https://www.cair.com/press_releases/cair-condemns-shaun-maguire-others-who-smeared-and-endangered-innocent-muslim-student-at-brown-university/ |access-date=2025-12-20 |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''David Dudzinski''' (born May 26, 1992) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Saga Ballooners]]. He played [[college basketball]] for [[Holy Cross Crusaders men's basketball|College of the Holy Cross]].

==Early life==
Dudzinski played high school basketball at [[Kaneland High School]]. He twice earned First Team All-Western Sun Conference honors and was selected All-Area by both the Daily Herland and the Kane County Chronicle. He played AAU basketball for Velocity Black.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dave Dudzinski - 2013-14 - Men's Basketball |url=https://goholycross.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/dave-dudzinski/7556 |website=Holy Cross Athletics |access-date=21 October 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

==College career==
In November 2009, he signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play for [[College of the Holy Cross]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Crusaders Sign Three Players To National Letters Of Intent |url=https://goholycross.com/news/2009/11/23/210194234.aspx |website=Holy Cross Athletics |access-date=20 October 2025 |language=en |date=23 November 2009}}</ref>

In February 2011, he was chosen to the All-[[Patriot League]] All-Rookie team after averaging 4.3 points and 2.7 rebounds per game during the 2010–2011 season.
<ref>{{cite web |title=Devin Brown & Andrew Keister Named To All-Patriot League Teams |url=https://goholycross.com/news/2011/2/27/210194429.aspx |website=Holy Cross Athletics |access-date=20 October 2025 |language=en |date=27 February 2011}}</ref> On December 25, 2011, he was named the AT&T Crusader of the Week. He had 20 points and 6 rebounds, hitting the 20-point mark for the third time that season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dave Dudzinski Named AT&T Crusader Of The Week |url=https://goholycross.com/news/2011/12/25/210193756.aspx |website=Holy Cross Athletics |access-date=20 October 2025 |language=en |date=25 December 2011}}</ref>

On June 26, 2012, he earned a spot on the 2011–2012 [[Patriot League]] Academic Honor Roll for the first time.<ref>{{cite web |title=Men's Basketball Places Two Players On Academic Honor Roll |url=https://goholycross.com/news/2012/6/26/210193789.aspx |website=Holy Cross Athletics |access-date=20 October 2025 |language=en |date=26 June 2012}}</ref> On December 26, 2012, he was named the [[Patriot League]] Player of the Week. This was the first time he had won [[Patriot League]] Player of the Week honors. He averaged 26.5 points, 4 rebounds and 2 blocked shots per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dave Dudzinski Named Patriot League Player Of The Week |url=https://goholycross.com/news/2012/12/26/210194005.aspx |website=Holy Cross Athletics |access-date=20 October 2025 |language=en |date=26 December 2012}}</ref> On March 3, 2013, he was selected to the 2012–2013 All-[[Patriot League]] second team in men's basketball. He averaged a team best 15 points and 6.6 rebounds. He finished the regular season ranked fourth in the league in scoring, fourth in rebounding, fourth in free throw percentage, eight in blocked shots and ninth in field goal percentage.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dave Dudzinski Named All-Patriot League |url=https://goholycross.com/news/2013/3/3/210194037.aspx |website=Holy Cross Athletics |access-date=20 October 2025 |language=en |date=3 March 2013}}</ref>

On October 23, 2013, he was selected to the 2013–2014 preseason All-[[Patriot League]] team.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dudzinski Named Preseason All-Patriot League |url=https://goholycross.com/news/2013/10/23/210194409.aspx |website=Holy Cross Athletics |access-date=20 October 2025 |language=en |date=23 October 2013}}</ref> On March 2, 2014, he was selected to the 2013–2014 All-[[Patriot League]] First Team. He averaged a team-best 15.3 points and 7.5 rebounds. He finished the season ranked first in the league in rebounding, third in scoring, 10th in blocked shots and 12th in free throw percentage. He ranked ninth all-time at Holy Cross in career blocked shots, 10th in games started and 20th in points scored.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dudzinski & Miller Named All-Patriot League |url=https://goholycross.com/news/2014/3/2/210194357.aspx |website=Holy Cross Athletics |access-date=20 October 2025 |language=en |date=2 March 2014}}</ref> On March 11, 2014, he was selected to the 2013–2014 [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]] All-District 13 first team.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dudzinski Earns NABC All-District Honors |url=https://goholycross.com/news/2014/3/11/210194407.aspx |website=Holy Cross Athletics |access-date=20 October 2025 |language=en |date=11 March 2014}}</ref>

In May 2014, he was the recipient of the Richard J Maloney Award. This award is presented annually by the Holy Cross Varsity Club to the men's basketball player who best exemplifies Mr. Maloney's spirit and energy as a loyal contributor to the program.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dave Dudzinski Receives Richard J. Maloney Award |url=https://goholycross.com/news/2014/5/4/210194382.aspx |website=Holy Cross Athletics |access-date=20 October 2025 |language=en |date=4 May 2014}}</ref>

In June 2014, he had a pre-draft workout with the [[Boston Celtics]]. He was one of six players at the Celtics' practice facility for the seventh workout ahead of the [[2014 NBA Draft]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Holy Cross' Dave Dudzinski Makes Most Of Celtics Draft Workout |url=https://nesn.com/2014/06/holy-cross-dave-dudzinski-makes-most-of-celtics-draft-workout/ |website=NESN.com |access-date=20 October 2025 |date=16 June 2014}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Fortitudo Agrigento (2014–2015)===
In August 2014, he signed his first professional contract to play basketball with [[Fortitudo Agrigento]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Dudzinski To Begin Professional Career With Fortitudo Agrigento |url=https://goholycross.com/news/2014/8/18/210194177.aspx |website=Holy Cross Athletics |access-date=20 October 2025 |language=en |date=18 August 2014}}</ref>

===Steaua CSM EximBank Bucuresti (2016–2017)===
In June 2018, he signed his third one-year contract to play for [[CSA Steaua București (basketball)|Steaua CSM]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Armstrong: Kaneland grad David Dudzinski climbing basketball ladder in Europe |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2016/06/24/armstrong-kaneland-grad-david-dudzinski-climbing-basketball-ladder-in-europe/ |website=Chicago Tribune |access-date=20 October 2025 |date=24 June 2016}}</ref>

===Telenet Giants Antwerp (2017–2021)===
In March 2020, his season ended early due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. He was team captain of the [[Antwerp Giants]] from 2019 to 2020. During his time with the team, they won the [[Belgian Basketball Cup]] for the first time in 12 years. The 2019–2020 season he became the first player in BCL history to record a game with 20 or more points and rebounds when he had 21 points and 22 rebounds.<ref>{{cite web |title=A season cut short: Kaneland product David Dudzinski a veteran of professional basketball in Europe with Belgium's Antwerp Giants |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2020/04/09/a-season-cut-short-kaneland-product-david-dudzinski-a-veteran-of-professional-basketball-in-europe-with-belgiums-antwerp-giants/ |website=Chicago Tribune |access-date=20 October 2025 |date=9 April 2020}}</ref>

===Frutti Extra Bursapor (2021–2023)===
On May 1, 2022, he was signed to a contract extension for the next two seasons. He was one of the leaders of the team that season scoring an average of 11.3 points per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bursaspor signs Derek Needham, David Dudzinski to contract extensions |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/eurocup/1339979/bursaspor-signs-derek-needham-david-dudzinski-to-contract-extensions/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=20 October 2025 |language=en |date=1 May 2022}}</ref>

On November 24, 2022, he earned Most Valuable Player after having a career-best performance that led his team to a road win. He had 30 points, 10 rebounds and 2 assists.<ref>{{cite web |title=EuroCup Round 5 MVP: David Dudzinski |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/eurocup/1424173/round-5-mvp-david-dudzinski/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=20 October 2025 |language=en |date=24 November 2022}}</ref>

===San-en NeoPhoenix (2023–2025)===
In June 2023, he signed with [[San-en NeoPhoenix]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Hassan Martin moved from Crvena Zvezda to Japan |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1522989/hassan-martin-moved-from-crvena-zvezda-to-japan/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=20 October 2025 |language=en |date=29 June 2023}}</ref>

===Saga Ballooners (2025-present)===
On June 10, 2025, he joined the [[Saga Ballooners]].<ref>{{cite web |title=David Dudzinski joins Ballooners |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Japan/news/937269/David-Dudzinski-joins-Ballooners |website=www.asia-basket.com |access-date=20 October 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Dudzinski is the son of Barbara and David Dudzinski Sr. He has a brother and a sister. His father played football at [[Northwestern University]] and his mother swam at [[Northwestern University]]. His sister, Katy, played volleyball at [[Wichita State University]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Dave Dudzinski - 2013-14 - Men's Basketball |url=https://goholycross.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/dave-dudzinski/7556 |website=Holy Cross Athletics |access-date=20 October 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

'''Lauren Edgar''' (born 1985) is an American geologist and [[NASA]] astronaut candidate.

== Early life and education ==
Edgar was born in Washington, D.C. in 1985, but considers [[Sammamish, Washington]] to be her hometown.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=Alan |date=2025-09-22 |title=NASA showcases its latest class of astronauts — including a geologist from the Seattle area |url=https://www.geekwire.com/2025/nasa-astronauts-geologist-lauren-edgar/ |access-date=2025-10-29 |website=GeekWire |language=en-US}}</ref> Edgar attended Discovery Elementary School<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-09-23 |title=Sammamish woman selected as one of NASA’s 10 astronaut candidates |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/business/boeing-aerospace/sammamish-woman-selected-as-one-of-nasas-10-astronaut-candidates/ |access-date=2025-10-29 |website=The Seattle Times |language=en-US}}</ref> and Skyline High School.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kent |first=Jackie |date=2025-10-03 |title=Former Skyline High School student picked for NASA candidate class |url=https://komonews.com/news/local/former-skyline-high-school-student-picked-for-nasa-candidate-class |access-date=2025-10-29 |website=KOMO |language=en}}</ref>

Edgar was part of [[Dartmouth College]]'s Class of 2007, originally majoring in engineering before switching to earth sciences. She earned her master’s and doctorate in geology at [[California Institute of Technology|Caltech]] under the direction of [[John P. Grotzinger]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=To the Moon and Beyond |url=https://dartmouthalumnimagazine.com/articles/nasa-lauren-edgar |access-date=2025-10-29 |website=Dartmouth Alumni Magazine |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite thesis |url=https://thesis.caltech.edu/7862/ |title=Identifying and Interpreting Stratification in Sedimentary Rocks on Mars: Insight from Rover and Orbital Observations and Terrestrial Field Analogs |last=Edgar |first=Lauren Ashley |year=2013 |degree=PhD |doi=10.7907/RAGV-WT91}}</ref>

== Career ==
Edgar previously worked for the [[United States Geological Survey]] as a research geologist at the USGS Astrogeology Science Center in [[Flagstaff, Arizona]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cowing |first=Keith |date=2025-09-24 |title=Former USGS Geologist Lauren Edgar Selected As A NASA Astronaut Candidate |url=https://astrobiology.com/2025/09/former-usgs-geologist-lauren-edgar-selected-as-a-nasa-astronaut-candidate.html |access-date=2025-10-29 |website=Astrobiology |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Julian Weinberger''' (born 14 February 1985<ref name="gdatum">{{cite news |title=Schiedsrichter-Steckbrief {{!}} Julian Weinberger |url=https://www.kicker.de/julian-weinberger/schiedsrichter-news |access-date=31 October 2025 |work=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |date=1 August 2025 |language=de |trans-title=Referee profile {{!}} Julian Weinberger}}</ref>) is an Austrian [[Referee (association football)|football referee]].

== Career ==
Weinberger began his refereeing career at the age of 15<ref name="15Jahrenseit"/> and ascended to officiating regional league matches in 2008.<ref name="15Jahrenseit"/><ref name="schiedsrichter1">{{cite news |title=Glück im Unglück für Schiedsrichter Weinberger |url=https://www.skysportaustria.at/glueck-im-unglueck-fuer-schiedsrichter-weinberger/ |access-date=31 October 2025 |work=[[Sky Sport (Germany)|Sky Sport]] |date=27 August 2018 |language=de |trans-title=A stroke of luck for referee Weinberger}}</ref> Since March 2011, Weinberger has officiated matches in the [[2. Liga (Austria)|2. Liga]] and since March 2015 in the [[Austrian Football Bundesliga|Bundesliga]].<ref name="15Jahrenseit"/> In August 2010, Weinberger made his debut in the [[Austrian Cup]] and, on 16 September 2018, he officiated his first [[Vienna derby]] between [[SK Rapid Wien]] and [[FK Austria Wien]].<ref name="15Jahrenseit"/>

In November 2010, during a match between [[Union St. Florian]] and [[Grazer AK]] in [[Enns (town)|Enns]], Weinberger suspended the game following an attack on [[Assistant referee (association football)|assistant referee]] Werner Meixner, who was injured by Grazer's supporters who threw [[Beer bottle|beer bottles]] at him. As a result, Meixner was taken to hospital with a severe cut in his face.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Baumgartner |first1=Günter |title=Schiedsrichter Julian Weinberger: "Ich habe mich bedroht gefühlt" |url=https://www.ligaportal.at/stmk/landesliga/13967-schiedsrichter-julian-weinberger-ich-habe-mich-bedroht-gefhlt |access-date=31 October 2025 |work=Liga Portal Austria |date=13 November 2010 |language=de |trans-title=Referee Julian Weinberger: "I felt threatened."}}</ref>

Since 2018, Weinberger has been on the [[List of FIFA international referees|FIFA list of referees]] and has officiated international football matches.<ref name="15Jahrenseit"/>

In the [[2021–22 UEFA Europa Conference League|2021–22 season]], Weinberger officiated his first [[UEFA Conference League]] match.<ref name="15Jahrenseit"/> He has also refereed matches in the [[UEFA Nations League]], in the [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|European World Cup qualifiers]] for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] in [[Qatar]] and for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Weinberger leitet WM-Quali-Spiel |url=https://www.oefb.at/oefb/News/SR-IntSpiele-05092025/ |access-date=31 October 2025 |work=OEFB Österreich |date=5 September 2025 |language=de |trans-title=Weinberger referees World Cup qualifier}}</ref> as well as in [[friendly matches]].<ref name="wcqk">{{cite news |title=WM-Quali: ÖFB-Schiedsrichterteam im Einsatz |url=https://www.oefb.at/oefb/News/WM-Quali-OeFB-Schiedsrichterteam-im-Einsatz |access-date=31 October 2025 |work=OEFB Österreich |date=2021 |language=de |trans-title=World Cup Qualifiers: Austrian Football Association (ÖFB) referee team in action}}</ref>

In addition, Weinberger was a [[Assistant referee (association football)|goal-line referee]] for [[Harald Lechner]]'s team at the [[2017 UEFA European Under-21 Championship]] in [[Poland]].<ref>{{cite web |title=U-21-Europameisterschaft Spielinfo |url=https://www.kicker.de/spanien-gegen-nordmazedonien-2017-u-em-3798706/spielinfo |publisher=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |access-date=31 October 2025 |language=de |date=2017 |trans-title=U-21 European Championship Match Information}}</ref>

Weinberger has been a [[police officer]] with the [[Federal Police (Austria)|Federal Police]] in [[Vienna]] since 2007 and is currently a precinct inspector.<ref name="schiedsrichter1"/><ref name="15Jahrenseit">{{cite news |last1=Wiederstain |first1=Wolfgang |title=Polizist und Schiedsrichter |url=https://www.bmi.gv.at/magazinfiles/2024/05_06/22_portraet.pdf |access-date=31 October 2025 |work=[[Ministry of the Interior (Austria)|Austrian Ministry of the Interior]] |date=6 May 2024 |language=de |trans-title=Police officer and football referee}}</ref>

'''José Francisco Juan Diego Montalva Feuerhake''' (born 28 May 1985) is a Chilean lawyer and political figure.

He served as Governor of the province of Cautín between 2014 and 2016, and later as Regional Presidential Delegate of La Araucanía from 2022 to 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.clave9.cl/?p=74734|title=Gobernador José Montalva presentó su renuncia al cargo|website=Clave9.cl|access-date=2024-11-17}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.soychile.cl/Santiago/Politica/2014/03/11/235653/Revise-la-lista-de-gobernadores-designados-por-Michelle-Bachelet.aspx|title=Lista de gobernadores designados por Michelle Bachelet|publisher=SoyChile.cl|access-date=2024-11-17}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.soychile.cl/Temuco/Politica/2014/03/11/235671/Malleco-y-Cautin-ya-tiene-nuevos-gobernadores.aspx|title=Malleco y Cautín ya tienen nuevos gobernadores|publisher=SoyChile.cl|access-date=2024-11-17}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Montalva was born on 28 May 1985 in Villarrica, Chile. He completed his secondary education at Colegio del Verbo Divino in Santiago and later studied law at the Universidad Diego Portales, obtaining his professional title in 2012.

== Political career ==
Between 2005 and 2007 he held student leadership positions at the Universidad Diego Portales.

He worked as a parliamentary adviser to Senator Eugenio Tuma, representing the southern sector of the La Araucanía Region. Within the Party for Democracy (PPD), he served as communal president in Villarrica.

In 2014 he was appointed Governor of the province of Cautín by President Michelle Bachelet, serving until November 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gobernacioncautin.gov.cl/noticias/jose-montalva-feuerhake-asume-como-gobernador-de-la-provincia-de-cautin/|title=José Montalva Feuerhake asume como Gobernador de Cautín|website=Gobernación Provincial de Cautín|access-date=2024-11-17}}</ref>

On 1 October 2022 he was appointed Regional Presidential Delegate of La Araucanía by President Gabriel Boric, replacing Raúl Allard.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.emol.com/noticias/Nacional/2022/09/30/1074329/delegado-presidencial-araucania-renuncia-montalva.html|title=Delegado presidencial de La Araucanía renuncia: será reemplazado por José Montalva|website=Emol|date=2022-09-30|access-date=2024-11-17}}</ref>  
He resigned on 15 November 2024 to pursue a congressional candidacy.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.biobiochile.cl/noticias/nacional/region-de-la-araucania/2024/11/15/delegado-presidencial-de-la-araucania-renuncia-al-cargo-quiero-seguir-sirviendo-desde-otros-lugares.shtml|title=Delegado presidencial renuncia: "Quiero seguir sirviendo desde otros lugares"|website=BioBioChile|date=2024-11-15|access-date=2024-11-17}}</ref>

'''Marie Laguerre''' (born 22 February 1996) is a French feminist activist, known for her campaigning against [[street harassment]] after she was assaulted while walking home in 2018.

== Early life and education ==
Laguerre was born on 22 February 1996 in [[Saint-Cyr-l'École]] in the western suburbs of [[Paris]] to a [[Lebanese people|Lebanese]] mother and a father of [[Basques|Basque]] heritage. In 2013, she enrolled in an engineering course in [[Rennes]], Brittany, graduating in 2018. Laguerre subsequently started studying for a bachelor's degree in architecture in Paris.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Lecas |first=Marion |date=7 August 2020 |title=Marie Laguerre, féministe à bout de souffle |url=https://www.la-croix.com/France/Marie-Laguerre-feministe-bout-souffle-2020-08-07-1201108183 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/index2.php?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.la-croix.com%2FFrance%2FMarie-Laguerre-feministe-bout-souffle-2020-08-07-1201108183#federation=archive.wikiwix.com&tab=url |archive-date=21 March 2021 |access-date=21 December 2025 |work=[[La Croix (newspaper)|La Croix]] |language=fr}}</ref>

== Activism ==

=== Assault and trial ===
On 24 July 2018, while Laguerre was returning to her home in the [[19th arrondissement of Paris]], a man on the street made obscene remarks to her. After Laguerre said to him "ta gueule" ({{Literal translation|shut up}}), the man threw an ashtray at her, missing her. Following a verbal altercation between the two, the man punched Laguerre in the face.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |last=Lauwereys |first=Zoé |date=29 July 2018 |title=Frappée au visage en plein Paris pour avoir répondu à son harceleur |url=https://www.leparisien.fr/faits-divers/frappee-au-visage-en-plein-paris-pour-avoir-repondu-a-son-harceleur-28-07-2018-7836573.php |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/index2.php?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.leparisien.fr%2Ffaits-divers%2Ffrappee-au-visage-en-plein-paris-pour-avoir-repondu-a-son-harceleur-28-07-2018-7836573.php#federation=archive.wikiwix.com&tab=url |archive-date=18 May 2023 |access-date=21 December 2025 |work=[[Le Parisien]] |language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2 August 2018 |title=Marie Laguerre, l'étudiante agressée à Paris, lance un site pour encourager les femmes à témoigner |url=https://www.huffingtonpost.fr/2018/08/02/marie-laguerre-letudiante-agressee-a-paris-lance-un-site-pour-encourager-les-femmes-a-temoigner_a_23494460/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/index2.php?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.huffingtonpost.fr%2F2018%2F08%2F02%2Fmarie-laguerre-letudiante-agressee-a-paris-lance-un-site-pour-encourager-les-femmes-a-temoigner_a_23494460%2F#federation=archive.wikiwix.com&tab=url |archive-date=11 December 2018 |access-date=21 December 2025 |work=[[Huffpost]] |language=fr}}</ref>

street, at work and at home.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Lauwereys |first=Zoé |date=2 August 2018 |title=Frappée par son harceleur, Marie Laguerre ouvre un site pour recueillir la parole des victimes In February 2020, Laguerre co-wrote a book, ''Rebellez-vous!'' ({{Literal translation|Rebel!}}), about the struggle for women's rights.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" />
