== Early years ==
Yeison Jiménez was born in [[Manzanares, Caldas]], on 26 July 1991 to a wealthy father, with both his parents being heavy alcoholics.<ref name="pm_2025_ap_1">{{Cite web |last=García |first=Steven |date=2025-04-10 |title=Yeison Jiménez reveló de cuánto era la impresionante fortuna de su papá; "mi papá a los 35 años era rico" |url=https://www.publimetro.co/entretenimiento/2025/04/10/yeison-jimenez-revelo-de-cuanto-era-la-impresionante-fortuna-de-su-papa-mi-papa-a-los-35-anos-era-rico/ |access-date=2026-01-11 |website=Publimetro Colombia |language=es}}</ref> Jiménez started singing at age seven, participating in singing contests in Caldas during his childhood.<ref name="blu_lk_2025_jl_1">{{Cite web |date=2020-08-06 |title=Yeison Jiménez, el aventurero que roba corazones en la música popular |url=https://lakalle.bluradio.com/entretenimiento/artistas/yeison-jimenez-el-aventurero-que-roba-corazones-en-la-musica-popular |access-date=2026-01-11 |website=La Kalle |language=es}}</ref> His parents broke up during his childhood after Orlando (Yeison's father) met a woman different from Luz Mery Galeano (Yeison's mother) and after Galeano suffered from domestic abuse from Orlando. Galeano escaped from Orlando's house and moved to the house of one of her sisters in [[Manizales]], the capital of Caldas.<ref name="ib_2022_se_1">{{Cite web |date=2022-09-12 |title=Yeison Jiménez habló de las dificultades de su infancia: "Tuve seis padrastros" |url=https://www.infobae.com/america/colombia/2022/09/12/yeison-jimenez-hablo-de-las-dificultades-de-su-infancia-tuve-seis-padrastros/ |access-date=2026-01-11 |website=infobae |language=es-ES}}</ref> Later, according to Yeison and his family, Orlando drained his own wealth.<ref name="pm_2025_ap_1" /><ref name="caracoltv_sddm">{{Cite web |title=Yeison Jiménez: de una infancia violenta y vender aguacates a ser estrella de música |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SlGP5fV4yg0 |access-date=11 January 2026 |series=Se Dice De Mí |publisher=[[Caracol Televisión]] |language=es |publication-date=10 April 2018 |via=YouTube}}</ref>

During his teenage years, Galeano moved with Yeison and his sister to [[Bogotá]], Colombia's capital,<ref name="pm_2025_ap_1" /> following a suggestion from Galeano's then-boyfriend, who abandoned them a week after the move.<ref name="pm_2025_ap_1" /><ref name="caracoltv_sddm" /> In Bogotá, Jiménez started writing songs and working at Corabastos, Bogotá's main wholesale market.<ref name="blu_lk_2025_jl_1" /><ref name="ee_vea">{{Cite web |date=2025-07-26 |title=Concierto de Yeison Jiménez en Bogotá: de trabajar en Corabastos a llenar El Campín |url=https://www.elespectador.com/revista-vea/famosos/concierto-de-yeison-jimenez-en-bogota-de-trabajar-en-corabastos-a-llenar-el-campin/ |access-date=2026-01-11 |website=EL ESPECTADOR|language=spanish}}</ref> During this time, he struggled with drug addiction (to the point he suffered a [[stroke]]), a life of crime for which he served a sentence in house arrest,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-31 |title=Yeison Jiménez contó los detalles de la sobredosis que sufrió: “Me pasé” |url=https://www.elespectador.com/revista-vea/famosos/yeison-jimenez-conto-los-detalles-de-la-sobredosis-que-sufrio-me-pase/ |access-date=2026-01-11 |website=EL ESPECTADOR|language=spanish}}</ref><ref name="pm_2023_oc_1">{{Cite web |last=García |first=Steven |date=2023-10-26 |title="Pagué casa por cárcel": Yeison Jiménez reveló el nombre de la iglesia cristiana que le salvó la vida |url=https://www.publimetro.co/entretenimiento/2023/10/26/pague-casa-por-carcel-yeison-jimenez-revelo-el-nombre-de-la-iglesia-cristiana-que-le-salvo-la-vida/ |access-date=2026-01-11 |website=Publimetro Colombia |language=es}}</ref> as well as an [[alcoholism]] problem that ran through his family.<ref name="ib_2022_se_1" />

== Career ==
At 17, Jiménez started to dedicate himself to his music career full-time.<ref name="ee_vea" /> His first commercial song was the 2013 song ''Te Deseo Lo Mejor'', released for the album "Con El Corazón: Vol. 1".<ref name="ib_2026_ja_10d_1" /><ref name="et_2026_ja_10d_1" />

In 2021, he was a member of the jury on the musical program ''Yo Me Llamo'' in its eighth season on the [[Caracol Televisión]] channel.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-01-10 |title=Accidente Yeison Jiménez: lo que se sabe de la muerte del cantante colombiano|url=https://www.univision.com/famosos/accidente-yeison-jimenez-muere-cantante |access-date=2026-01-11 |website=Univision|language=es}}</ref>

== Plane crash and death ==
[[File:N325FA (19502964306).jpg|thumb|The plane involved in the crash]]

A [[Piper PA-31-325 Navajo]] carrying Jiménez and five others crashed on 10 January 2026 whilst heading from [[Juan José Rondón Airport]], [[Paipa]], to [[Olaya Herrera Airport]], [[Medellín]], for a concert Jiménez was due to perform that evening in [[Marinilla]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-01-10 |title=Accidente Yeison Jiménez: lo que se sabe de la muerte del cantante colombiano  |url=https://www.univision.com/famosos/accidente-yeison-jimenez-muere-cantante |access-date=2026-01-15 |website=www.univision.com |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Minota Hurtado |first=José Antonio |date=2026-01-10 |title=En Marinilla, Antioquia, lloran la muerte de Yeison Jiménez en accidente aéreo: tenía programado presentarse en las fiestas populares del municipio |url=https://www.eltiempo.com/colombia/medellin/en-marinilla-antioquia-lloran-la-muerte-de-yeison-jimenez-en-accidente-aereo-tenia-programado-presentarse-en-las-fiestas-populares-del-municipio-3523405 |access-date=2026-01-11 |website=El Tiempo |language=spanish}}</ref> The aircraft required more time than usual to start its engines and was delayed before taking off.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2026-01-13 |title=Last Minutes Before Yeison Jiménez's Accident Revealed: "The Pilot Looked Worried" |url=https://newsroompanama.com/2026/01/12/last-minutes-before-yeison-jimenezs-accident-revealed-the-pilot-looked-worried/ |access-date=2026-01-15 |website=Newsroom Panama |language=en-US}}</ref> After taking off the Navajo failed to gain altitude, quickly turning right on a 290° heading. The aircraft crashed into a farm field, just under 2 km from the end of the runway, killing all on board, including Jiménez.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hurtado |first=Angie Nataly Ruiz |date=2026-01-11 |title=Así fue el accidente de avioneta en el que murieron el cantante Yeison Jiménez y cinco personas más en Boyacá: aparecen las primeras hipótesis |url=https://www.eltiempo.com/colombia/otras-ciudades/asi-fue-el-accidente-de-avioneta-en-el-que-murieron-el-cantante-yeison-jimenez-y-cinco-personas-mas-en-boyaca-aparecen-primeras-hipotesis-3523453 |access-date=2026-02-04 |website=El Tiempo |language=spanish}}</ref> Police, the fire service, Civil Defence personnel and the Technical Corps of Criminal Judicial Investigation attended the scene.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-01-10 |title=Colombian singer Yeison Jiménez among 6 killed in plane crash near Bogotá |url=https://bnonews.com/index.php/2026/01/colombian-singer-yeison-jimenez-among-6-killed-in-plane-crash-near-bogota/ |access-date=2026-01-10 |publisher=[[BNO News]]}}</ref><ref name="HT1">{{Cite news |date=2026-01-10 |title=What happened to Yeison Jimenez? Paipa plane accident sparks fears; scary videos emerge |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/us-news/what-happened-to-yeison-jimenez-paipa-plane-accident-sparks-fears-scary-videos-emerge-101768086786702.html |access-date=2026-01-10 |publisher=[[Hindustan Times]]}}</ref>

The Colombian [[Ministry of Transport (Colombia)|Ministry of Transport]] launched an investigation into the crash. The Technical Directorate for Accident Investigation, the [[Colombian Civil Aviation Authority|Civil Aviation Authority]] (Aerocivil), the Bogotá search and rescue centre, and the [[National Police of Colombia|national police]] are also investigating.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-01-10 |title=Muere Yeison Jiménez: se confirma que el cantante iba en avioneta accidentada en Boyacá |trans-title=Yeison Jiménez dies: it is confirmed that the singer was on the plane that crashed in Boyacá |url=https://www.noticiascaracol.com/colombia/muere-yeison-jimenez-se-confirma-que-el-cantante-iba-en-avioneta-accidentada-en-boyaca-rg10 |access-date=2026-01-10 |publisher=[[Noticias Caracol]] |language=es}}</ref> A preliminary report by Aerocivil was published on 28 January 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Preliminary report by Aerocivil |url=https://www.aerocivil.gov.co/investigacion/Accidentes/info/aeronautica_civil/media/1769552428_INFORME%20PRELIMINAR%20ACCID%20N325FA.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Acosta |first=Javier |date=2026-01-28 |title=Revelan informe preliminar del accidente en el que falleció Yeison Jiménez y su equipo de trabajo |url=https://www.portafolio.co/economia/regiones/revelan-informe-preliminar-del-accidente-en-el-que-fallecio-yeison-jimenez-y-su-equipo-de-trabajo-487188 |access-date=2026-02-04 |website=Portafolio.co |language=es}}</ref>

'''Clara Peya Rigolfas''' (born 6 April 1986, [[Palafrugell]]) is a Catalan pianist, composer, and performer.<ref>{{cite news |title=Clara Peya, música enlluernadorament bona |url=https://www.vilaweb.cat/noticies/clara-peya-musica-enlluernadorament-bona-mail-obert-opinio-merce-ibarz/|work=vilaweb.cat}}</ref> She has recorded several albums both as a solo artist and with other musicians and vocalists.<ref>{{cite news |title=L'art sense concessions de Clara Peya |url=https://www.elnacional.cat/ca/cultura/art-sense-concessions-clara-peya-ha-aconseguit-aturar-temps_1445981_102.html |work=elnacional.cat}}</ref> She is also the co-founder, together with Ariadna Peya, of the company Les Impuxibles. In 2019, she received the National Culture Award of Catalonia.<ref>{{cite news |title=La palafrugellenca Clara Peya esdevé el Premi Nacional de Cultura més jove |url=https://www.diaridegirona.cat/cultura/2019/03/20/palafrugellenca-clara-peya-esdeve-premi-48844008.html |work=diaridegirona.cat}}</ref> She is openly a [[lesbian]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Clara Peya: “La cultura comença al barri; no és allò ‘cool’ que es fa al MACBA” |url=https://www.elcritic.cat/entrevistes/clara-peya-la-cultura-comenca-al-barri-no-es-allo-coo-que-es-fa-al-macba-40868 |newspaper=El Critic |date=2019-11-20 |access-date=2026-02-16}}</ref>
==Early years and studies==
Clara Peya is the daughter of two doctors and grew up in a family environment with a strong presence of music, thanks to the influence of her aunt, Josefina Rigolfas i Torras, a well-known Catalan pianist.<ref>{{cite news |last1= |title=Parlem amb la pianista i compositora Clara Peya, neboda de Josefina Rigolfas |url=https://anoiadiari.cat/entrevista/josefina-tenia-relacio-amor-odi-piano-grans-passions-vida/ |work=Anoia Diari}}</ref> Clara began studying piano at a young age together with her sister Ariadna.

In 2007, she graduated in classical piano from the [[Catalonia College of Music|ESMUC school of music]], where she studied with Professor Leonid Sintsev. She studied with Sintsev for more than twelve years all in all, including time at the Rimsky-Korsakov Conservatory in [[Saint Petersburg]]. She later pursued higher studies in jazz and modern music at the Taller de Músics workshops in [[Barcelona]].<ref>{{cite web |last1= |title=Clara Peya biography |url=https://tallerdemusics.com/profesorado/clara-peya/ |website=Taller de músics}}</ref>

==Musical career==
Clara has recorded many piano-based albums; some as a solo pianist, others with a variety of musicians and vocalists. Her style combines elements of free-style, jazz, chamber music, rap, electronic music, and pop, and she often incorporates themes of social justice, diversity, mental health issues and feminism into her work.<ref name=":0" /> She is also the co-founder, together with her sister Ariadna Peya, a choreographer and dancer, of the company Les Impuxibles which combines music, dance and theatre.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |last1= |title=Clara Peya i Les Impuxibles |url=https://www.cccb.org/es/participantes/ficha/clara-peya/222818 |website=CCCB}}</ref>

'''Giada Andreutti''' (born 16 February 1995) is an Italian athlete and [[Bobsleigh|bobsledder]]. She represented Italy at the [[2022 Winter Olympics|2022]] and [[2026 Winter Olympics]].<ref name=OlympicProf />

==Career==
===Athletics===
Andreutti began her sports career in athletics, specializing in [[discus throw]]. She found success, earning multiple national medals at the junior level. In 2018, she earned a gold medal at the senior level at the Italian Winter Throwing championships.<ref name="ItaOly" /><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.messaggeroveneto.it/sport/italiani-di-lanci-a-rieti-giada-andreutti-e-la-regina-del-disco-dqys17gy |title=Italiani di lanci a Rieti Giada Andreutti è la regina del disco |trans-title=Italian Throwing Championships in Rieti: Giada Andreutti is the queen of the discus |website=messaggeroveneto.it |language=it |publisher=[[Messaggero Veneto]] |date=26 February 2018 |access-date=28 February 2026}}</ref> She competed at the [[2019 Summer Universiade]] in [[Athletics at the 2019 Summer Universiade – Women's discus throw|discus throw]], where she finished 11th.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://worldathletics.org/competition/calendar-results/results/7133328?eventId=10229531&gender=W |title=Universiade 2019 |website=worldathletics.org |publisher=[[World Athletics]] |access-date=28 February 2026}}</ref>

===Bobsleigh===
Andreutti began competing in bobsleigh in 2018, making her debut at [[Lillehammer Olympic Bobsleigh and Luge Track|Lillehammer]].<ref name=OlympicProf /> In 2019 she was named to be part of the [[Italy national bobsleigh team]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ibsf.org/en/news/detail/italian-bobsleigh-team-for-season-2019-2020-announced |title=Italian bobsleigh team for season 2019/2020 announced |website=IBSF.org |publisher=[[International Bobsleigh and Skeleton Federation]] |date=2 May 2019 |access-date=28 February 2026}}</ref> In 2023, she won a Europe Cup event in monobob at the [[Sigulda bobsleigh, luge, and skeleton track|Sigulda]] track, marking her first win in bobsleigh competition.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ibsf.org/en/news/detail/ibsf-europe-cup-bobsleigh-in-sigulda-andreutti-and-boch-win-monobob-and-2-woman-bob |title=IBSF Europe Cup Bobsleigh in Sigulda: Andreutti and Boch win Monobob and 2-woman Bob |website=IBSF.org |publisher=[[International Bobsleigh and Skeleton Federation]] |date=22 January 2023 |access-date=28 February 2026}}</ref>

Andreutti has represented Italy in the Olympics twice. In the [[2022 Winter Olympics]], she participated in the [[Bobsleigh at the 2022 Winter Olympics – Women's monobob|monobob]] event, where she finished 15th.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ibsf.org/en/news/detail/premiere-at-beijing-2022-womens-monobob-is-the-newest-olympic-bobsleigh-discipline |title=Premiere at Beijing 2022: Women’s Monobob is the newest Olympic bobsleigh discipline |website=IBSF.org |publisher=[[International Bobsleigh and Skeleton Federation]] |date=13 February 2026 |access-date=28 February 2026}}</ref> At the [[2026 Winter Olympics]], she participated in both monobob and the two-woman. She finished 24th in monobob and 20th in two-woman.<ref name=OlympicProf />

'''Jorge Alfredo Casillas González ''' (born 15 August 1990) is a Mexican professional [[basketball]] player.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lja.mx/2025/06/pocholo-casillas-la-leyenda-hidrocalida-llega-a-gallos-de-aguascalientes/|title=“Pocholo” Casillas: La leyenda hidrocálida llega a Gallos de Aguascalientes|publisher=LJA|access-date=9 May 2020|language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.venados.com/alfredo-pocholo-casillas-regresa-a-su-segunda-casa-para-aportar-experiencia-y-corazon-a-venados-basketball/|title=Alfredo «Pocholo» Casillas regresa a su segunda casa para aportar experiencia y corazón a Venados Basketball|publisher=Venados de Mazatlán|access-date=9 May 2020|language=es}}</ref>

==Career ==
Casillas made his debut in the 2008 season with the [[Panteras de Aguascalientes]] to play in the [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto Profesional|LNBP]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.heraldo.mx/regresa-a-panteras-2/|title=Regresa a Panteras|publisher=El Heraldo de Aguascalientes|access-date=9 May 2020|language=es}}</ref> He has played with [[Mineros de Cananea (basketball)|Mineros de Cananea]], [[Náuticos de Mazatlán]] and [[Venados de Mazatlán (basketball)|Venados de Mazatlán]] in the [[CIBACOPA]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://oem.com.mx/elsoldemazatlan/deportes/casillas-reaparece-con-venados-y-fortalece-el-trabajo-rumbo-al-cibacopa-2026-28159453|title=Casillas reaparece con Venados y fortalece el trabajo rumbo al Cibacopa 2026|publisher=El Sol de Mazatlán|access-date=9 May 2020|language=es}}</ref> He played with Manzaneros de Cuauhtémoc in the LBE.

==National team career==
In 2015, he was a member of the preliminary list of the Mexican national team that participated in the [[2015 Pan American Games]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.milenio.com/deportes/mexico-define-preseleccion-panamericana-de-basquetbol|title=México define preselección panamericana de basquetbol|publisher=Milenio|access-date=9 May 2020|language=es}}</ref>

'''Matheus Ferreira de Sousa''' (born 19 February 1993), commonly known as '''Ferreira''', is a Brazilian [[association football|footballer]] who plays for [[Clube Atlético Juventus|Juventus-SP]]. Mainly a [[defensive midfielder]], he can also play as a [[centre-back]].

==Career==
Born in [[Divinópolis]], Minas Gerais,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/rn/futebol/times/america-rn/noticia/2025/08/18/do-luto-a-gloria-ferreira-se-emociona-com-gol-da-vitoria-do-america-rn.ghtml|title=Do luto à glória: Ferreira se emociona com gol da vitória do América-RN|trans-title=From grief to glory: Ferreira gets emotional with América-RN's winning goal|publisher=[[Grupo Globo|ge]]|language=pt-BR|date=18 August 2025|accessdate=7 May 2026}}</ref> Ferreira played for [[Red Bull Brasil]] as a youth, before making his senior debut in 2011. He moved to [[Atlético Monte Azul|Monte Azul]] in 2013, and served a loan stint at [[Clube Atlético Penapolense|Penapolense]] in the following year before moving to [[São Caetano Futebol|São Caetano]] ahead of the 2015 season.

On 4 April 2018, after being a regular starter for ''Azulão'', Ferreira was loaned to [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|Série A]] side [[Sport Club do Recife|Sport Recife]] until the end of the year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/pe/futebol/times/sport/noticia/mais-dois-reforcos-ferreira-e-max-sao-integrados-aos-treinos-no-sport.ghtml|title=Mais dois: reforços, Ferreira e Max são integrados aos treinos no Sport|trans-title=Two more: signings, Ferreira and Max are included in Sport's trainings|publisher=[[Grupo Globo|ge]]|language=pt-BR|date=4 April 2018|accessdate=7 May 2026}}</ref> He made his top tier debut on 15 April, starting in a 3–0 away loss to [[América Futebol Clube (MG)|América Mineiro]], but subsequently featured rarely before departing in December and returning to his parent club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.diariodepernambuco.com.br/noticias/futebol/sport/2018/12/apos-rebaixamento-com-sport-rafael-marques-max-e-ferreira-acertam-co.html|title=Após rebaixamento com Sport, Rafael Marques, Max e Ferreira acertam com São Caetano|trans-title=After Sport's relegation, Rafael Marques, Max and Ferreira sign with São Caetano|publisher=Diário de Pernambuco|language=pt-BR|date=11 December 2018|accessdate=7 May 2026}}</ref>

In 2019, Ferreira moved abroad for the first time in his career, joining [[Campeonato de Portugal (league)|Campeonato de Portugal]] side [[Berço S.C.|Berço]]. On 10 January of the following year, he returned to his home country after being announced at [[Botafogo Futebol Clube (SP)|Botafogo-SP]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://botafogofutebolsa.com.br/botafogo-oficializa-contratacao-do-volante-ferreira/|title=Botafogo oficializa contratação do volante Ferreira|trans-title=Botafogo turn official the signing of defensive midfielder Ferreira|publisher=Botafogo FC|language=pt-BR|date=10 January 2020|accessdate=7 May 2026}}</ref>

On 16 August 2021, after spending the first half of the season without a club, Ferreira signed for [[Oeste Futebol Clube|Oeste]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://webdiario.com.br/noticias/oeste-acerta-com-o-volante-ferreira/|title=Oeste acerta com o volante Ferreira|trans-title=Oeste sign with defensive midfielder Ferreira|publisher=Diário da Região|language=pt-BR|date=16 August 2021|accessdate=7 May 2026}}</ref> He moved to [[Esporte Clube XV de Novembro (Piracicaba)|XV de Novembro]] on 14 December,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.futebolinterior.com.br/paulista-a2-xv-de-piracicaba-acerta-com-zagueiro-rebaixado-na-serie-c-do-brasileirao/|title=Paulista A2: XV de Piracicaba acerta com zagueiro rebaixado na Série C do Brasileirão|trans-title=Paulista A2: XV de Piracicaba sign with centre-back relegated in the ''Brasileirão'' Série C|publisher=Futebol Interior|language=pt-BR|date=14 December 2021|accessdate=7 May 2026}}</ref> before joining [[Centro Sportivo Alagoano|CSA]] on 5 July 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/al/arquivo/futebol/noticia/2022/07/05/csa-contrata-o-volante-matheus-ferreira-ex-xv-de-piracicaba.ghtml|title=CSA encaminha a contratação do volante Ferreira, ex-XV de Piracicaba|trans-title=CSA set the signing of defensive midfielder Ferreira, formerly of XV de Piracicaba|publisher=[[Grupo Globo|ge]]|language=pt-BR|date=5 July 2022|accessdate=7 May 2026}}</ref>

On 9 January 2023, Ferreira agreed to a deal with [[Associação Atlética Aparecidense|Aparecidense]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://esportegoiano.com.br/aparecidense-anuncia-contratacao-volante-ex-csa/|title=Aparecidense anuncia a contratação de volante ex-CSA|trans-title=Aparecidense announce the signing of former CSA defensive midfielder|publisher=Esporte Goiano|language=pt-BR|date=9 January 2023|accessdate=7 May 2026}}</ref> Regularly used, he moved to [[América Futebol Clube (RN)|América de Natal]] on 1 December,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/rn/futebol/times/america-rn/noticia/2023/12/01/america-rn-oficializa-volante-ferreira-ex-aparecidense.ghtml|title=América-RN oficializa volante Ferreira, ex-Aparecidense|trans-title=América-RN turn official the defensive midfielder Ferreira, formerly of Aparecidense|publisher=[[Grupo Globo|ge]]|language=pt-BR|date=1 December 2023|accessdate=7 May 2026}}</ref> where he was an undisputed first-choice before being loaned out to [[Athletic Club (MG)|Athletic-MG]] in August 2024.

Back to América for the 2025 season, Ferreira was again a first-choice before departing the club on 31 October.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tribunadonorte.com.br/esportes/america-anuncia-saida-do-volante-ferreira-apos-duas-temporadas/|title=América anuncia saída do volante Ferreira após duas temporadas|trans-title=América announce the departure of defensive midfielder Ferreira after two seasons|publisher=Tribuna do Norte|language=pt-BR|date=31 October 2025|accessdate=7 May 2026}}</ref> On 4 December, he was announced at [[Clube Atlético Juventus|Juventus-SP]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.futebolinterior.com.br/juventus-volante-ex-america-rn-serie-a2/|title=Juventus confirma volante ex-América-RN para a Série A2|trans-title=Juventus confirm former América-RN defensive midfielder for the Série A2|publisher=Futebol Interior|language=pt-BR|date=4 December 2025|accessdate=7 May 2026}}</ref>

'''Travin Marquell Thibodeaux''' (born February 19, 1996) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Bogor Hornbills]] of the [[Indonesian Basketball League]] (IBL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[New Orleans Privateers men's basketball|New Orleans Privateers]]. Standing at 6 ft 8 in (2.03 m), he plays the [[power forward]] position.

==Early career==
Thibodeaux attended [[Brusly High School]] in [[Brusly, Louisiana]], averaging 17.1 points, 15.3 rebounds and 3.9 blocks as a senior.

He garnered All-District 7-3A honors in his final two seasons, earning second team recognition as a junior and first team as a senior while also awarded Defensive MVP.<ref>{{cite web|title=All-District Basketball Teams|url=https://www.nola.com/sports/high_schools/all-district-basketball-teams/article_a129911f-76db-5f38-94b2-141b66822a8a.html|website=nola.com|date=6 April 2013|access-date=22 June 2026}}</ref>

==College career==
Thibodeaux spent all four years of his collegiate eligibility with the [[New Orleans Privateers men's basketball|University of New Orleans Privateers]]  (NCAA Division 1). Over the course of his four-year collegiate career, Thibodeaux gained recognition for his defensive tenacity, as well as his ability to put the ball in the basket. 

Thibodeaux averaged 8.4 points, 5.8 rebounds and 1.9 assists over the course of his four-year career.<ref>{{cite web|title=Travin Thibodeaux Overview|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/travin-thibodeaux-1.html|website=sports-reference.com|date=1 June 2018|access-date=22 June 2026}}</ref> As a junior, Thibodeaux led the University of New Orleans in assists (104), while ranking second in rebounds (233) and rebounds per game (7.3). In his senior year for the Privateers, Thibodeaux led the team in scoring 16.2 points per game, field goal percentage (54.2), rebounds (5.8), free throws (89), steals (39) and blocks (29).<ref>{{cite web|title=Saskatchewan Rattlers Sign Dynamic Big Man Travin Thibodeaux|url=https://www.cebl.ca/news/saskatchewan-rattlers-sign-dynamic-big-man-travin-thibodeaux|website=cebl.ca|date=1 April 2021|access-date=22 June 2026}}</ref>

Thibodeaux’s impressive collegiate career earned him a multitude of accolades including the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]] 2017-2018 All-District (23) First Team<ref>{{cite web|title=NCAA Division I Basketball Awards|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/ncaa/awards/13/NABC-All-District-23-First-Team#710|website=realgm.com|access-date=22 June 2026}}</ref>, as well as the 2016-2017 Southland All-Defensive Team<ref>{{cite web|title=Historical Southland Conference Awards|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/ncaa/conferences/Southland-Conference/30/Awards/Historical#548|website=realgm.com|access-date=22 June 2026}}</ref> and  Southland All-Academic Second Team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Travin Thibodeaux Named To SLC Men's Basketball All-Academic Team|url=https://unoprivateers.com/news/2017/3/30/mbb-slc-academic.aspx|website=unoprivateers.com|date=30 March 2017|access-date=22 June 2026}}</ref>  

==Professional career==
===Fort Wayne Mad Ants===
After going undrafted in the 2018 NBA draft, Thibodeaux joined the [[Indiana Pacers]]' [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Noblesville Boom]], which was still known as '''Fort Wayne Mad Ants''' at the time.<ref>{{cite web|title=Travin Thibodeaux Signs with Mad Ants|url=https://unoprivateers.com/news/2018/10/23/mens-basketball-travin-thibodeaux-signs-with-mad-ants.aspx|website=unoprivateers.com|date=23 October 2018|access-date=22 June 2026}}</ref> In his two years, he averaged 6.2 points, 5.4 rebounds, and 1.6 assists in 61 games.<ref>{{cite web|title=NBA gleague stats for Travin Thibodeaux|url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/player/1629290/?Season=2019-20&SeasonType=Regular%20Season|website=gleague.nba.com|access-date=22 June 2026}}</ref>

===BC Kyiv===
On 13 January 2021, Thibodeaux signed with The [[BC Kyiv-Basket]] of [[Ukrainian Basketball SuperLeague]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Travin Thibodeaux is a newcomer at Kyiv Basket|url=https://basketball.eurobasket.com/Ukraine/news/663108/Travin-Thibodeaux-is-a-newcomer-at-Kyiv-Basket|website=eurobasket.com|date=13 January 2021|access-date=22 June 2026}}</ref> 

===Saskatchewan Rattlers===
On 1 April 2021, Thibodeaux signed with The [[Saskatoon Mamba|Saskatchewan Rattlers]], member club of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Rattlers Sign Dynamic Big Man Travin Thibodeaux|url=https://www.saskatoonmamba.ca/welcome-travin-thibodeaux|website=saskatoonmamba.ca|date=1 April 2021|access-date=22 June 2026}}</ref> 

===BC Balkan Botevgrad===
On 1 September 2021, Thibodeaux signed with The [[BC Balkan Botevgrad]] of the [[National Basketball League (Bulgaria)]].<ref>{{cite instagram |user=balkanbotevgrad |postid=CTP4wWGMzXE|title=Американският център Трейвин Тибодо е последното чуждестранно попълнение в тима на Балкан.|date=1 September 2021|accessdate=22 June 2026}}</ref>

===APOEL B.C.===
On 12 February 2022, Thibodeaux started to play for Cypriot professional basketball club based in the city of Nicosia, [[APOEL B.C.]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2021-2022 APOEL BC Roster|url=https://www.cbf.basketball/el/team-statistics?teamId=4638723&seasonId=131022#mbt:261-200$t&0=2|website=cbf.basketball|access-date=22 June 2026}}</ref> 

===Manama Club===
On 7 July 2023, Thibodeaux signed with The [[Manama Club (basketball)|Manama Club]], member club of the [[Bahraini Premier League (basketball)|Bahraini Premier League]].<ref>{{cite instagram |user=manamaclub |postid=CuYwE1Uqi2x|title=Officially, T Thibodeaux is Manami for the coming challenges|date=7 July 2023|accessdate=22 June 2026}}</ref> 

===Shabab Al Ahli Club Dubai===
In June 2024, Thibodeaux signed with The [[Shabab Al Ahli Club (basketball)|Shabab Al Ahli]], member club of the [[UAE National Basketball League]] based in the city of [[Dubai]].

He represented Shabab Al Ahli in the inaugural [[2024 Basketball Champions League Asia]]. Appearing in five games, he helped the team finish as runners-up in the tournament. He averaged 14.8 points, 9.8 rebounds, and 2.8 assists per game, earning selection to the tournament's All-Star Five.<ref>{{cite instagram |user=bclasia
 |postid=C8ZhTOPynXr|title=Travin Thibodeaux powered his way through an All-Star Five selection|date=19 June 2024|accessdate=22 June 2026}}</ref>

===Kesatria Bengawan Solo===
On 26 June 2024, Thibodeaux signed with The [[Kesatria Bengawan Solo]], of the [[Indonesian Basketball League]] in the middle of ongoing season, replacing [[:it:Taylor Johns|Taylor Johns]]. In his 6 matches with the Kesatria Bengawan, he averaged 22.83 points, 10 rebounds, and 3.5 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Travin Thibodeaux, dari Al Ahli ke Kesatria|url=https://iblindonesia.com/news/travin-thibodeaux-dari-al-ahli-ke-kesatria|access-date=2026-03-16 |website=iblindonesia.com|language=indonesia}}</ref>

===Al Riyadi Club Beirut===
On 28 August 2024, The Lebanese Basketball League defending champion, [[Al Riyadi Club Beirut]], agreed terms with Thibodeaux to play for the [[2024 FIBA Intercontinental Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Al Riyadi inks Travin Thibodeaux, ex Kesatria BS|url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Lebanon/news/889281/Former-players:-Al-Riyadi-inks-Travin-Thibodeaux,-ex-Kesatria-BS|website=asia-basket.com|date=28 August 2024|accessdate=22 June 2026}}</ref>

===Return to Kesatria Bengawan Solo===
On 23 November 2024, Thibodeaux re-joined the [[Kesatria Bengawan Solo]] for the 2025 IBL season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kesatria Panggil Travin Thibodeaux Lagi|url=https://iblindonesia.com/news/kesatria-panggil-travin-thibodeaux-lagi|website=iblindonesia.com|date=23 November 2024|accessdate=22 June 2026|language=indonesia}}</ref> By averaging 7.0 defensive rebounds and 1.4 steals per game, he earned a place on the 2025 IBL All-Defensive Team.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kesatria Punya Dua Pemain Bertahan Terbaik di Liga|url=https://iblindonesia.com/news/kesatria-punya-dua-pemain-bertahan-terbaik-di-liga|website=iblindonesia.com|date=1 August 2025|accessdate=23 June 2026|language=indonesia}}</ref>

===Bogor Hornbills===
In December 2025, after spending two seasons with the Kesatria Bengawan Solo, Thibodeaux joined fellow [[Indonesian Basketball League|IBL]] club the [[Bogor Hornbills]] for his third season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Travin Thibodeaux Pindah ke Hornbills|url=https://iblindonesia.com/news/travin-thibodeaux-pindah-ke-hornbills|website=iblindonesia.com|date=15 December 2025|accessdate=22 June 2026|language=indonesia}}</ref>
In 20 regular-season games, he averaged 25.9 points, 9.3 rebounds, 3.7 assists, and 2.0 steals per game. 

His performances helped improve the Bogor Hornbills' fortunes, leading the team from missing the playoffs the previous season to finishing third in the final standings of the 2026 IBL season. As a result of his contributions, he earned a place on the [[2026 Indonesian Basketball League#All-Team's Awards|2026 All-IBL First Team]], while also named as the [[IBL Foreign Player of the Year#Winners|2026 IBL Most Valuable Player]].<ref>{{cite instagram |user=hornbills
 |postid=DZwdPKbD4uf|title=Hats off to Mr. MVP for All-IBL GoPay First Team|date=20 June 2026|accessdate=22 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Travin Thibodeaux Kalahkan DJ Cooper II Untuk Raih Gelar IBL League MVP 2026|url=https://iblindonesia.com/news/travin-thibodeaux-kalahkan-dj-cooper-ii-untuk-raih-gelar-ibl-league-mvp-2026|website=iblindonesia.com|date=23 May 2026|accessdate=22 June 2026|language=indonesia}}</ref>

'''Isadora Martinatti Penna''' ([[São Paulo]], 28 March 1991) is a Brazilian labor lawyer, feminist, LGBTQ rights activist and politician affiliated with the [[Communist Party of Brazil]] (PCdoB).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Ribeiro |first=Weudson |date=16 March 2022 |title=Isa Penna troca PSOL por PCdoB e concorrerá à vaga de deputada federal |url=https://www.uol.com.br/eleicoes/2022/03/16/isa-penna-troca-psol-por-pc-do-b-e-concorrera-a-vaga-de-deputada-federal.htm |access-date=27 June 2026 |website=[[Universo Online]] |language=pt-br|trans-title=Isa Penna switches from PSOL to PCdoB and will run for a seat in the Chamber of Deputies}}</ref> She was a state deputy of [[São Paulo (state)|São Paulo]] between 2019 and 2023.

==Political career==
Isa joined the [[Socialism and Liberty Party]] (PSOL) in March 2011.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Certidão de Filiação Partidária |url=https://www.tse.jus.br/partidos/filiacao-partidaria/certidao-filiacao |access-date=27 June 2026 |website=[[Superior Electoral Court]] |language=pt-br|trans-title=Party Membership Certificate}}</ref> She ran in the 2014 elections at the age of 23, when she was a candidate for state deputy. She was not elected, as she received only 6,915 votes. In 2016, she ran for election to the [[São Paulo City Council]] and received more than 12,000 votes, becoming the first alternate for PSOL. In March 2017, Isa Penna assumed the position of councilwoman for 30 days, after Toninho Vespoli took a leave of absence, and with [[Sâmia Bomfim]] formed a 100% female and feminist bench in the São Paulo City Council during Women's Month.<ref>{{Cite web |date=17 March 2017 |title="Me chamou de vagabunda", diz Isa Penna (PSOL) sobre agressão |url=https://www.cartacapital.com.br/politica/me-chamou-de-vagabunda-diz-isa-penna-psol-sobre-agressao/ |access-date=27 June 2026 |website=[[CartaCapital]] |language=pt-BR|trans-title="He called me a slut," says Isa Penna (PSOL) about the attack}}</ref>

In 2018, she was elected state representative with 53,838 votes, representing the PSOL/[[Brazilian Communist Party|PCB]] coalition. She assumed the position of state deputy in the [[Legislative Assembly of São Paulo]] (Alesp) in 2019 along with three other parliamentarians elected by PSOL.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Apuração dos votos: Isa Penna |url=https://especiais.gazetadopovo.com.br/eleicoes/2018/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180410173827/https://especiais.gazetadopovo.com.br/eleicoes/2018/ |archive-date=10 April 2018 |access-date=27 June 2026 |website=[[Gazeta do Povo]] |language=pt-BR|trans-title=Vote count: Isa Penna}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Lima |first=Juliana |date=3 October 2018 |title=Ativista Feminista, Isa Penna Quer Ocupar a Assembleia Legislativa de São Paulo |url=https://www.modefica.com.br/ativista-feminista-isa-penna/#.W_6DYmhKjIU |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181128170145/https://www.modefica.com.br/ativista-feminista-isa-penna/#.W_6DYmhKjIU |archive-date=28 November 2018 |access-date=27 June 2026 |work=Modefica |language=pt-BR|trans-title=Feminist activist Isa Penna wants to occupy the Legislative Assembly of São Paulo}}</ref>

In October 2019, during a speech in the plenary session, she was accused of indecency for reciting the poem "{{Lang|pt|sou puta, sou mulher}}" ({{Literal translation|I'm a slut, I'm a woman}}) by the poet Helena Ferreira.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lara |first=Mahila Ames de |date=3 October 2019 |title=Deputada do Psol é ameaçada de cassação por recitar poema controverso na Alesp |url=https://www.poder360.com.br/brasil/deputada-do-psol-e-ameacada-de-cassacao-por-recitar-poema-polemico-na-alesp/ |access-date=27 June 2026 |website=Poder360 |language=pt-br|trans-title=A deputy from the PSOL party is threatened with expulsion for reciting a controversial poem in the Legislative Assembly of São Paulo}}</ref>

In March 2022, she announced her affiliation with the Communist Party of Brazil (PCdoB), aiming to run for federal deputy for the state of São Paulo, but was unsuccessful in the election.<ref name=":0" />

==Personal life==
Isa Penna identifies as a feminist, bisexual, and an activist for minority rights.<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 September 2016 |title=Bissexual e feminista, Isa Penna é aposta do Psol para vereadora |url=https://www.guiagaysaopaulo.com.br/noticias//bissexual-e-feminista-isa-penna-e-aposta-do-psol-para-vereadora |access-date=27 June 2026 |website=Guia Gay São Paulo |language=pt-BR|trans-title=Bisexual and feminist, Isa Penna is the PSOL party's candidate for city councilor}}</ref>

==Attacks==
===2017===
In March 2017, during an alleged argument with councilman Camilo Cristófaro ([[Brazilian Socialist Party|PSB]]) at the São Paulo City Council, Cristófaro called Isa a "slut" and a "terrorist" and told her not to be surprised if she "got slapped in the street." Isa classified the episode as an "aggression" and an "attempt at verbal and physical intimidation." Cristófaro denied the accusations.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lara |first=Wallace |date=21 March 2017 |title=Vereador do PSB xingou colega do PSOL de 'vagabunda', diz testemunha |url=https://g1.globo.com/sao-paulo/noticia/vereador-do-psb-xingou-colega-do-psol-de-vagabunda-diz-testemunha.ghtml |access-date=27 June 2026 |website=[[G1 (website)|G1]] |language=pt-BR|trans-title=PSB councilman called PSOL colleague a 'slut,' witness says}}</ref> In April 2017, Isa's cell phone number was exposed via WhatsApp as a way to pressure her in favor of the ''[[Escola sem Partido|Escola Sem Partido]]'' movement (which she opposes). One of the messages labeled her as "in favor of indoctrination in schools." Isa classified the situation as a form of "intimidation."<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 April 2017 |title=Vereadoras de São Paulo têm celular exposto e criticam 'intimidação' |url=https://valor.globo.com/politica/noticia/2017/04/07/vereadoras-de-sao-paulo-tem-celular-exposto-e-criticam-intimidacao.ghtml |access-date=27 June 2026 |website=[[Valor Econômico]] |language=pt-br|trans-title=City councilors in São Paulo have their cell phones exposed and criticize 'intimidation'}}</ref>

===Sexual harassment in 2020===
In December 2020, during the voting on the state budget for 2021, a security camera at the Legislative Assembly of the State of São Paulo captured the moment when deputy Fernando Cury groped the side of Isa Penna's breast.<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 December 2020 |title='Me sinto enojada', diz Isa Penna sobre assédio sexual |url=https://www.cartacapital.com.br/sociedade/me-sinto-enojada-diz-isa-penna-sobre-assedio-sexual-de-fernando-cury/ |access-date=27 June 2026 |website=CartaCapital |language=pt-BR|trans-title='I feel disgusted,' says Isa Penna about sexual harassment}}</ref> Cury denied the harassment, claiming it was a hug and apologized, but Isa Penna denounced him for sexual harassment and indecency, demanding the revocation of his mandate. Cury's mandate was interrupted by the Legislative Assembly of the State of São Paulo (ALESP) on 1 April 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reis |first=Vivian |date=1 April 2021 |title=Caso Isa Penna: em decisão inédita, Alesp suspende deputado Fernando Cury por seis meses por passar a mão na colega |url=https://g1.globo.com/sp/sao-paulo/noticia/2021/04/01/caso-isa-penna-em-decisao-inedita-alesp-suspende-por-6-meses-mandato-do-deputado-fernando-cury-que-passou-a-mao-em-colega.ghtml |access-date=27 June 2026 |website=G1 |language=pt-BR|trans-title=Isa Penna case: in an unprecedented decision, Alesp suspends deputy Fernando Cury for six months for touching his colleague inappropriately}}</ref>

With the aim of pressuring for the removal of Fernando Cury from office, personalities and civil society organizations carried out a campaign entitled "Por uma Punição Exemplar" (''For an Exemplary Punishment'') whose website allowed the sending of messages to pressure the deputies of the Legislative Assembly of the State of São Paulo to remove the parliamentarian. The campaign included writer [[Beatriz Bracher]], cultural manager Mari Stockler, director Daniela Thomas, lawyer Rafael Poço, designer Julia Mariani, and administrator Maísa Diniz, co-founder of Vote Nelas, as well as the organizations 342 Artes, Update, Elas no Poder, Girl Up, and Vamos Juntas.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mena |first=Fernanda |date=21 March 2021 |title='Punição exemplar de deputado assediador é uma questão civilizatória', dizem articuladoras de campanha |url=https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/poder/2021/03/punicao-exemplar-de-deputado-assediador-e-uma-questao-civilizatoria-dizem-articuladoras-de-campanha.shtml |access-date=27 June 2026 |website=[[Folha de S.Paulo]] |language=pt-BR|trans-title='Exemplary punishment of a harassing congressman is a matter of civilization,' say campaign organizers}}</ref>

Open letters and petitions demanding Cury's removal from office were also published, one of which included signatories such as actresses [[Patrícia Pillar]], [[Alessandra Negrini]], and [[Letícia Sabatella]]; writers [[Milton Hatoum]] and [[Antonio Prata]]; historian [[Lilia Moritz Schwarcz]]; lawyers Alberto Toron and Augusto Arruda Botelho; and musicians [[Nando Reis]] and [[Tony Bellotto]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=28 March 2021 |title=Personalidades pedem cassação do deputado estadual Fernando Cury |url=https://www.poder360.com.br/brasil/personalidades-pedem-cassacao-do-deputado-estadual-fernando-cury/ |access-date=27 June 2026 |website=Poder360 |language=pt-br|trans-title=Public figures call for the removal of state representative Fernando Cury from office}}</ref>

Those who voted for Cury's removal from office were rapporteur [[Emídio de Souza]] ([[Workers' Party (Brazil)|PT]]), congresswoman [[Erica Malunguinho]] (PSOL), Barros Munhoz ([[Brazilian Social Democracy Party|PSDB]]), and the president of the Council, Maria Lúcia Amaray (PSDB). However, the group that defended the more lenient penalty proposed by Moura won; this group was composed only of men and included Adalberto Freitas ([[Social Liberal Party (Brazil)|PSL]]), Wellington Moura (author of the vote), Delegado Olim ([[Progressistas|PP]]), [[Alex Madureira]] ([[Social Democratic Party (Brazil, 2011)|PSD]]), and Estevam Galvão ([[Democrats (Brazil)|DEM]]).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Soares |first=Gabriella |date=5 March 2021 |title=Conselho de Ética ameniza punição para deputado que apalpou colega na Alesp |url=https://www.poder360.com.br/brasil/conselho-de-etica-ameniza-punicao-para-deputado-que-apalpou-colega-na-alesp/ |access-date=27 June 2026 |website=Poder360 |language=pt-br|trans-title=Ethics Committee softens punishment for deputy who groped colleague at Alesp}}</ref>

In addition to being suspended from ALESP, Cury was also expelled from his then party, [[Cidadania]], as a result of the incident,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Arcoverde |first=Léo |last2=Ferraz |first2=Vivian |date=22 November 2021 |title=Cidadania expulsa deputado Fernando Cury por caso de importunação sexual na Alesp |url=https://g1.globo.com/sp/sao-paulo/noticia/2021/11/22/cidadania-expulsa-deputado-fernando-cury-por-caso-de-importunacao-sexual-na-alesp.ghtml |access-date=27 June 2026 |website=G1 |language=pt-BR|trans-title=The Cidadania party expels deputy Fernando Cury for sexual harassment case in the Legislative Assembly of São Paulo}}</ref> and is now affiliated with the [[Brazil Union]] party. In April 2021, the [[Public Prosecutor's Office (Brazil)|Public Prosecutor's Office]] filed criminal charges against Cury,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lara |first=Walace |last2=Reis |first2=Vivian |date=3 April 2021 |title=Caso Isa Penna: Ministério Público denuncia por importunação sexual deputado Fernando Cury, que passou a mão na colega |trans-title=Isa Penna Case: Public Prosecutor's Office files charges of sexual harassment against congressman Fernando Cury, who allegedly touched his colleague inappropriately |url=https://g1.globo.com/sp/sao-paulo/noticia/2021/04/03/caso-isa-penna-ministerio-publico-denuncia-por-importunacao-sexual-deputado-fernando-cury-que-passou-a-mao-na-colega.ghtml |access-date=11 October 2026 |website=G1 |language=pt-BR}}</ref> which were accepted by the São Paulo courts in December 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rodrigues |first=Rodrigo |date=15 December 2021 |title=Justiça de SP aceita denúncia contra deputado Fernando Cury por importunação sexual |url=https://g1.globo.com/sp/sao-paulo/noticia/2021/12/15/justica-de-sp-aceita-denuncia-contra-deputado-fernando-cury-por-importunacao-sexual.ghtml |access-date=27 June 2026 |website=G1 |language=pt-BR|trans-title=São Paulo court accepts charges against congressman Fernando Cury for sexual harassment}}</ref> On 6 December 2023, Cury was sentenced to one year, two months, and twelve days in prison, under an open regime, which was converted into a fine of [[Brazilian real|R$]] 26,400 and community service.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tomaz |first=Kleber |last2=Machado |first2=Lívia |date=6 December 2023 |title=Justiça de SP condena ex-deputado Fernando Cury por importunação sexual contra ex-parlamentar Isa Penna; crime ocorreu em 2020 |trans-title=A court in São Paulo has convicted former congressman Fernando Cury of sexual harassment against former lawmaker Isa Penna; the crime occurred in 2020 |url=https://g1.globo.com/sp/sao-paulo/noticia/2023/12/06/justica-de-sp-condena-ex-deputado-fernando-cury-por-importunacao-sexual-contra-ex-parlamentar-isa-penna-em-2020-crime-foi-gravado.ghtml |access-date=11 October 2026 |website=G1 |language=pt-BR}}</ref>

On 8 October 2025, the [[Superior Court of Justice (Brazil)|Superior Court of Justice]] upheld Cury's conviction, making him ineligible for office for 8 years.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cócolo |first=Victória |date=8 October 2025 |title=Justiça confirma condenação de Fernando Cury por importunação sexual e o torna inelegível |trans-title=The court upholds Fernando Cury's conviction for sexual harassment, making him ineligible to run for office |url=https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/colunas/monicabergamo/2025/10/justica-confirma-condenacao-de-fernando-cury-por-importunacao-sexual-e-o-torna-inelegivel.shtml |access-date=11 October 2026 |website=[[Folha de S.Paulo]] |language=pt-BR}}</ref>

After his parents' separation, he later spent time living in [[Nantes]]. It was there that he joined [[Elephanz]], an [[electropop]] duo.{{cite web |date=29 January 2012 |title=Thibaud, bassiste professionnel déjà réputé |url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/pays-de-la-loire/loire-atlantique/thibaud-bassiste-professionnel-deja-repute-212312 |access-date=7 March 2026 |language=fr |newspaper=Ouest-France}} He later described this period as important in developing his skills as a musician.{{cite web |date=6 February 2020 |title=Voyou |url=https://www.sinon-magazine.com/voyou/ |access-date=1 August 2026 |website=Sinon Magazine |language=fr}} Vanhooland began writing songs in 2017 under the pseudonym Voyov, which later became Voyou.{{cite web |author=Louis |date=19 December 2017 |title=Découvertes : Promenade en tandem avec VOYOU |url=https://www.soul-kitchen.fr/79450-promenade-tandem-voyou |access-date=9 April 2026 |website=Soul Kitchen |language=fr}} == Career == [[File:NantesVoyouAuxNefs 1.jpg|thumb|Voyou (bottom right) performing with {{ill|November Ultra|fr}} as a member of [[Elephanz]] ]] Under the name Voyou, Vanhooland released "{{langr|fr|Seul sur ton tandem}}" on 1{{nbsp}}December 2017.{{cite AV media notes |title=Seul sur ton tandem - '''Carla Jaran Jeffery''' (July 10, 1993 – September 1, 2026) was an American actress best known for playing the cheerleader Bree in Disney Channel's ''[[Zombies (franchise)|Zombies]]'' film franchise.<ref name="billboard">{{Cite web |last=Atkinson |first=Katie |title='Zombies' Actress Carla Jeffery Dies at Age 33 |url=https://www.billboard.com/culture/tv-film/carla-jeffery-death-zombies-actress-1236332008/ |website=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |date=September 2, 2026 |access-date=September 3, 2026}}</ref><ref name="variety">{{Cite web |last=Saperstein |first=Pat |title=Carla Jeffery, Actress in Disney Channel's 'Zombies,' Dies at 33 |url=https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/carla-jeffery-dead-disney-channel-zombies-1236849763/ |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=September 2, 2026 |access-date=September 3, 2026}}</ref>

==Early life==
Jeffery was born in [[Houston]], Texas on July 10, 1993.<ref name="hht1">{{Cite web |last=Jaiswal |first=Ojas |title=Was Carla Jeffery single? What we know about the 'ZOMBIES' star's family amid her death at 33 |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/trending/us/was-carla-jeffery-single-what-we-know-about-the-zombies-star-s-family-amid-her-death-at-33-101788387779295.html |website=Hindustan Times |date=September 3, 2026 |access-date=September 3, 2026}}</ref><ref name="abc">{{Cite web |last=Bernabe |first=Angeline Jane |title='Zombies' star Carla Jeffery dies at 33 |url=https://abcnews.com/GMA/Culture/zombies-star-carla-jeffery-dies-33/story?id=136156558 |website=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] |date=September 2, 2026 |access-date=September 3, 2026}}</ref> Her twin brother, [[Carlon Jeffery]], also became an actor, appearing on Disney Channel's ''[[A.N.T. Farm]]'' as Cameron Parks.<ref name="hht1"/><ref name="vulture">{{Cite web |last=Squires |first=Bethy |title=Zombies and Curb Your Enthusiasm Star Carla Jeffery Dies at 33 |url=https://www.vulture.com/article/disney-channel-star-carla-jeffery-dies-at-33.html |website=[[Vulture (magazine)|Vulture]] |date=September 2, 2026 |access-date=September 3, 2026}}</ref> According to the ''[[Hindustan Times]]'', Carlon's interest in music and entertainment reportedly helped inspire the family's move from [[Ohio]] to [[California]], and Jeffery began taking acting classes as a child, initially alongside her twin brother, as a way to become more comfortable performing despite being naturally shy.<ref name="hht1"/>

She joined Alexanders Talent Management at age 12 and remained with the agency for more than 20 years, until her death.<ref name="billboard"/><ref name="vulture"/>

==Career==
Jeffery's first screen role was in the 2006 film ''[[Phat Girlz]]''; she played a 10-year-old version of [[Mo'Nique]]'s character.<ref name="billboard"/><ref name="abc"/><ref name="vulture"/> From 2007 to 2009, she had a recurring role as Keysha Black in HBO's ''[[Curb Your Enthusiasm]]'', appearing for two seasons as part of the Black family, who move in with Larry David after Hurricane Katrina in the show's storyline.<ref name="billboard"/><ref name="vulture"/> She also appeared in Nickelodeon's ''[[iCarly]]'' in 2008, and, according to ABC News, on Disney Channel's ''[[Good Luck Charlie]]'' in 2011 and ''[[Shake It Up (American TV series)|Shake It Up]]'' the following year, as well as ''[[Scream Queens (2015 TV series)|Scream Queens]]'' and ''[[Crazy Ex-Girlfriend]]''.<ref name="abc"/> Other credits cited across sources include ''[[Southland (TV series)|Southland]]'' and ''[[American Vandal]]''.<ref name="billboard"/><ref name="vulture"/>

In 2018, Jeffery was cast as Bree, an aspiring cheerleader and best friend of the character Addison, in Disney Channel's original film ''[[Zombies (2018 film)|Zombies]] (2018)''.<ref name="vulture"/><ref name="billboard"/> She reprised the role in the sequels ''[[Zombies 2]]'' (2020) and ''[[Zombies 3]]'' (2022), and voiced the character in the 2024 animated series ''[[Zombies: The Re-Animated Series]]''.<ref name="billboard"/><ref name="vulture"/>

==Death==
Jeffery died at her California home on September 1, 2026, at the age of 33.<ref name="billboard"/><ref name="variety"/><ref name="hht2">{{Cite web |last=Banerjee |first=Shamik |title=Carla Jeffery cause of death: What happened to actor behind Bree in Disney's Zombies franchise? |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/us-news/carla-jeffery-cause-of-death-what-happened-to-actor-behind-bree-in-disneys-zombies-franchise-101788385823035.html |website=Hindustan Times |date=September 3, 2026 |access-date=September 3, 2026}}</ref> Her death was announced by her talent agency, Alexanders Talent Management, in a statement posted to her [[Instagram]] account. No cause of death was disclosed.<ref name="billboard"/><ref name="variety"/><ref name="hht2"/><ref name="fox">{{Cite web |last=Stoddard |first=Catherine |title=Carla Jeffery, known for roles in Disney's 'Zombies,' 'Curb Your Enthusiasm,' dies at 33 |url=https://www.livenowfox.com/news/carla-jeffery-known-roles-disneys-zombies-curb-your-enthusiasm-dies-33 |website=LiveNOW from Fox |date=September 2, 2026 |access-date=September 3, 2026}}</ref>

Tributes were shared by several of her ''Zombies'' co-stars, including [[Milo Manheim]], who called her "the sweetest person I have ever met", and [[Chandler Kinney]], who described her as "the brightest shining light in any room she walked into".<ref name="abc"/>
